### [1] [ReCoPII: A Relation-Grounded Framework for Building Contextual PII Masking Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35925)
*Taehwan Lee*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: ReCoPII 是一个面向韩语长文档「上下文脱敏」(contextual masking) 训练数据构建的关系驱动框架。核心洞察：现有基于作者身份的单数据主体增广（SPY）在多主体文档中会生成错误的 KEEP 标签；ReCoPII 改为先用「域条件实体—关系配置」规划本体约束的关系图，再由 LLM 写带占位符的插入句、代码确定性填值并重建标注、独立 LLM 复审，最后由关系图按公式(1)推导每个实体的 MASK/KEEP 标签，产出 ReCoPII-Ko（1,857 篇韩文长文档、18 类实体、19 种关系标签、25,656 条边）。人工审计中其 KEEP 标签一致率 88.42%，远超同源 SPY 增广的 26.27%；在其上训练的分类器过度脱敏显著更少；与紧凑检测器联合微调的系统在固定泄漏预算内把过度脱敏从约 95% 压到 2.5–5.04%，检测器以约 1/4 参数量达到与 XLM-R-large 相当的 KDPII 性能。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 任务本身是「同类型不同决策」：韩语长文档中同一实体类型的提及需分别标注 MASK（须隐藏，如个人电话）或 KEEP（可保留，如机构对外客服号），训练数据必须是语义连贯且文本本身支持该标签的文档。障碍有二：隐私限制使真实标注数据难以获取；现有合成路线均以单一参照点判定所有提及——查询条件方法（CAPID、PII-Bench）以问题为参照，无查询设定下的 SPY 以「文本作者」为参照。作者基准隐含单数据主体假设：文档若含多人（如合同中的交易对手），与作者无关但仍属私人的信息会被误标为非 PII。作者实测 1,857 篇文档中 703 篇含两个以上可脱敏 NAME 实体，人工审计显示 SPY 式增广的 KEEP 标签一致率仅 26.27%（约五成为 UNCERTAIN），而据此训练的分类器在匹配测试集上会脱敏近一半应保留提及；仅按实体类型检测几乎脱敏全部人工确认可保留的提及。作者受 Contextual Integrity、Privacy Checklist、GoldCoin 启发，主张改用「域条件实体—关系配置」刻画谁的信息、以何种角色被传达，并假定 MASK/KEEP 标签可由关系配置加文档证据推导。

Method: 框架（ReCoPII）：(1) 受控数据构建——源语料 Basic（2,355 篇韩语长文档、六域、18 类实体、句子级 PII span 与字符级 BIO 标签）；用 GPT-5.6-Sol 定义域特定关系 schema，标注文档级实体登记表、关系与边级隐私标签；(2) 本体约束规划——GPT-4o-mini 接收文档、已有关系图与域本体，提出「机构公开管理」的实体及暂定 NON_PII 边，边必须满足 (τ(v_i), r, τ(v_j)) ∈ Ω_d，代码拒绝端点类型不符、孤立新实体、不可填值的计划并要求重生成；(3) 占位符实现与确定性重建——GPT-4o-mini 只写含 <TYPE:E10> 形式占位符的插入句（禁止写实值、禁止复用源文 PII 值、需保持韩语助词一致），代码按替换轨迹填入 persona pool 值（Nemotron-Personas-Korea，约束 SQL 查询），重建 span、关系、边级隐私标签，仅可脱敏实体进入 PII_set 与 BIO 掩码，候选检测则覆盖全部登记表提及；(4) 独立复审与接收——GPT-5-mini 在不知计划标签的前提下按 PII/NON_PII/AMBIGUOUS 判定边并给出证据引文，新边被判 PII 且引文校验通过、或报告缺失涉新实体的 PII 关系，则拒收文档；另要求≥3 个新可保留实体、≥2 个插入点、无本体违规、自然度高；(5) NAME 增强——补充公开引用或假设性虚构人物，各以一条文本支持的 NON_PII 关系挂到既有 NAME 实体，专设复审；(6) 标签推导——公式(1)：对实体 v_i 聚合其全部入射边（不分方向），n_i=|I_i|、p_i=其中标 PII 的边数，μ(v_i)=0（KEEP）当且仅当 n_i>0 且 p_i=0，否则为 1（MASK），即保留需有关系证据且无入射 PII 边，无关系实体默认脱敏。模型侧：候选检测器 A.X+Gazetteer+CRF+MLP（共享编码器 + 训练期 Gazetteer 特征投影 + 线性链 CRF 解类型/跨度 + 字符边界 MLP 修正偏移，因韩语边界可能落在 token 内），在 KDPII 上训练；上下文脱敏用同一编码器，两种头部——直接头（由提及表示均值预测实体掩码标签）与关系条件头（对实体对预测 19 类关系及该关系的 PII 概率，阈值化后按公式(1) 聚合，可回溯到具体边）；训练设置含 Joint Fine-tuning（联合更新编码器/检测器/头）与 Frozen Detector（仅训头）。评测设 RQ1 检测与跨集迁移、RQ2-A 文档与标签效度（LLM 三评审 + 四名人工标注者，300 组配对）、RQ2-B 上下文掩码监督可用性、RQ3 端到端系统，并引入插入无关探针（另一管线整篇生成 402 篇无插入句文档）、句子来源分层分析（Mantel–Haenszel 优势比）等诊断。

Result: 数据：ReCoPII-Ko 含 1,857 篇（源池 2,355 中 1,996 通过增广接收、剔除 139 篇孤立新实体后 1,857），六域（职业/教育 302、合同 318、金融 334、法律 246、医疗 299、客服 358），25,656 条边 / 19 种关系标签，17,104 MASK 与 6,780 KEEP 实体（KEEP 占比 28.4% vs SPY 40.7%）；官方划分为按源组划分的 1,245/208/404。RQ1：A.X+Gazetteer+CRF+MLP 在 KDPII 上 86.71±1.47（五种子）vs XLM-R-large 85.32±1.24，1.40 点差的 95% CI [−0.37, 3.04] 含 0，参数量约为其 1/4（148.9M vs 558.9M）；合成测试上其三种子均值最高（69.40%）。RQ2-A：四名标注者对 ReCoPII-Ko 抽样 KEEP 标签一致率 88.42%（CI [86.50, 90.12]）对 SPY 26.27%，MASK 一致率 96.29% vs 95.75%；人工偏好 ReCoPII-Ko 76.92% vs 7.92%（平局 15.17%），文档连贯性 3.15 vs 2.24，矛盾率 1.25% vs 14.92%；LLM 评审自然度 2.77 vs 2.37、偏好 60.89% vs 30.33%，但 NON_PII 有效性 35.06% vs 29.19% 差异不显著（p=0.236）；关系审计中 95.46% 关系获文本支持，边级隐私一致率 89.50%。RQ2-B：在 279 篇匹配测试（15,604 MASK / 2,422 KEEP 提及）上，四个通过预注册泄漏检查的 A.X 配置用 ReCoPII-Ko 训练比用 SPY 训练 Macro-F1 高 2.54–3.83 点、过度脱敏低 5.68–8.84 点，配对 CI 均不含 0，泄漏差 CI 均含 0；KLUE-R-base 与 XLM-R-large 未过预注册检查（自身插入句最大泄漏 8.83%/9.78%），仅为描述性证据；上下文分析显示全文输入增益在 ReCoPII-Ko 为 16.27–19.55 点、SPY 仅 1.63–2.39 点，「仅值+类型」在 SPY 上已达 96.80–97.31 Macro-F1 而在 ReCoPII-Ko 仅 79.60–83.09，说明前者决策主要靠表面形式、后者真正依赖上下文。RQ3：官方 404 篇测试上，Detection only 过度脱敏 95.66%/泄漏 13.02%，Frozen Detector 实际退化为全掩码（95.66%），Joint FT 直接头过度脱敏 1.10%、泄漏 1.13%，关系条件头 2.36%/1.20%（预算 1.5%）；在 100 篇人工核验记录上，四个满足预算的检测器联合微调后过度脱敏 2.52–5.04%、泄漏 1.14–4.18%，而 Detection only 对九个检测器几乎脱敏全部应保留提及（98.9–99.9%）；候选辅助 LLM（GPT-4o-mini/K-EXAONE/Solar Pro）过度脱敏 28–95%、泄漏 13–24%，全部劣于联合微调；XLM-R-large 六次运行中五次无法满足预算。诊断：直接头比关系条件头少过度脱敏约 1–1.5 点；关系条件头的过度脱敏中 73.2–98.2% 来自被判 PII 的边，其中 84.8–95.7% 的端点—关系组合在标注图中不存在（即幻觉关系）；句子来源分层后插入句的 MASK 释放率显著更高（OR 5.9–32.0），说明部分准确度来自「识别插入句」这一文体线索；插入无关探针上过度脱敏升至 11.33–34.21%、泄漏至多 4.95%，仍显著优于 Detection only 的 88.59–95.99%，但明显劣于官方测试。

Conclusion: ReCoPII 以「域条件实体—关系配置 + 文档证据」替代单作者假设，用本体约束规划、占位符实现、代码确定性标注重建与独立语义复审构建上下文掩码数据，并由关系图经公式(1)导出 MASK/KEEP，在不依赖真实标注数据的前提下同时满足同一实体类型下两种标签的需求；人工核验其 KEEP 标签有效性显著优于 SPY（88.42% vs 26.27%），数据可训练出过度脱敏更少、且明显依赖文本上下文而非实体表面值的分类器。端到端看，与紧凑检测器联合微调可在固定泄漏预算内消除「仅检测即全掩码」造成的绝大部分过度脱敏。推理时直接头已足够，关系条件头虽使每个决策可回溯到具体边，却因预测出标注中不存在的边而额外过度脱敏。局限与后续：评估仅在合成的韩语文档上进行，其他语言与自然文档未验证；除人工核验集外模型评估度量的是与构造流水线的一致性而非隐私判断本身的正确性；无经裁决的金标准，人工核验样本量小（238 个应保留提及）导致区间宽；可保留提及几乎全部位于插入句，官方测试分数部分反映句子来源；四名标注者均为项目成员。作者表示将发布数据集与代码，并将下一步定为对每个提及做独立裁决验证。

Abstract: Training contextual masking systems for personally identifiable information (PII) requires examples distinguishing maskable from preservable mentions of one entity type, but privacy restrictions limit access to real data. Author-based augmentation (SPY) labels mentions unrelated to the author as non-PII, presuming a single data subject and overlooking others. We propose ReCoPII (Relation-grounded Contextual PII masking), a framework that builds such data without this premise: it plans ontology-constrained entity relations, writes insertion sentences with placeholders, reconstructs annotations with code, checks the result with a separate LLM, and derives MASK/KEEP labels from entity relations. On Korean documents from six domains, it yields ReCoPII-Ko, a corpus with relation, privacy, and MASK/KEEP annotations, which we validate. Across 300 pairs, four annotators agree with 88.42% of its sampled KEEP labels, against 26.27% for SPY-style augmentation of the same sources. Classifiers trained on it over-mask less than under that reference on a matched test. Contextual masking fine-tuned jointly with a PII detector removes most over-masking of detection alone within a fixed leakage budget; on human-verified entity records, the four detectors meeting it over-mask at most 5.04% with at most 4.18% leakage. The detector is comparable to XLM-R-large on KDPII with about a quarter of its parameters.

</details>


### [2] [MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36006)
*Simon A. Lee,Jiahang Sha,Moonseong Jeong,Yunbei Pan,Jeffrey N. Chiang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文评测了 MedJev——一个可在笔记本本地运行的开放权重“System-One”决策模型（基于 OpenJev/Qwen3.5-9B 微调），它在单次前向传播中直接输出结构化概率（Choice/Noul 请求）而不生成文本。作者在 10 个医学基准上将其与零样本开源 LLM、已发表的 GPT-3.5/4/4o/o1 结果以及有监督基线（XGBoost、TF-IDF+LR）对比。结论是：MedJev 在医学知识类任务上接近 GPT-4 零样本水平（MedQA 72.5%、USMLE 75.4%、NEJM 80.1%，ECE 0.028–0.063），在院内死亡风险上 AUROC 0.926 优于 XGBoost（0.902），但患者级概率严重失准（死亡 ECE 0.286），且在运营性结局（急诊分诊收治）上弱于监督模型；一种仅需 50–200 个标注样本的两参数 Platt 重校准可将死亡 ECE 降至 0.007。作者开源代码与评测框架，主张开放 System-One 模型可作为医疗 AI 的新零样本基线。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 生成式大模型评测需要解码并解析文本输出，而死亡风险、住院时长、急诊去向等临床任务本质上是对固定结局集合的概率估计，难以用文本生成高效表达。System-One 模型（Jev/OpenJev）以类型化请求（Choice/Noul/Score）直接给出概率分布，速度快、算力低、可本地运行，但其在医学知识、诊断推理与基于 EHR 的患者级预测上的适用性尚不明确：既能正确排序风险，并不意味着其概率与真实发生率一致。已有 Jev 评测仅覆盖 37 个通用数据集与 PubMedQA，未涉及患者级预测，因此需要在统一管线下同时考察判别力（AUROC/准确率）与概率校准（ECE），并厘清零样本推理、本地校准与监督训练三者之间的取舍。

Method: 构建 MedJev（基于 OpenJev，微调 Qwen3.5-9B），将每个基准表示为“状态 + 类型化问题”的 Jev 请求：知识与诊断任务用 Choice（选项字母单 token 概率读出 + 温度校准），患者级结局用 Noul（二元事件概率），提示包含序列化状态 JSON、问题指令与选项说明；EHR 状态基于 MEDS 标准化纵向事件，只使用预测时点（入院 24 小时、急诊到达 2 小时、分诊时刻、出院时）之前的信息。四个知识/诊断基准：MedQA、USMLE、NEJM Case Challenges、DiagnosisArena（915 例公开子集）；六个 EHR 结局来自 MIMIC-IV 与 MIMIC-IV-ED（院内死亡、住院>7 天、30 天再入院、ED 2 小时收治、ED 分诊收治、ED 分诊去向）。对比零样本 LLM（Qwen3.5-9B/2B、MedGemma-1.5-4B、Gemma-3-4B、Pythia-2.8B，相同提示与概率读出）、文献中 GPT-3.5/4/4o/o1 成绩（作外部参照）以及监督基线（XGBoost、TF-IDF+LR）。指标含准确率、AUROC、ECE、选择性预测覆盖率-准确率曲线、95% bootstrap 置信区间与配对差异；采用 Platt 缩放（两参数）做本地重校准，并扫描 25–1000 个标注样本的标签预算曲线。数据处理与推理全部本地完成（模型服务器仅绑定回环地址）。

Result: 知识/诊断：MedJev 零样本 MedQA 72.5%、USMLE 75.4%、NEJM 80.1%、DiagnosisArena 55.5%，ECE 0.028–0.063，均远超随机水平；较其基座 Qwen3.5-9B 高 3.9/4.6 个百分点（置信区间显著），大幅优于 GPT-3.5，并接近已发表 GPT-4 零样本结果（74.7%/78.9%）；在 NEJM 上高于 GPT-4 报告值（70.3–75.8%），DiagnosisArena 优于 GPT-4o（36.4%）但低于 o1（61.9%），但因评测协议不同（多选 vs 开放式）不可直接比较；MedGemma/Gemma-3-4B/Pythia 明显更差且校准更差。患者级：MedJev 院内死亡 AUROC 0.926（XGBoost 0.902，TF-IDF 0.879），30 天再入院与监督模型相当；在 ED 分诊收治（0.745 vs 0.809）、ED 2 小时收治、住院>7 天上弱于监督模型；System-One 训练相对基座仅在部分任务提升。校准：知识任务 ECE 极低，但患者级严重失准（死亡平均预测 0.312 vs 实际 2.6%，ECE 0.286；其他任务 ECE 0.147–0.272），Platt 重校准后降至 0.007–0.041（与 XGBoost 相当）且不改变 AUROC；跨基准迁移校准参数无效甚至变差。标签效率：50 个样本即可把死亡 ECE 降至约 0.03，200 个样本时各任务 ECE 介于 0.014–0.064；监督模型需约 100–1000 个样本才能匹配 MedJev 的判别力，院内死亡任务在预算内始终无法匹配。选择性预测显示 MedJev 置信度可用于筛选更可靠的预测。局限：正例比例低（死亡 2.6%）导致区间宽；单一提示与序列化格式未调优；MEDS 抽取不完整；MIMIC 单一中心数据；知识题可能存在预训练污染。

Conclusion: System-One（单次前向、无生成文本）模型可以在无需任务特定训练的前提下完成医学决策任务，并有望成为医疗 AI 的新零样本基线：其知识类表现接近闭源前沿模型，且能完全在本地运行、避免传输患者数据。但在患者级结局上，零样本概率不能直接解释为患者风险，必须用少量本地标注（50–200 例）做后验重校准；而当结局受本地流程/资源影响（收治、床位、运营决策）时，监督 XGBoost 仍能获得更高 AUROC。因此建议在评测流程中把“零样本预测”“本地校准”“监督训练”三者分开评估：System-One 提供初始预测，小规模标注集用于对齐概率与本地流行率，必要时再引入本地训练以提升判别力。作者强调结果为研究性产物，未经临床验证，不应用于指导患者诊疗。

Abstract: System One decision models such as Jev answer structured questions in a single forward pass without generating text, offering fast and computationally efficient clinical decision support. We evaluate MedJev, an open System One model that runs locally on a laptop, across ten medical benchmarks spanning medical knowledge, diagnosis, and patient level prediction using MIMIC IV and MIMIC IV ED. We compare MedJev against zero shot LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models. MedJev achieves accuracies of 72.5 percent on MedQA, 75.4 percent on USMLE, and 80.1 percent on NEJM, approaching published GPT 4 performance while maintaining well calibrated confidence estimates (ECE 0.028 to 0.063). On patient level tasks, MedJev achieves an AUROC of 0.926 for In Hospital Mortality, exceeding XGBoost (0.902), but underperforms supervised models on operational outcomes such as ED Triage Admission (0.745 vs. 0.809). Patient level predictions also exhibit substantial miscalibration (In Hospital Mortality ECE 0.286). We introduce a lightweight, two parameter recalibration method that adapts predictions to local patient populations using 50 to 200 labeled examples, reducing ECE to 0.007. Our findings establish open System One models as a promising zero shot baseline for medical AI, combining competitive predictive performance with low computational cost and efficient local calibration. We release our code and evaluation harness to support future research.

</details>


### [3] [Do AI Scientists Know What's New?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36511)
*Miri Liu,Xiayu Zhao,Encheng Xie,ChengXiang Zhai*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文针对 AI 科学发现流水线中的"新颖性检查"提出评测框架并设计新模块 ClaimNov。作者主张新颖性的基本单位应是"贡献主张（claim）"而非整份提案，构建了含 1,060 个提案的四个数据集（已伪装论文、审稿人争议主张、被后人实现的想法、拼接先前贡献的混合提案），配合时间截断的真实标签，审计了 7 个现有新颖性检查并发现：拒绝非新颖工作最多的检查，同样误拒最多后来真正被学界发表的想法（最高误报率 96%–98.5%），且只能靠"整体拒绝"来指认主张级先前工作。提出的 ClaimNov 是一个可解释的细粒度主张级模块：抽取带类型/属性/值的贡献主张→同维度检索先验主张→分级蕴含判定→维度加权聚合→基于完整主张级证据画像的裁决。它在 1.5% 误报率下捕获 97% 的伪装论文（367/380，366 次正确点名源论文），并把 LLM 裁判的误报从 11.8% 降到 1.5%；对 ICLR 接收论文中"被审稿人质疑贡献"的样本仅拒绝 3%，对 100 个拼接了先前贡献的混合提案保留 91 个（最强现有检查为 76）。结论是：按当前检查，AI 科学家基本"不知道什么新"，而 ClaimNov 让新颖性可逐主张地对具体先验论文进行判定，甚至可作为训练 AI 科学家的奖励信号。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AI 科学发现系统（AI Scientist、CoI-Agent、Agent Laboratory 等）普遍在生成想法后插入"新颖性检查"（检索 Semantic Scholar + LLM 裁判）以决定哪些想法值得投入算力与人力。但把新颖性判断放在"整份提案"层面存在三个缺陷：(1) 连人类专家都难以判定整份提案的新颖性，标注昂贵且标注者之间分歧大；(2) 整体通过/拒绝的二元裁决偏离了人类科学的"增量式"（Uzzi et al., 2013）传统，人类高度新颖的论文也并非每个贡献都新颖；(3) 整体拒绝时无法说明到底命中了哪一篇先验工作，也就无法把已有贡献与新贡献区分开。作者因此主张以"主张（claim）"为新颖性的基本单元。同时，现有工作缺少以时间真实标签（后来的真实发表、审稿人争议归因）为基础、系统性的新颖性检查评测，现有基准多基于专家标签或审稿文本，无法衡量"误拒后来被发表想法"这一关键指标。

Method: ① 评测框架与统一契约：向每个检查输入统一的（标题 + 150–400 词描述）提案与固定先验池 {id,title,abstract}，沙箱化其检索（以 text-embedding-3-large 稠密检索替换开放搜索），统一裁判为 Sonnet 4.6（训练截止 2026-01），设定时间截断 T=2026 年 3 月以避免裁判"认识"截断后的论文；输出分三层：L1 判决、L2 新颖性分数、L3 主张级新颖性画像。② 四个数据集共 1,060 个提案：(a) 已完成想法/伪装集——100 篇 ICML 2026 spotlight 论文改写为 4 个递进伪装层级（换口吻、深度改写、换动机重构、对抗性重构），要求 6-gram 重合≤2%，得 380 个可用伪装，池含源论文 + 最多 19 篇 pre-T 近邻；(b) 主张争议集——用正则 + gpt-5-nano 从 8.3k 条 ICLR 2022–23 评审中挖掘"审稿人指认贡献已被 B 建立"的样本，改写为提案体，得到 160 个（其中 62 接收/96 拒稿），并经 3 名标注者人工核验（κ=0.62/0.47，39% 真实争议、67% B 正确）；(c) 后来实现集——30 篇 NeurIPS 2025 锚点论文生成 3,000 个提案，由 Opus 4.6 逐贡献标注在 pre-T 池与 post-T 引用集 F 中的成立情况，取"至少一项在 F 中成立、在池中不成立"的 400 个；(d) 混合集——取 100 个后实现的"新颖"想法，各拼接一篇余弦排名 5–15 的论文 B 的核心贡献。③ 指标：catch（拦截伪装率）、FA（对后实现想法的误报率）、Src. out（移除源论文后仍拒绝的比例）、信息量 J=catch−FA、池翻转 Δ=catch−Src. out、归因命中率（pointing to B / on pass）。④ ClaimNov 五阶段：主张抽取（gpt-4o-mini，GEPA 调优提示词，四维度 {Problem, Methodology, Resource, Result} + 属性/值对，平均 2.4–2.7 条/提案，F1≈0.67）；同维度主张检索（text-embedding-3-large，题名+claim 嵌入，k=max(10, 0.2n_d)，上限 40，每篇论文最多取一条 claim）；分级蕴含判定（1–5 级序数刻度并映射到 [0,1]，给标题+摘要上下文）；新颖性聚合（秩折减均值 α=0.5，维度权重 Problem 0.4/Result 0.3/Methodology 0.2/Resource 0.1，得 N(P)）；裁决（claude-sonnet-4-6 读取完整主张级画像 Φ(P)，输出 novel/not_novel、点名先验论文、已成立的 claim 子集与理由）。⑤ 审计对象：AI Scientist v1、CoI-Agent、Si et al.、ARC、ResearchAgent、ScholarEval、AI-Scientist-v2，加一个仿 OpenNovelty 的逐贡献基线，以及 ClaimNov 的五个消融（去主张画像、去裁决裁判、逐 claim 判决规则、固定检索深度等）。

Result: 整体提案层面：除 ARC 与 ScholarEval 外各检查可拦下 380 个伪装中的 ≥338 个，但多数检查"移走源论文后仍继续拒绝"（Si et al. 移除后仍拒 359/380）。除 ClaimNov（1.5%）与 CoI-Agent（3.8%）外，各检查对后实现想法误报极高：Si et al. 96%、ResearchAgent 98.5%、AI Scientist v1 51.8%、AI-Scientist-v2 39.2%、OpenNovelty 式 11.5%。ClaimNov 捕获 367/380 并点名源论文 366 次，J=+0.95、Δ=+0.92 均为最高，判定成本 $0.010/提案 vs CoI-Agent $0.039。消融显示：去掉主张级画像（改读 top-8 摘要）FA 由 1.5% 升至 11.8%；改为"任一核心 claim 被蕴含即拒绝"可捕获全部 380 但 FA 升至 56.8%、误拒 197 个已移除源论文的伪装，说明"提案不是一个大 claim"。主张层面（n=160）：ClaimNov 对 ICLR 接收论文的拒绝率仅 3%（Si et al. 81%、AI Scientist v1 53%、ResearchAgent 47%）；现有检查只在拒绝时才点名先验，故"通过时仍能点名 B"比例极低（Si et al. 0%、CoI-Agent 0%、OpenNovelty 式 12%，ClaimNov 20%）；统一使用稠密排序归因后，ClaimNov 通过并点名 B 的比例 36%（CoI-Agent 31%，p=.016）。混合提案（n=100）：ClaimNov 通过 91（CoI-Agent 76，p=.004），用 BM25 共享排序时保留 67 个且点名 B（CoI-Agent 53，p=.004；OpenNovelty 式 64 但 FA 11.5%）。稳健性上：换 gpt-5 标注器 FA 仍为 1.3%；换 gpt-oss-120b / Llama 4 Maverick 作裁决裁判时提供画像仍能降低 FA；池扩至约 200 篇时最難层级 catch 下降但 Src. out 仍近零；人工审计 60 个生成想法，28/45 后实现想法被判为新颖，ClaimNov 在这些新颖想法上仅误拒 2 个。

Conclusion: 现有新颖性检查"要么几乎不拒（ARC/ScholarEval），要么拒掉大量学界后来真正发表的工作"，整体上 AI 科学家并不擅长判断什么新；且以提案为单位的检查只能在整体拒绝时顺带指认主张级先验。ClaimNov 证明"逐主张、带证据的可解释新颖性判定"可以同时做到高敏感度与高特异度（97% 拦截 @1.5% 误报），并且能保留"建立于已有工作之上的部分新颖提案"，在同等归因排序下让更多正确归因的提案进入下游流水线。展望：ClaimNov 的主张级画像不仅可作过滤器，还可能作为训练 AI 科学家的奖励信号（不惩罚科学主流的增量式后续工作，并告诉智能体哪些贡献是新的）。局限：新颖性定义依赖启发式与 LLM 标注而非"真实"数据集；仅限 AI 领域与英文研究，维度权重等先验需按领域重调；先验池为固定列表而非开放搜索，故难以评估检索环节；伪装与生成想法与最终裁判同属 Sonnet 4.6 家族，存在 LLM-as-judge 偏差；时间截断构造会随时间失效，需重建数据；模块在"生成—检查—再生成"回路中对最终提交想法集合的影响与算力成本仅做了小规模试验，留待未来工作。

Abstract: A major challenge facing AI scientific discovery pipelines is how to determine when a generated idea is meaningfully novel. Ideally, novelty checks in these pipelines must be able to reject non-novel ideas while not rejecting too many novel ideas, and they should also be able to distinguish which parts of a proposal are non-novel, as opposed to opaquely discarding entire proposals. We design an analytical framework for evaluation of novelty checks with temporal ground truth at both the proposal- and claim-level, using four datasets of 1,060 proposals built from published papers, reviewer disputes, and generated ideas matching ones the field went on to publish. Auditing existing novelty checks with this framework, we find that checks with high rejection rates on non-novel work also tend to have high false alarms on ideas that are later realized by human researchers, and observe that checks built to evaluate proposals as a whole can point to claim-level prior art only by rejecting the whole proposal. We therefore introduce ClaimNov, a fine-grained, interpretable claim-level novelty module. ClaimNov catches 97% of disguised papers at a 1.5% false-alarm rate, and its claim-level novelty profile cuts the LLM judge's false alarms from 11.8% to 1.5%. Because its verdict rests on claim-level evidence, ClaimNov also keeps proposals that build on established contributions, rejecting only 3% of ICLR-accepted proposals with a reviewer-disputed contribution and keeping 91 of 100 novel proposals with one spliced prior contribution, against 76 for the strongest existing check. Code and data are available at this https URL .

</details>


### [4] [A Quantitative Approach to Asch Conformity in Frontier Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36668)
*Senthil Rajasekaran,Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出一种定量化的阿希从众（Asch conformity）测量方法：对同一道题反复采样得到答案分布，再与呈现人造共识后的答案分布做分布对分布比较。在10个SAT式填空句、6个前沿LLM（OpenAI/Anthropic/Google各2个）上的实验表明：所有模型都会从众；且从众程度强烈依赖于共识答案与模型自身偏好的语义距离——向模型自己会说出的"偏好词"从众最强（n=1时22个百分点，n=10时49个百分点），向语义相近但未说过的词明显较弱（近30、中24），向语义很远的词几乎为0；且从众幅度在群体规模超过5后基本饱和甚至回落。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 阿希从众实验近来被广泛用于测量LLM的从众倾向，但已有研究（Bito等、Zhu等、Bajaj & Tiganj、Weng等、Choi等、Baltaji等）大多只在"多道题各问一次"的定性层面展示从众现象，缺乏量化指标；同时人类阿希实验的关键机制——社会压力——在LLM设定中并无对应物，因此需要一个既能自然触发LLM能力、又能替代社会压力的实验设计。作者的目标是利用LLM固有的概率性，把"单题多次采样"形成的答案分布作为基线，从而定量刻画共识介入前后的分布变化，并揭示促成从众的条件及程度。此外，随着智能体系统（agentic systems）中文本模型之间以及与人类交互的增多，从众行为的安全与可控性变得愈发重要。

Method: 任务设计：将阿希的"线条匹配"替换为2015年SAT式带对比从句的填空句（填形容词/名词），因补词任务贴近LLM训练的下一词预测；将社会压力替换为提示中列出的"其他参与者答案"。三步流程：（1）采样阶段——每个模型对每个句子做T=100次开放式补词（temperature=1，每次独立新会话），得到答案分布；出现频率≥τ=5%的词为"偏好词"（preferred-model-words），按频次排序为w1…wR（R=4）；（2）生成"非偏好词"——用gpt-5.6-terra（temperature 0、关闭推理）生成模型从未输出的合法词，按与w1的语义接近度分为near/medium/far三级（比较填入前后的句子含义），另加两个far词作为填充项f1、f2；填充词由gpt-5.6-terra生成，模型间共用以保证可比性；（3）组建设问——(w1,wr)型问题（R-1个）与(w1,u)、(u,u')型问题（6个），每题四选项为所选词对加两个填充词。测量：单独阶段（alone）与群体阶段（group）各T=100次，群体阶段提示中列出n个"其他参与者"且均选择单独阶段中模型较少选择的词（即干扰项distractor）；群体规模G={1,2,5,10}，各阶段使用相同的选项排列顺序以排除位置效应。指标：分众位移Δn=ŝn−ŝ0（干扰项选择率变化），以及单独/群体答案分布间的总变差距离（TVD）与Jensen–Shannon散度（JSD，比特）。统计：每题每n用双侧Fisher精确检验，p值在"单模型单句"内用Holm校正；跨模型/句子汇总用模型-句子对的95%聚类自助区间；题型间比较用配对差值的Wilcoxon符号秩检验；另用2万次相位置换检验（卡方统计量，未校正）交叉验证。共6模型×10句×6种题型的396道题、197,976次计入试验，运行时间2026年10月13–19日。

Result: 六个前沿模型全部表现从众，强化了既有文献。汇总结果：(w1,wp)题型从众位移最大，n=1时22个百分点升至n=10时49个百分点；与w1配对的非偏好词中，near在n=10时位移30个百分点、medium为24、far为0；两个非偏好词互配时(near,medium)达43个百分点，而涉及far的两类组合均低于1个百分点。所有有位移的题型位移随n从1增至5而上升，n=5到10之间变化不足3个百分点；单题检验中，(w1,wp)36题中31题显著、(w1,near)60题中38题、(w1,medium)60题中28题、(near,medium)60题中47题显著，(medium,far)仅3题显著，(w1,far)与(near,far)无一显著，另有2题显著下降。模型差异明显：n=10时(w1,wp)位移从claude-opus-5-5的33个百分点到gemini-3.8-flash的73个百分点不等，后者在其余三类题型上同样位移最大；个别模型（如gpt-6-sol）在四类题型上n=5到n=10反而下降。句内配对对比：(w1,wp)比(w1,near)高14–19个百分点（26个模型-句子对，Wilcoxon p≤.016）；(w1,near)比(w1,medium)高3–7个百分点但不显著（p≥.052）；(w1,medium)比(w1,far)高5–24个百分点（60对，p≤1.4×10⁻⁴）。分布层面：填充词仅在197,976次试验中被选择583次，说明分众位移几乎解释了答案分布的全部变化；1,584个"题×n"组合中有1,564个的TVD与|Δn|相差不超过0.02。

Conclusion: 三点核心结论：（1）从众高度依赖于被期望从众的答案本身——若共识答案接近模型自身输出（如(w1,wp)），从众即刻且显著；面对语义很远的答案几乎为零。（2）从众在"信息性影响"设定（偏好词，即模型本已认为可行的答案）明显强于"规范性影响"设定（非偏好词，即模型从未给过的答案）。（3）从众并不随"其他参与者"人数单调放大：n=5与n=10差异很小，多例中n=5时反而选择干扰项更多，这与"人数越多压力越大"的直觉相悖。作者据此提出一条"制造从众"的可行路径：与其用大量智能体让模型一次性从众到与其自身判断相距甚远的答案，不如通过一系列由更少智能体提出的、语义上小幅渐进的步骤来实现顺从，这对多智能体系统中的说服与抗性设计有直接意义。局限：前沿模型不开放内部输出分布，只能用T=100次采样作经验近似，引入额外不确定性；题型刻意限定为2015年SAT式填空，通用性受限；仅10个句子、10个规模档位，样本覆盖有限。

Abstract: The Asch conformity experiment has recently gained considerable attention as a way of measuring conformity in large language models (LLMs). While previous studies have focused on demonstrating conformity in LLMs, our work adds a further quantitative layer to this approach. Instead of sampling a frontier LLM on a suite of questions, our approach samples a single question repeatedly, leveraging the probabilistic nature of LLMs to produce a distribution of answers. In doing so, we can compare the distributions of answers before and after the model is presented with the manufactured consensus. Our experiments confirm that frontier LLMs do conform, reinforcing prior literature, and, through our distribution-to-distribution comparisons, provide additional quantitative data on the conditions that lead to conformity and the degree to which it occurs.

*Steven Y. Feng,Michael C. Frank*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本研究在"儿童尺度"数据量下系统考察小语言模型的学习：固定学习器（GPT-2 风格模型），只改变训练数据的数量、来源与多样性，并在自然数据（BabyView 家庭录音转写，约 4.67M 词）与合成数据（TinyDialogues 2 岁儿童导向对话，最高 12.8M 词）上对照，辅以 Kneser-Ney 5-gram 计数基线作为诊断。三个核心发现：(1) 模型强烈"特化"到训练过的某个儿童的语言环境（同环境优势约 0.77 BPW，16/16 儿童一致），且该效应主要来自少量未见词（占评估词 6.2% 却贡献 94.8% 的优势），简单的 5-gram 即可复现跨儿童模式（r=.91），说明特化主要是词汇/分布性的而非语法性的；(2) 在固定 100k 词预算下，混合更多儿童的环境显著改善对合并留出语言的预测（每 ln k 下降 0.124 BPW，p<.001），但语法基准（Zorro）无清晰提升（p≈.28）；(3) 自然与合成输入在规模化过程中支持不同的语法与词汇语义学习模式：BabyView 在 Zorro 上更好（+4.51 个百分点，差异几乎全由负极性项 NPI 贡献），TinyDialogues 在词汇相似度上更好，且 5-gram 无法复现该神经模式；低数据区单一幂律拟合不通过预设检验。结论是：描述小数据语言学习不能只看数据量，还须考虑输入来自哪些环境以及训练分布与评测分布的匹配度。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现代语言模型预训练语料规模（10^12–10^13 词）远大于儿童早期实际接触量（10^7–10^8 词），而关于"从小型自然数据中学习"我们知道得很少。BabyLM 等工作固定训练数据而比较学习方法，本文采取互补路径：固定学习者与训练管线（controlled-rearing 思路），只改变输入数据的性质，从而回答"什么样的输入让学习与泛化更容易或更难"。作者明确声明目的不是模拟儿童的学习机制，而是利用儿童尺度的真实数据变異来研究分布支持（distributional support）与训练—评测匹配度如何影响小数据学习。此外，当数据极小时，复杂神经表征未必必要，故引入计数基线以判断"看似高级的环境学习效应"能否被简单局部统计量解释。

Method: 【数据】BabyView 2026.1 释出的儿童家庭环境第一视角录音转写，英文过滤后约 4.67M 词；主扩展系列取 25k/50k/100k/200k/400k/800k/1.6M/3.2M 词的嵌套随机子集，每规模 3 次语料抽样（full 4.67M 单独报告，1 draw × 3 seeds）。TinyDialogues 合成儿童导向对话（age-2 条件，25k–12.8M 词；另设 M1 混合年龄 2/5/10，M2 因同时更换生成器而不用于年龄归因）。【模型】GPT-2 风格因果 LM：micro（13.9M，6 层/8 头/宽 384）与 small（91.6M，12 层/12 头/宽 768），1024 上下文、tied embeddings；扩展实验每个语料单独训 7.5k BPE（保留切分上训练）；个体环境/持续性/多样性实验用共享 16k BPE 的 micro（17.2M）；训练 20 epoch，按验证损失选主 checkpoint（另报最终 checkpoint）。对照实验：Kneser-Ney 5-gram（KN-5，小写、仅句内条件、闭合词表）。【评测】内容 bits per word（BPW，交叉语料时仅在同文本上比较）；语法基准 Zorro（46k 最小对、13 类现象，比较两句对数概率和）＋按 token 归一化的敏感度分析＋BLiMP；词汇语义用五个词相似度基准（WordSim 等）末层表示的余弦相似度与人类评分做 Spearman 相关（固定层选择，不逐测试集选层）。【统计】扩展用两阶段 bootstrap（先重采样嵌套语料轨迹再重采样种子，2000 次）；个体环境/持续性用儿童聚类 bootstrap 与置换检验（持续性 10000 次）；多样性用 HC1 区间与对 63 个固定预算混合集的 Monte-Carlo 标签置换；幂律拟合按预先设定的 5 项判据（A1–A5）检验。另做超参网格（学习率/dropout/weight decay/训练轮数，600 次运行）、儿童自身言语移除对照（10 儿童）、合成环境异质性操纵（α∈{0,.25,.5,.75,1} 等）与 JSD 测量。

Result: 1) 特化：16 儿童 × 3 抽样 × 3 种子 = 144 个模型，同环境优势 0.769 BPW（95% CI [0.623, 0.921]，16/16 为正）；Zorro 跨儿童差异很小（方差比 0.13）。仅用他人言语评测时优势几乎不变（0.775 vs 0.769 BPW），说明特化超出儿童自身言语；特异移除该儿童言语比随机移除同等量言语更差（+0.257 BPW，10/10，p=.002），但 Zorro/BLiMP 无差异。优势高度集中于训练未见词（6.2% 词贡献 94.8% 优势）。KN-5 与 GPT-2 跨儿童矩阵相关性 r=.91（240 组非对角；含对角 r=.968；Spearman ρ=.883），说明跨儿童模式基本可由局部统计量解释。
2) 持续性：以 CDI 词汇表日期设训练截止点，评估之后他人言语；0–3 月 0.640、3–6 月 0.525、6–12 月 0.456、12 月以上 0.326 BPW；斜率 −0.0376 BPW/月（−0.0575, −0.0218），独立的按时间前缀分析为 −0.0321；因时间与儿童年龄共变，不能做因果解释。
3) 多样性（100k 词固定预算，k∈{1,3,10,18}）：合并留出 BPW 每 ln k 下降 0.1236（p=0.0001）；留一法中 unigram JSD 解释力 R²=.930 高于 ln k 的 .673（组合描述符 .974，词表覆盖 .719）；Zorro 无清晰趋势（斜率 +0.20 pp/ln k，p=.279），250k 复现中 per-token Zorro 为正（p=.044）、主指标较弱（p=.085）、BLiMP 为空。
4) 规模与来源：BabyView 在 Zorro 上整体优于 age-2 TinyDialogues（GPT-2 small 800k–3.2M 词约 +4.51 pp，micro +2.36），优势几乎全部来自 NPI 许可（约 +32.4 pp；仅 only/even 子集），BabyView 在 binding、岛效应、不规则形式上也更好，而 TinyDialogues 在量词等类别更好；KN-5 的 NPI 差异反而倒向合成数据（−13.9 pp），且总体优势较小（+1.69 pp），故计数基线不能解释该神经模式。词相似度方向相反：800k–3.2M 词共同词对下 BabyView 比 age-2 低 0.057（全部词对 −0.017），即合成数据在词汇语义上更好。25k 词时 BabyView Zorro 59.44%（随机初始化 48.41%），增益集中在主谓一致之外的现象（主谓一致 +0.1、省略 −13.7）。KN-5 与 GPT-2 的交叉点：固定配方下 BabyView 在 800k–1.6M、age-2 在 200k–400k；调参后 BabyView 提前到 400k–800k，age-2 不变。单一幂律未通过全部预设判据（BabyView micro 加权 R²=.965，幂律 AICc 71.9 劣于对数线性 58.5）。
5) 合成操纵：随混合参数 α 增大，JSD 由 0.0345 升至 0.1524，同环境优势从 −0.002 增至 2.107 BPW，单调；但 interlocutor-only 操纵在相近 JSD 下优势达 0.976 BPW（约为主序列插值的 4.1 倍），说明 unigram JSD 不是普适预测量。BabyView 在 JSD 0.106 处的 0.769 BPW 与合成主序列相容，但更集中于未见词汇。
6) 发展学指标：模型词汇学习顺序未能超出词频/具体性/词类的基线来预测 Wordbank 习得年龄（ΔAIC=+0.66，r=−0.085）；基于 CDI 的"能产 vs 不能产"区分优势（ΔAUC=0.0229，p=.0006）在控制词频后消失并反转（−0.0147）。

Conclusion: 小数据语言学习的成败不仅取决于"看了多少词"，还取决于"词来自哪些环境"以及训练分布与待预测分布的匹配程度。(1) 儿童语言环境在模型预测上留下强且持续的印记，但这种特化主要是词汇与分布性的，集中于极小比例的未见词，并能被简单 5-gram 复现，因此不能据此断言每个儿童拥有不同的全局语法；(2) 跨儿童在语法基准上的差异很小，说明"环境匹配度"与"更广泛的语言泛化"不必同步变化；(3) 固定预算下增加说话人数/环境多样性明确改善对合并留出语言的预测（且与训练—目标分布相似度而非人数本身更相关），但对语法泛化的增益较小且不一致，作者因此不主张"多样性对语法从无助益"；(4) 自然与合成输入在语法与词汇语义上各有优势，且这些差异具有现象级特异性并无法由局部计数统计解释，说明不存在哪种输入"总体更优"的通用结论。局限：数据规模远小于儿童真实暴露量（100k 词个体实验尤甚）、仅覆盖 18 个儿童且语料抽样仅 3 次（bootstrap 精度有限、多重比较未校正）、GPT-2 非儿童的认知模型、Zorro/BLiMP/WordSim 只测特定模型行为、不同语料的绝对 BPW 不可直接互比、实验为固定配方（非算力最优）、合成数据带生成器特征、未测试对全新儿童的迁移。作者建议后续区分专名/转写伪影与生僻词、检验对未见儿童的迁移、扩展到视频音频的多模态接地输入、以及在更大或算力匹配模型上重复。

Abstract: Modern language models are trained on far more language than children experience, but we know much less about learning from small, naturalistic datasets. We train small GPT-2 models on transcripts of speech with children from dense home recordings (BabyView) and on synthetic child-directed dialogue (TinyDialogues), varying the amount, source, and diversity of training data. Models trained on one child's language environment predict that environment substantially better than other children's environments. Much of this specialization is lexical and distributional: a simple 5-gram model reproduces the cross-child pattern (r=.91). Across data sizes, naturalistic and synthetic training inputs also produce different grammatical and lexical-semantic patterns, with important differences between grammatical phenomena. Together, these results show that small-data language learning depends not only on how much language a model sees, but on which environments it comes from and how well that input matches what the model is asked to predict.

<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有语音语言模型（SLM）几乎都是闭源且以英语/中文为主，巴斯克语等少数民族语言在多模态浪潮中差距被进一步拉大：语音数据必须属于目标语言，且不存在公开的巴斯克语语音指令数据集。同时，LLaMA-Omni、LLaMA-Omni2、Spirit LM 等开源权重模型仍集中于英语和中文，缺乏针对低资源语言的设计与训练配方研究。因此作者希望探索：在不进行大规模多模态预训练的前提下，如何用模块化架构与合成数据构建一个低延迟、端到端的巴斯克语 SLM，其方案有望推广到其他同规模低资源语言。

### [7] [Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36948)
*XinYu Piao,Myunghoon Ryu,Joongheon Kim,Jong-Kook Kim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出 SKIM（Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization，自密钥参数内记忆）：在冻结模型、无外部记忆、且事先不知道未来提问与答案的设定下，由模型自己为每一轮对话生成"自问"并把问答对以闭式（岭回归）解一次性写入某一中后层前馈网络的下投影矩阵中，从而在后续用户提问时仅靠一次前向传播从参数内检索并回答对话内容。五个开源模型、LongMemEval 上 32 轮存储时平均召回率 63.1%（最强模型 75.0%），显著高于"无缓存"下限 3.1%–15.6%；且逐轮流式写入与整体批处理编辑结果完全一致（无遗忘）。主要瓶颈在存储期的片段抽取与选择，而非寻址（routing 失败为 0）。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有对话式 LLM 把历史对话存放在参数之外：KV cache 随对话长度线性增长并抬升显存与推理成本，RAG 则把对话放进外部索引，答案质量取决于索引是否命中以及问题能否被改写成有效查询。作者提出的核心问题是：一个冻结的模型能否把对话"内化"进自身参数，在没有任何外部记忆的条件下，仅凭后续提问从参数中给出答案？

已有参数内记忆路线（ROME、MEMIT、AlphaEdit 等闭式权重编辑）依赖两个在对话场景中不成立的假设：(1) 必须预先提供要写入的"对象"（ground-truth answer）作为编辑求解的目标标签；(2) 必须事先知道固定的"线索"（如 subject–relation）作为触发键。对话既没有标注答案，也没有已知的未来提问，因此这些监督无法获得；而外部缓存/检索则用不断增长的存储成本换取了这种监督的免需求。

因此本文的目标被明确界定为"可行性验证"而非超越检索或长上下文系统：考察在四种约束下（无梯度微调、召回时无外部记忆、每轮存储开销不随已存轮数增长、保持模型原有通用行为）能否实现参数内对话记忆。

Method: **总体框架（三阶段 + 召回）**

1. **候选片段抽取（value harvest）**：用冻结模型对当前用户轮 u 提示，列出该轮陈述的短答案短语；同时直接取文本中的引号标题与首字母大写实体短语，滤成数词的短连续片段，构成候选值集合 S(u)。每个片段 s 在无答案条件下打分：
 ρ(s) = E_{q~Q0(s)}[log p_M(s|q,u)] + β·π(s)，
 其中第一项衡量"可被自身问题复原"的恢复性，第二项是特异性先验 π(s)（在中性提示下的负对数概率，偏向稀有片段），β 平衡二者。保留 top-k 片段，把"该存什么"的选择推迟到召回时刻。

2. **自生成问题作为键（self-keyed construction）**：对每个片段 s，用 k_q 种固定风格提示生成以其为答案的问题 q，并以判别性间隔排序：
 μ(q,s) = log p_M(s|q,u) − max_{s'≠s} log p_M(s'|q,u)。
 保留 top-m 个问题（先剔除与同轮竞争片段表面形式的用词），再用确定性字符串变体扩展（疑问词替换、包裹为"Earlier, the answer to '…' was"等重构）。这些多样化的键替代了传统编辑必须预先给定的固定 subject–relation 线索，使得措辞不同的后验提问仍能匹配某个键。

3. **单层联合闭式编辑**：键 k_j = h^(ℓ)(frame(r_j)) 取第 ℓ 层下投影在答案位置的隐藏状态（存储键与召回键共用同一 frame，保证一致）；值 d_j = f·δ_j，其中 δ_j 通过一次短梯度优化求出（权重保持冻结），使 span 成为 frame 的续写；f 为写入强度。累积所有 (问题, 片段) 对组成 K、D，用岭回归闭式解 ΔW = D(KᵀK + λI)⁻¹Kᵀ 一次性解出，加入第 ℓ 层下投影 W，层充当"值记忆"。

4. **召回**：把用户提问放入同一 frame，编辑后的模型一次前向传播解码出答案（按模型选用贪心或小 beam，阻止重复 n-gram，按答案完成/句末停止）。

**抗遗忘**：每来一批对话就丢弃旧 ΔW、从原始权重对"到目前为止的全部对"重新求解（式 14）。由于 Gram 矩阵 KᵀK 与 D Kᵀ 是顺序无关的求和，流式结果恒等于一次性批处理编辑；而"增量叠加 ΔW ← ΔW + ΔW_t"（AlphaEdit 式）会从不联合求逆而使早期轮次漂移。

**自探针超参选择**：θ = (ℓ, f, 解码预设, 键预算) 在存储时固定、不可按未来问题调优。用每个条目自身问题的"未使用改写"做替身探针，统计是否干净输出该片段（含该片段、无三阶 token 重复、词汇多样性 > 0.5），以 af_clean(θ) 最大者选配置，全程不需要真值答案。

**实验设置**：LongMemEval 单会话用户子集，去除数值型问题后剩 33 条非数值事实，N 从 4 增长到 32；五个模型 Qwen3-14B、Mistral-Nemo-12B、Yi-1.5-9B、Llama-3-8B、Mistral-7B（四个独立家族），各配一套 (ℓ, f, λ, 解码, Self-Q=k_q,m)；单卡 A100 80GB，前向 BF16、闭式解 FP32。正确判定需归一化真值被生成包含且双向 DeBERTa-MNLI 判定蕴含。

Result: **召回归因（N=32）**：KV cache 与 True-Q（给答案+真问题）约 90%–100%；Self-Q（给答案、用自生成问题）≥80%、均值约 91.3%（较 True-Q 平均仅降约 6.88%）；SKIM（答案也自抽取）46.9%–75.0%，五模型均值 63.1%（较 Self-Q 平均降约 26.9%）；"无任何记忆"下限 3.1%–15.6%。这说明参数本身足以承载并寻址记忆，主要损失来自"用自抽取片段替代给定答案"。

**规模趋势**：所有模型 N=4 时接近 100%，随 N 增大平缓下降、无突变台阶；N=32 时 Qwen3 最高 75.0%（未召回 8/32），Mistral 最低 46.9%（未召回 17/32）。

**失效阶段定位**：五模型共 59 次失败——store 期的 missing 22、selection 22，recall 期的 routing 0、decoding 15。约四分之三失败发生在存储期（片段未抽出或被同轮竞争片段顶替），routing 为 0 表明闭式键总能命中目标事实、寻址不是瓶颈。13 种干预（改键几何、扩键预算、重调层与正则、放宽 beam 与停止准则）均无法修正 selection 失败。

**答案类型与写入位置**：专有名词答案召回 81.1%，描述性多词短语仅 36.9%，相差约 44 分，且在各位置组内普遍成立；表面上的"近期轮次更难"实为答案类型混杂（近期组恰含更多描述性事实），并非遗忘。

**流式=批处理**：五个模型 N=4→32 的流式召回与批处理召回点全部落在恒等线上，与式 (14) 的置换不变性推导一致。

**其他局限**：数值型答案（日期/计数）缺乏特异性且难以精确复现数字位；作者也承认由于环境设定（无真值答案/问题）不同，既往权重编辑方法无法直接作为可比基线，True-Q 条件实际上就充当了该上限参照。

Conclusion: 在"无外部记忆、无未来问题与答案、冻结模型、对话逐轮到来"的假设环境下，SKIM 证明了对话内容确实可以被内化进固定大小的模型参数：模型自生成的问题充当键、自抽取的片段充当值，经一次闭式联合编辑写入单个中后层前馈下投影；32 轮存储下五模型平均召回 63.1%、最强模型 75.0%，远高于无记忆下限 3.1%–15.6%。通过每次从原始权重重解，流式写入与一次性批处理编辑完全等价，说明顺序写入带来的遗忘可被规避；且存储规模不随对话增长，代价仅为离线重解的计算开销（与"每轮开销恒定"的约束略有张力）。

研究同时定位了真正的瓶颈与后续方向：限制因素是存储期的自我抽取与片段选择（尤其是带同轮竞争片段的描述性多词答案，召回仅 36.9%），而非寻址或生成（routing 失败为 0）；因此改进自监督的片段抽取质量是"最清晰的提升杠杆"，13 种针对选择失败的干预均无效也印证了这一点。此外，数值型答案与措辞极度偏离自生成键的提问仍是未解难题。整体而言，本文给出的是可行性证明与失效模式诊断，而非可与 RAG/长上下文系统正面比较的性能成果。

Abstract: A large language model maintains conversational content in an external storage that is outside the model and grows as the dialogue continues. This work assumes an environment where a language model has no external memory and no prior knowledge of the future question or its answer. The motivation is to research whether a dialogue can be stored in the model parameters and later answer a question about it. This work proposes self-keyed in-parameter memorization (SKIM), a closed-form method in which the model generates its own questions about each dialogue turn and writes those questions into its parameters as the keys that later retrieve the turn's content. Generating many varied questions for each turn allows a later user question to match one even when phrased differently, and its answer is recalled from the parameters alone. Evaluated on five language models, SKIM recalls most stored dialogue turns from later user questions, and it answers from the model parameters without any external storage.

</details>


### [8] [Aligning Large Language Models for Safety in African Languages: A Case Study of Hausa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37245)
*Valdini Douglace Lemofouet,Blessing Ngozi Uzor,Paula Chikaodinaka Anyanwu,Danielle Blanche Kapsa,Saminu Mohammad Aliyu,Seid Muhie Yimam,Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文以豪萨语（Hausa）为案例，构建了首个豪萨语安全偏好数据集 HausaSafeLM（1 万条：3,000 条人工校译「金标」+ 7,000 条纯机器翻译「银标」，覆盖 6 大危害宏类），并在 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 上用 LoRA 做了 Base / SFT-G / SFT-GS / DPO-G / DPO-GS 五种配置的受控对比。核心结论是：在低资源语言中「拒答率（RR）」会立刻饱和（所有配置均为 1.000），无法区分「真正对齐」与「根本不会用该语言输出」；SFT 主要提升拒答的语言流畅度与数据规模收益，DPO 主要提升拒答判别精度却几乎不改善流畅度且对数据量不敏感，最终不存在同时兼顾安全、有用与语言流畅度的单一最优配置。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有 LLM 安全对齐研究与评测几乎全部集中在英语等高资源语言，低资源且文化情境迥异的语言中「什么算有害」并不同一，且英语语境下产生拒答行为的机制不能自动迁移（已有工作显示低资源语言的毒性更高、拒答质量更差，翻译攻击可绕过安全护栏）。豪萨语拥有超 2 亿使用者但缺乏系统性对齐研究，因此本文将其作为「多语言表征有限时对齐方法表现如何」的自然实验场。论文由此提出四个研究问题：基座模型在豪萨语有害提示上的真实行为；SFT 与 SFT+DPO 的对比；对齐税（安全—流畅—有用之间的权衡）；数据质量与数据量孰重。

Method: 数据集：以 PKU-SafeRLHF（约 7 万条英文安全偏好数据）为源，剔除 4 类在西非语境不 salient 的类别，将 15 个细类归并为 6 大危害宏类（暴力与身体伤害、仇恨言论与歧视、性内容、犯罪活动、健康与公共安全、心理操纵），得到约 1 万条过滤样本；按类别均衡分层抽样为互不重叠的金标（3,000 条，Google Translate 逐字段翻译后经流畅性—语义—语域—本地化四道人工后编辑）与银标（7,000 条，仅机器翻译），从而隔离「翻译噪声」与「生成流程」两类变量；每条另标注敏感度（低 40%/中 40%/高 20%），并导出 SFT（prompt, chosen）与 DPO（prompt, chosen, rejected）两种训练格式。模型与训练：基座为 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct，LoRA（作用于 q/k/v/o 投影层）参数高效微调，2×A100 80GB，数据划分为 gold-only 与 gold+silver 两种制度，依次得到 Baseline、SFT-G、SFT-GS、DPO-G、DPO-GS 五个配置（DPO 在对应 SFT 检查点上继续训练）。评测：500 条留出豪萨语有害提示（按危害类别与数据层分层）+ 200 条取自 Aya 的豪萨语良性提示，由 Gemini 作为单一 LLM 裁判依据结构化评分细则给出三轴判定（SAFE/UNSAFE；HELPFUL/PARTIAL/REFUSED；HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW）；报告 RR、FRR、HR、SafeQ、AyaQ 五个指标，并刻意不报 ASR（因其定义为 1−RR，无额外信息），另用雷达图做多维权衡分析。

Result: RQ1：基座模型 RR=1.000 看似完美安全，实为伪信号——96.2% 的拒答被评为低质量（SafeQ=0.021，仅 0.4% 为 HIGH），良性提示上 74.4% 无帮助（HR=0.256，AyaQ=0.165），大量输出根本不构成有效豪萨语回应（含直接输出中文的现象），即「无法生成该语言内容」必然带来「不产生有害内容」。RQ2：SFT 显著提升拒答流畅度（SFT-G 高/中质量占 32%，SFT-GS 占 45%），但 SFT-G 过度拒答严重（FRR=0.405、HR=0.180）；DPO 将 FRR 拉低到 0.110 且保持 RR=1.000，却使 SafeQ 跌回 0.023–0.036（94–95% 低质量），接近未调优基座——因为 DPO 优化的是相对偏好而非绝对质量，对流畅性无激励。RQ3：不存在同时安全、有用、流畅的配置，形成清晰的权衡面：DPO 换取判别精度却牺牲语言质量，SFT 换取流畅与有用却牺牲拒答精度；SFT-GS 是相对最均衡者（SafeQ=0.350、HR=0.260、FRR=0.245）。RQ4：数据规模收益具有阶段性——银标数据对 SFT 收益显著（FRR 0.405→0.245 即 −0.160，HR +0.080，SafeQ +0.112），因其从 chosen 响应中直接模仿；银标偏好对多为「两个安全响应质量不同」的近似重复对，缺乏安全/不安全对比信号，故对 DPO 几乎无效（FRR 不变、HR −0.020、SafeQ 仅 +0.013）。

Conclusion: 论文主张：（1）低资源语言中拒答率是最不可靠的安全代理指标，会立即饱和，必须辅以拒答精度、拒答语言质量与良性有用性等联合指标；（2）现行对齐配方更擅长迁移安全的「决策边界」，而非实施该边界所需的「语言能力」——SFT 教模型「如何」流畅拒答，DPO 教模型「何时」精确拒答，二者不能兼得；（3）数据质量—数量的权衡是阶段依赖的：噪声更大的数据对模仿式 SFT 高度有益，对偏好对比目标几乎无用；（4）因此「错拒或因不理解而全拒」与「自然地拒答并说明理由」提供的是两种本质上不同的安全保证。局限：仅测试单一 7B 基座、单一 LLM 裁判、500+200 条评测规模且缺少 bootstrap 置信区间与显著性检验、AyaQ 部分数值待核验、数据全部源自英语翻译而非豪萨语原生撰写（本地特有危害可能表征不足）。未来方向：构建非洲语言原生安全数据集、引入母语者标注评测、设计在优化偏好的同时抑制语言质量退化的对齐目标，并开发跨语言对齐基准工具与区域化安全数据集（如 UbuntuGuard、AfriGuard、SEALGuard 等方向）。

Abstract: Safety alignment research for large language models (LLMs) remains concentrated on high-resource languages, leaving open how existing alignment methods perform in low-resource, culturally distinct settings. We study this question for Hausa, a language spoken by more than 200 million people across West Africa. We introduce HausaSafeLM, one of the first Hausa safety preference dataset, built from 10,000 prompts derived from PKU-SafeRLHF: 3,000 human-corrected (gold) and 7,000 machine-translated (silver) examples spanning six harm macro-categories. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, we compare supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and SFT followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) under both data regimes, evaluating on 500 harmful and 200 benign Hausa this http URL find that the untuned base model appears highly safe by refusal-rate metrics alone, but this reflects limited Hausa generation ability rather than genuine alignment: its refusals are almost uniformly low quality. SFT improves both refusal fluency and precision and benefits substantially from the larger, noisier silver-tier data, while DPO sharpens refusal precision but comes at a steep, largely data-invariant cost to linguistic quality. No single configuration jointly maximizes safety, helpfulness, and fluency. Our results suggest that current alignment techniques teach models when to refuse more readily than how to do so fluently in underrepresented languages, and that refusal-rate metrics alone are an unreliable signal of safety in low-resource settings.

### [9] [Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37649)
*Zhen Yang,Wen Wang,Xander Xu,Ying-Cong Chen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出 LongChang：一个完全自动化的框架，在 MuJoCo 物理仿真中构造"物理定律被篡改"的模拟世界（1 个正常对照 + 14 个各含一条异常定律的场景），让大语言模型作为"探索者"在无研究任务、无任何提示的条件下自由操作物体、自行设计工具并做实验，试图自主发现隐藏定律；报告再由独立的 LLM 评审与判分（正确性 C + 证据支持性 S）。12 个模型中仅 GPT-6-Astra 取得 16.7% 的发现率，其余 11 个为 0%；且其证据支持率高达 97.6% 而定律正确率仅 19.0%，说明当前 LLM 能"记录到证据"但极少能提炼出完整、有触发条件与适用范围的定律。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 科学发现常始于意外观察，但现有 LLM 科学发现基准（PhysGym、NewtonBench、DiscoverPhysics）都预先指定了发现目标，或直接提供异常现象，因此测量的是"给定问题后的求解能力"而非"自主发现能力"。真正困难的环节是：LLM 能否自己注意到偏离常规物理的现象、提出值得研究的问题、设计能区分竞争解释的实验，并在无人类干预的情况下把结论立起来（既能正确识别定律，又有实验证据支持）。此外，现实世界中大量问题尚无定论，需要一种"答案已知但仅存在于隐藏的仿真定律中"的可控评估环境来系统性检验这一能力。

Method: 框架分三部分：(1) 环境构建——LLM 场景设计者指定物体、几何、物理程序与一条被改写的物理定律，编译为 MuJoCo 仿真（15 个基础场景：Scene 01 为常规物理对照，02–15 各改写一条定律，如红色球相互吸引 F=20d/max(r,0.5)^3、质量相关下落 g0√(m0/m)、振荡重力、速度上限、接触换色、速度复制、北向力等）；设计者同时记录定律的目标对象/条件/可观测效应供评估用，但对探索者保密。场景演化有生成、细化、组合三种操作，依据探索记录中"被纠正的错误"与"未解决问题"来提出修改，且需引用探索证据，通过自动仿真测试与 LLM 复核后才被采纳。(2) 自主探索——探索者以"自由探索并报告所学"为唯一指令，可 PUSH/THROW/WAIT/GRASP/MOVE/RELEASE/MARK 等操作，必要时用 BUILD 提交 MJCF XML 自建装置（摆、称重盘等），由 LLM 审查物理有效性；每轮记录观察与行动理由，最终按严格 JSON 格式提交实验与结论报告，结论必须引用具体轮次且不得引入探索中未记录的新解释。(3) 发现评估——由 LLM 评审对照隐藏定律与完整记录给出两项独立判定：正确性 C（识别全部定律、目标对象、条件、触发器、可辨识常数；机制描述可不同但可观测预测须等价）与证据支持性 S（记录中的实验须支撑全部主张与确定性等级）；同时统计探索长度 L、提前停止 ES、动作失败 AF、构造成功 CS、失败率 CF、控制场景误报数 R。实验包含 12 个 LLM（GPT-5.6-Luna、GPT-6-Astra、Claude-Opus-5、Gemini-3.7-Flash、GLM-5.3/-Flash、Kimi-K3、MiMo-V2.6-Flash/Pro、DeepSeek-Flash、Qwen3-Max、Grok-4.7），统一 15 场景、固定初始状态、最多 100 轮，并做任务引导、轮数预算（100 vs 500）、装置访问（开/关）三组消融。

Result: 主结果：GPT-6-Astra 发现率 D=16.7%（C=19.0%、S=97.6%），其余 11 个模型 D=0%。Claude-Opus-5 呈相反模式（C=16.7% 而 S=0%）；多数模型 S 也很低（0–38%），说明"猜对定律"与"有证据支撑的发现"是两种不同能力。控制场景中 36.1% 的报告被拒（虚构异常定律或对常规物理作无据解释，如把装饰性灰砖上的更远滑行误判为低摩擦，而忽略了初始速度不同）。消融：加入任务引导后 D 从 16.7% 升至 28.6%、C 从 19.0% 升至 31.0%，平均探索长度由 39.3 轮降至 30.9 轮；把预算从 100 轮提高到 500 轮反而略降（D=14.3%），因模型普遍提前停止；禁用装置构建则 D 从 16.7% 降至 4.8%、C 从 19.0% 降至 4.8%。行为统计揭示多种失败模式：Gemini-3.7-Flash 全部提前停止（平均仅 10.9 轮）；GLM 系列约用 90 轮、每次都能造出可用装置却零发现，且 >60% 构造成败率失败、16.8–20.2% 的轮次为失败动作；Grok-4.7 最少提前停止但仍零发现，说明"坚持"与"有装置"都不足以带来发现。案例分析显示关键差异在"提出问题"与"区分竞争解释"：GPT-6-Astra 会因红球意外重启而推迟原计划、测量延迟并测试推挤是否也能重置计时，从而发现"任何推/掷会让北向力暂停 10 秒"；Gemini 观察到同样现象却仍按原计划走。Scene 12 中它用"两个红球"测试区分了"颜色交换"与"独立翻转"两种解释。场景演化实验以 Scene 15 的纠正错误为引导，生成/细化/组合出三个新场景，GPT-6-Astra 在源场景 D=33.3%、Scene 14 为 66.7%，而在三个演化场景中 D 均为 0（S 仍 100%），能部分察觉现象却无法复原多条叠加的触发条件与时序规则。

Conclusion: 当前 LLM 几乎无法在完全自由的探索中完成真正的物理定律发现：12 个模型中仅 1 个取得非零发现率，且其成功几乎全部来自"证据支持"而非"定律正确"，多数模型表现为要么忽略已观察到的异常、要么只做部分识别而无法确定适用条件与触发规则。失败根源不在预算或工具本身——更多轮数无用、造出能用的装置也无用——而在于两点：能否从意外观察中自发形成研究问题，以及能否设计预测结果可区分的对照实验来排除竞争解释。任务引导能提升定律识别但仍远不足以解决，场景演化（引入更复杂的多条件叠加定律）会进一步压低发现率，表明 LLM 在条件依赖、时序与组合律的建模上仍有根本短板。LongChang 提供了一个无需人工标注、可全自动运行的诊断与研究平台，用于研究"决定研究什么并设计实验以消解不确定性"的 LLM；其局限是仅覆盖有明确隐藏答案的仿真场景，尚未解决的真实科学问题仍需新的评估方法。

Abstract: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

</details>


### [10] [FinLLM-KG: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment Analysis in Algorithmic Trading](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36083)
*Giorgos Iacovides,Oliver Hannibal,Wuyang Zhou,Danilo Mandic*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Recent advances in Generative AI have substantially improved financial sentiment analysis through post-trained financial large language models (LLMs). However, existing approaches remain confined to predicting the sentiment of each article in isolation and operate as black boxes, which limits contextual understanding and hinders deployment in high-stakes financial decision-making. To this end, we introduce FinLLM-KG, a model-agnostic framework that combines causal LLMs with a financial knowledge graph, in order to inject temporally grounded, company-level knowledge from SEC 10-K filings at inference time, without updating model weights. Within FinLLM-KG, context is supplied either as a natural-language company profile or as a small set of relevance-ranked factual triples. This enables sentiment predictions to account for broader firm-level information rather than the article alone, at almost zero computational cost and for any causal LLM. In addition, attributing each article-level sentiment score to individual sentences and to the retrieved knowledge-graph facts makes the evidence behind the prediction inspectable, thereby enhancing explainability and supporting human-in-the-loop review. Simulations demonstrate that FinLLM-KG consistently improves portfolio performance over the state-of-the-art baseline.

### [11] [LLM Hallucination Detection via Low-rank Multilinear Decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36191)
*Devansh Sharma,Faizul Rakib Sayem,Shahana Ibrahim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate fluent yet factually incorrect responses, raising concerns about their reliability. Recent hallucination detectors increasingly exploit internal representations, but extracting informative signals from high-dimensional hidden states remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on selected activations or pooling-based compression, potentially overlooking discriminative information distributed across Transformer layers, feature modes, and tokens. We propose LOTUS (Low-rank Order-statistic TUcker-based Subspace learning), a multilinear low-rank decomposition framework for hallucination detection that extracts compact representations from LLM hidden states while reducing dependence on labeled data. Our approach first summarizes variable-length token representations using complementary statistical descriptors that capture peak activations, activation distributions, and cross-layer changes. We then leverage low-rank multilinear decomposition to extract compact representations that capture the underlying structure of LLM hidden states, which are subsequently used to train a lightweight hallucination classifier. Experiments across multiple LLMs and question-answering benchmarks demonstrate improved hallucination detection performance over recent state-of-the-art baselines.

### [12] [Causal Localization of Evidence Effects in Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36524)
*Jipeng Li,Pramod Khargonekar,Yanning Shen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Can controlled symbolic inputs reveal attention heads that influence a language model's decisions from natural language evidence? We introduce controlled evidence aggregation (CEA), which varies the counts and order of two symbols in otherwise fixed prompts and measures changes in a frozen Transformer's preference between two answer tokens. The preference is measured by their logit difference; the prompts prescribe no correct answer. Balanced utility causal selection (BUC) identifies compact head sets by jointly evaluating how much ablating their outputs removes the count effect and how closely patching mean outputs between count conditions recovers the effect in both directions. We derive conditional bounds linking head attribution to intervention effects and specifying when the attribution shortlist can be recovered from finite samples. In Pythia-410M, ablating sets of 1-12 heads selected separately for four ordering regimes removes 65.5-91.6% of the count effect. The sets retain their influence on count comparisons not used for selection. To test relevance beyond symbolic inputs, we evaluate a natural language task asking which state is supported by more reports. Ablating eight heads selected only on symbolic yes/no prompts lowers mean accuracy by 8.2 percentage points, versus 0.8 for random sets matched by size and layer. Our results demonstrate that controlled symbolic probes can identify compact attention head sets whose causal influence extends to natural language decisions.

### [13] [OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36013)
*Xiaomi Embodied Intelligence Team,Yuechen Luo,Chong He,Fang Li,Shaoqing Xu,Jingkai Wang,Menglun Su,Jiaxin Liu,Shengyin Jiang,Zhiyi Lai,Long Chen,Longlong Wang,Liang Hu,Haochen Liu,Yuncheng Jiang,Hongwei Xie,Jieming Cui,Hanbing Li,Junjie Huang,Zhixiang Duan,Hexin Zhang,Weixiang Liang,Ying Gong,Yuhan Wang,Yong Pan,Pengna Li,Kangyi Wu,Ken Deng,Kun Ma,Fuxi Wen,Zhi-xin Yang,Hangjun Ye*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.

### [14] [3, 7, 14, 17, 42: Instruction Tuning Installs and Sharpens Number-Choice Heuristics in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36178)
*Samar Ansari*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We measure, without sampling error, the probability a language model assigns to each integer from 1 to N when asked for a random number. For a fixed prompt the model defines one probability vector, which we compute by summing over each integer's scored spellings rather than estimate by sampling, removing the noise that limits earlier studies [1, 4]. We evaluate 18 open-weight model lines at five ranges up to N = 100, under 29 decoding configurations, on two inference stacks; 15 of them have matched base and instruction-tuned checkpoints that both give usable answers. Instruction tuning makes the distribution less uniform in all 15 pairs. It installs one heuristic, round-number avoidance, and sharpens another, endpoint avoidance. Base checkpoints do not avoid round numbers once the endpoints are removed from those sets; tuned checkpoints avoid them, multiples of 10 almost completely. Base checkpoints return the endpoints 1 and N at 0.30 to 0.60 of the interior rate; tuned checkpoints almost never return them. A preference for odd numbers is consistent across tuned checkpoints only at N = 100, where base checkpoints also show it weakly. Endpoint avoidance and the odd preference fit the account Kubovy and Psotka [6] proposed for human number choice; round-number avoidance is not part of that account, and the midpoint avoidance it predicts is essentially absent, with one slight exception at N = 100. Tuning does not install a new favourite integer shared across models: above N = 10 no modal integer is shared by more than 42 percent of tuned conditions, and P (17) rises in 10 of 15 pairs and falls in 5. The concentration is present in the model's own distribution: at temperature 1.0, nucleus truncation at top-p 0.95 adds a median of 0.035 to the total variation distance.

### [15] [Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36184)
*Sanjid Hasan,A H M Fuad,Risalat Labib,Bayazid Hasan Simon*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Bengali, spoken by over 230 million people, remains severely under-resourced in spoken language research. Existing open Bengali ASR corpora are confined to short, read or crowd-sourced speech and lack speaker diarization and long-form audio. We present Lipi-Ghor, a large-scale weakly-supervised Bengali speech corpus comprising 885 hours of audio sourced from 998 YouTube videos across 596 unique channels, spanning 17 diverse domains including audiobooks, drama, religious sermons, news, and regional dialects. Each recording is annotated in SSTT format (Speaker, Speech, Transcription, Timestamp), which combines automated diarization with Bengali YouTube caption tracks. To our knowledge, Lipi-Ghor is the first Bengali speech corpus to pair large-scale coverage with speaker-diarized, long-form audio annotations, both of which are absent from existing open Bengali resources. We also present the construction methodology as a replicable pipeline for any language with a sufficient captioned YouTube presence. Targeted channel curation across a handful of rich domains yields corpus scales that were previously out of reach for low-resource languages. We benchmark four widely-used ASR models under zero-shot and fine-tuned conditions. All four degrade consistently on emotive, dialectal, and long-form content. Because caption targets are noisy, we also release a human-annotated gold evaluation split, verified by 17 volunteer annotators over 30 hours of human-in-the-loop correction and stratified across all 17 domains. We release our original contributions (video-ID lists, diarization output, pipeline code, and the gold annotations) under CC-BY-4.0, and distribute caption-derived transcripts for research use only; no raw audio is redistributed.

### [16] [Frankly Speaking: The Company Election Integrity Keeps in Congressional Communication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36187)
*Michael A. Robinette,Christina Barsky,Amanda D. Clark,Helen Flannery,Juniper Lovato*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Election integrity is a shared commitment in American politics, but Democrats and Republicans in Congress increasingly mean different things by it. Analyzing 10,420 congressional e-newsletters sent from 2010 to 2025, we examine how the two parties invoke election terms such as ``integrity,'' ``security,'' and ``fraud.'' Using diachronic word embeddings, which track semantic change through how words are used in context, we measure how differently each party uses each term, how much each party shifts, and whether they share nearest semantic neighbors. We show that members of Congress do not need different words to tell different stories about elections. They need only place those same words in different company. Across nearly every term and year, the two parties surround election-integrity vocabulary with entirely different words. That divergence is easy to miss, because most election vocabulary is no more divergent than other words used at roughly the same frequency, and neither party's usage shifted more than the other's. Only a subset of terms grew more divergent, most notably ``certification,'' while ``rigged'' and ``stolen'' entered election discourse after 2020 and polarized there. By 2024, Democrats surround ``voter,'' ``election,'' and ``integrity'' with the language of access and administration. Republicans surround the same terms with ``citizenship verification,'' ``noncitizen voting,'' and ``border security.'' For one party, integrity means protecting eligible voters' ability to cast a ballot. For the other, it means protecting the electoral process from illegitimate ballots. Election officials, who must administer a single system under both definitions, inherit this tension.

Abstract: Election integrity is a shared commitment in American politics, but Democrats and Republicans in Congress increasingly mean different things by it. Analyzing 10,420 congressional e-newsletters sent from 2010 to 2025, we examine how the two parties invoke election terms such as ``integrity,'' ``security,'' and ``fraud.'' We show that members of Congress do not need different words to tell different stories about elections. They need only place those same words in different company. ### [17] [Beyond IceBERT: Open-Data ModernBERT Encoders for Icelandic from 12M to 1B Parameters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36230)
*Hafsteinn Einarsson*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: IceBERT, the reference encoder for Icelandic, found that a cleaned web crawl is enough to train a strong model and that starting from a multilingual model can help on some tasks. We revisit both findings with the ModernBERT architecture. We train Icelandic encoders from 12M to 1B parameters on 9B tokens of open data, and rerun IceBERT's benchmarks and five newer tasks for 30 encoders under one protocol with confidence intervals. Our 1B model trained from scratch, to our knowledge the first monolingual Icelandic encoder of that size, is significantly better than IceBERT on all eleven tasks; warm-started from the English Ettin encoder of the same shape, it has the best score of all encoders on every task we rank. Because our model shapes match the English Ettin encoders and the multilingual mmBERT, we can also test the warm start under controlled conditions, at six model sizes and four token budgets. With our vocabulary transplanted, a warm start was never significantly worse than scratch training on the same Icelandic text, and from base size up it was not significantly worse on four tasks than scratch training on 4 times the text (8 times at base and 1B). As models grow, most of the transfer comes from the source model's transformer layers, so even an English source helps. Keeping the source vocabulary instead cost 5 F1 on question answering and nearly three times the compute.

### [18] [Detect Before You Disambiguate: Perturbation-Based Input Ambiguity Detection in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36353)
*Tiejin Chen,Xiaoou Liu,Michael Clifford,Ahmadreza Moradipari,Yitao Chen,Kyungtae Han,Nejib Ammar,Hua Wei*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) often answer ambiguous inputs as if they had a single intended meaning. This is problematic because input ambiguity is an upstream source of uncertainty: when a prompt admits multiple valid interpretations, the key question is whether the model should answer directly at all. Existing input uncertainty methods often rely on LLM-generated statements or clarifications, but such transformations may already disambiguate the input before the ambiguity is measured. We propose a label-preserving perturbation framework for input ambiguity detection in which perturbations remain close to the original input while preserving its label. We instantiate this principle with two detectors: a black-box rule-based perturbation library and a white-box importance-guided method using model-internal signals. Experiments across four datasets in open-domain, conversational, and visual QA show that our methods outperform output-side uncertainty baselines and LLM-paraphrase-based perturbation baselines. Our results highlight the importance of detecting ambiguity before attempting to disambiguate it. Our code is available \href{ this https URL }{\textcolor{purple}{here}}.

### [19] [AK_QMUL at ArGuard Shared Tasks: A Single Fine-Tuned JAIS for Arabic Harmful-Prompt Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36360)
*Ali Khairallah,Arkaitz Zubiaga*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We present AK_QMUL's submissions to the ArGuard-2026 shared tasks on Arabic harmful-prompt detection: a binary safe/unsafe task (B1) and a seven-way harm-domain task (B2). Both submissions use one backbone -- JAIS-6.7B fine-tuned with 4-bit QLoRA and a linear classification head over its last-token representation. For B1 we train a four-way head that factors the label by dialect register {safe, unsafe} x {MSA, other}, we augment the training fold with MSA prompts from AraSafe, and decode with a plain argmax to score safe/unsafe. For B2 we fine-tune the same backbone as a seven-way classifier and average the softmax outputs of five random seeds. Both submissions ranked first on their track, with macro-F1 0.984 on B1 and 0.790 on B2. We report results by dialect and by class: on B1 the model is accurate across all six dialects (93.6--99.8%) and its predicted unsafe rate tracks the true rate closely; on B2 six of the seven classes reach F1 between 0.73 and 0.98, with the residual error concentrated in the Bully class, which overlaps semantically with harassment and harm-to-others.

### [20] [No Tokenizer, Still a Gap: Cross-Lingual Fairness of Homoglyph and Invisible-Character Watermarking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36432)
*Alexander Nemecek,Yuqiao Xu,Joseph Falkenburg,Erman Ayday*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Homoglyph and invisible-character watermarks are edit-based watermarks. Instead of changing how a model generates text, they hide a signal in the text after it is written. They swap some characters for homoglyphs, which look the same, or very similar, but have different Unicode code points, or they insert characters that do not display, all without access to the model that wrote the text. Generation-time watermarks work less well for lower-resourced languages due to how tokenizers split their text. Because they work on individual characters, these watermarks never touch a tokenizer, so we ask whether they escape this gap. Across 40 language varieties in 24 scripts, we measure capacity (the hidden bits each character can carry), how much of it survives routine handling and targeted removal, and how much text a keyed detector needs. Capacity varies 3.3-fold and script accounts for 96\% of that variation. Within Latin script, resource level makes no detectable difference ($\rho=+0.095$, $p=0.78$), but across scripts capacity rises with it ($\rho=+0.54$, 95\% CI $[+0.14,+0.83]$), because lower-resourced languages tend to use scripts with few homoglyphs. Ordinary copy-paste, which strips invisible characters, widens the gap: a detector then needs about 2 code points of English or Persian but 93 of Lao. Removing the tokenizer does not remove the inequity, but instead only changes its source.

### [21] [CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36437)
*Jixuan Leng,Si Si,Fei Wang,Cho-Jui Hsieh,Jiong Zhang,Hsiang-Fu Yu,Inderjit S. Dhillon*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: When a Large Language Model (LLM) is trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) on multiple tasks, a task's primary reward can gate auxiliary rewards such as a length reward: on a failing response, an auxiliary cannot exceed the primary. However, group-relative advantage estimators treat a gated auxiliary like any other component, so it can reverse the primary's order, and at the primary's ceiling only auxiliaries order responses. Keeping gated auxiliaries hurts some tasks, while dropping them hurts others. We propose CONCUR, an advantage estimator that replaces the standardized scores of each gated auxiliary with the closest scores that satisfy two conditions: responses with higher primary rewards cannot receive lower scores, and responses at the primary's ceiling receive equal scores. CONCUR-T applies both conditions throughout training, and CONCUR-A lifts the second for an auxiliary that agrees with the primary's order more often than it reverses it among passing responses. On three models from two families and across math, code, instruction following, and writing, both variants score higher on average than all baselines and than when all the gated auxiliaries are dropped.

### [22] [Benchmarking Task Takeover Across Agent Handoffs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36523)
*Wenyuan Li,Guang Li,Dongyuan Li,Keisuke Maeda,Takahiro Ogawa,Miki Haseyama*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: As agents collaborate on longer tasks, responsibility may pass between models before the work is complete. The receiving model must build on prior decisions, observations, and actions while addressing the remaining requirements. Evaluating this transition requires connecting the information preserved at handoff to how the receiver continues the work, a relationship that task-success and memory-retention scores alone do not capture. We introduce the Handoff State Continuity Benchmark (HSC-Bench), comprising 1,039 tasks that evaluate two complementary aspects of task takeover: recovering relevant repository evidence and continuing from established conversational, tool, and file-work state. Comparisons across six receiving models show that structured handoff state improves repository evidence recovery for every model and continuation performance for most models. The strongest receivers differ between the two tracks, showing that evidence-recovery rankings alone do not characterize performance when continuing from inherited state. By combining these comparisons with checks of subsequent responses and actions, HSC-Bench evaluates both access to prior evidence and adherence to established commitments and completed work. This provides a basis for selecting receiving models and assessing handoff representations according to the work that must be carried forward.

### [23] [ETC-Bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluation-Side Transcript Canonicalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36527)
*Zhiheng Qian,Junhao Du,Jing Peng,Hanqi Li,Kunyang Peng,Feng Xue,Kai Yu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Written transcripts of the same speech can differ in ways that are not uniquely determined by the speech signal. We formulate evaluation-side transcript canonicalization (ETC), which maps multiple surface forms to a single canonical form when their differences are not determined by speech. To our knowledge, ETC-Bench is the first and most comprehensive multilingual benchmark for evaluation-side transcript canonicalization, covering 181 phenomenon types across 12 languages. Each instance is a minimal pair that shares a sentence context and differs only in a target span exhibiting one phenomenon. To evaluate both canonicalization success and semantic preservation, we propose Semantic-preserving Exact-match Normalization Accuracy (SENA), which combines exact agreement between independently canonicalized pair members with a pair-relative BERTScore constraint against information loss. We further introduce the Taxonomy-guided Agent Canonicalization Skill (TACS), which provides LLM agents with phenomenon descriptions and explicit canonicalization contracts. Experiments with five baseline configurations and three TACS-based agents show that the agents outperform the baseline systems on shared languages. ETC-Bench provides a systematic testbed for evaluation-side transcript canonicalization across languages.

### [24] [Agentic Data Sampling Framework for Multilingual ASR via Linguistic-Aware Error-Driven Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36538)
*Zhiheng Qian,Junhao Du,Jing Peng,Hanqi Li,Kunyang Peng,Feng Xue,Lu Chen,Shuai Wang,Kai Yu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) has achieved rapid progress with large-scale pretrained models and multilingual speech corpora. Previous studies have proved the pivotal role of data sampling in multilingual ASR performance. However, existing sampling strategies largely rely on time-consuming manual, heuristic-based designs. To address this, we propose a linguistic-aware agentic data sampling framework that introduces a data sampling LLM agent into the multilingual ASR training loop. The agent is driven by a linguistically grounded rubric that analyzes ASR errors from phonological, morphological, and syntactic perspectives, and uses the resulting feedback together with training statistics, budget constraints, and algorithm profiles to select domain-level, sample-level, and token-level sampling strategies. This design turns evaluation results into adaptive data-selection decisions rather than treating WER/CER as final endpoints only. We conduct experiments on twelve Common Voice languages using Whisper-medium as the ASR backbone. The results show that our method achieves performance better than full-data training while using less training data and lower computational resources, and substantially accelerates training convergence compared to conventional sampling strategies.

### [25] [Structured Maps for Landmark-Based Route Instructions with LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36582)
*Mifu Matsumoto,Yuki Nakanishi,Tomoya Hashiguchi,Hiroaki Ohshima*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: To generate landmark-based route instructions, models must understand both map geometry and human landmark preferences. Although large language models (LLMs) show great abilities in language tasks, the best way to structure map data for these models is not yet established. This paper proposes a structured text representation for landmark selection tasks in route navigation, utilizing SVG format to encode spatial features. The structured text maintains a geometric connection with rendered map images, allowing language models to directly access spatial and semantic data. Using a new dataset created from human-written route descriptions and OpenStreetMap data, we evaluate models on two tasks: landmark selection at turns and around destinations. Experiments with five LLMs show that the proposed structured text input performs as well as or better than image-based PNG inputs. In addition, task-specific fine-tuning enables smaller local LLMs to effectively leverage map layouts to achieve high selection accuracy. These results demonstrate that structured text is an efficient and lightweight interface for spatial reasoning in human-oriented navigation.

### [26] [Japanese Discourse Structure Analysis Based on Segmented Discourse Representation Theory Using LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36667)
*Satomu Tomisaki,Yosuke Mikami,Amane Watahiki,Hitomi Yanaka*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Discourse parsing based on Segmented Discourse Representation Theory (SDRT) is crucial for capturing the structural dynamics of dialogues. However, most prior research focuses on English, and its effectiveness for Japanese remains unclear owing to the lack of Japanese SDRT corpora. To address this issue, we construct Japanese SDRT corpora by translating existing English SDRT corpora using an LLM. Through a comparative evaluation of prompt-based and fine-tuned LLMs, we show that the models achieve comparable performance between English and Japanese, suggesting the cross-lingual applicability of SDRT-based discourse parsing. In order to investigate why the English and Japanese parsers achieve similar performance, we conduct ablation analyses on discourse markers and contextual inputs. Our results reveal that most of the Japanese discourse markers we examined have little impact, and the models' predictions depend heavily on contextual discourse relations rather than on the content of the context clauses. This structural reliance might explain the comparable performance despite the substantial typological differences between English and Japanese.

### [27] [Is Token Confidence Just Chain Length? A Signal-Processing Audit of Reasoning Traces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36709)
*Pragna Mallappa*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reasoning language models answer math problems by writing long chains of thought, and sampling many chains per problem and taking a majority vote raises accuracy at a large cost in generated text. A popular way to cut that cost scores each chain by the model's confidence in each token it writes, where a token is a word or part of a word. The method averages this confidence over a sliding window of 2048 tokens and keeps or stops chains based on the lowest average. We treat the confidence, recorded token by token, as a signal in the sense of audio or radio, and examine the method with standard signal-processing tools such as spectral analysis and statistical tests for detecting a sudden change. We sampled 16 chains for each of 500 problems from two math benchmarks with a small open reasoning model. The windowed-minimum score turns out to measure mostly how long a chain is. Ranking chains by length alone does as well as or better than the confidence score, and once length is accounted for the score carries no information about correctness. Signal processing explains why: the minimum of a longer stretch of a slowly drifting signal is lower by chance alone, and the confidence signal drifts slowly enough that this effect dominates. The spectrum does hold a small signal that length does not explain, since incorrect chains carry more rapid token-to-token fluctuation, but it is too weak to improve the vote. For stopping chains early, neither the sliding average nor a classical change detector beats the simpler choice of sampling fewer chains.

We treat the confidence, recorded token by token, as a signal in the sense of audio or radio, and examine the method with standard signal-processing tools such as spectral analysis and statistical tests for detecting a sudden change. We sampled 16 chains for each of 500 problems from two math benchmarks with a small open reasoning model. The windowed-minimum score turns out to measure mostly how long a chain is. Ranking chains by length alone does as well as or better than the confidence score, and once length is accounted for the score carries no information about correctness. Signal processing explains why: the minimum of a longer stretch of a slowly drifting signal is lower by chance alone, and the confidence signal drifts slowly enough that this effect dominates. The spectrum does hold a small signal that length does not explain, since incorrect chains carry more rapid token-to-token fluctuation, but it is too weak to improve the vote. For stopping chains early, neither the sliding average nor a classical change detector beats the simpler choice of sampling fewer chains.

</details>


### [28] [A Harness Reducing over-Defensive Writing in Agents by Isolating Objections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36717)
*Xiaochen Chang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: When expanding a report, writing with agents may introduce a stronger claim than the article makes and then disclaim it. This is called over-defensive writing. We assume that this is because the agent is writing for responding to an adversarial AI reviewer, instead of a human reader. The defensive context may also influnce the consequent when we simply ban defensive writing in the output through prompts. In order to reduce over-defensive writing, we produce a harness that separates the reviewer, filter, and writer. The writer agent receives only the problems choosen by the filter, which is an independent context. We evaluate this harness on 25 business-project drafts expanded into formal reports, the result shows that the defensive propositions decreased from 59 to 2, which is a 96.61\% reduction, no unsupported factual additions were identified while the source-claim retention rises from 80.35% to 93.12%.

### [29] [CAMR: Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay for Continual Learning in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36734)
*Jingpu Yang,Tianhao Li,Fengxian Ji,Yufeng Wang,Shuxin Zheng,Xiaoqing Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Continual learning requires large language models to acquire new knowledge and capabilities while retaining what they have learned. Fine-tuning and replay support acquisition and retention, but deciding whether incoming examples need supervision and which historical examples to revisit remains a challenge. We propose Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay (CAMR), an adaptive framework that jointly controls current-example supervision and historical replay. CAMR combines compatibility checks with a learned memory gate to guide an online policy over three actions: learning incoming examples with general replay, jointly reinforcing compatible related examples, and skipping direct supervision of verified mastered duplicates. The policy learns from acquisition, retention, and training-cost feedback under a bounded per-arrival replay budget. We evaluate CAMR with Qwen3-8B-Base on continual factual updating and cross-task and cross-domain learning. On WikiBigEdit, CAMR consistently leads evaluated methods in Original Match from 3K to 100K facts, reaching 93.66% after just 3K facts and surpassing Full-history Replay (LoRA) after 100K facts. It also achieves the highest final scores on all four selected TRACE tasks and maintains or improves earlier-task performance relative to post-acquisition levels in a sequence spanning financial question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and summarization.

### [30] [DocSkill: Skill-Integrated Agentic Reasoning for Multilingual Multi-Hop Document Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36759)
*Jing Huang,Zhiya Tan,Changtao Miao,Shutao Gong,Yang Wang,Joey Tianyi Zhou,Jianshu Li,Ying Yan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multilingual multi-hop document question answering (MMHop-DocQA) requires locating and integrating evidence across complex layouts, document pages, and diverse languages. Existing approaches include single-pass processing and adaptive tool use, but learning to coordinate evidence acquisition, cross-page integration, and answer verification remains challenging. To address this challenge, we present DocSkill, an agentic framework with a learned skill-orchestration policy for adaptive evidence acquisition and reasoning. The policy selects, revisits, or skips skills according to the evolving evidence state. To construct supervision for skill orchestration, bounded Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) explores alternative skill trajectories offline. These trajectories provide demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and preference pairs for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). We further introduce MMHop-DocBench, a multilingual multi-hop document QA dataset with training and test splits, containing 60K QA pairs across 10 languages and eight document domains. Its HopGen pipeline builds hierarchical page-element graphs to derive traceable cross-page evidence paths and generate grounded QA pairs with page- and element-level evidence annotations. Experiments show that DocSkill with Qwen3-VL-8B achieves 41.0 accuracy and 49.2 F1 on MMHop-DocBench, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 5.5 and 6.3 points, respectively, and achieving competitive performance on MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench.

### [31] [Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36797)
*Xiang Ding*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reading "While the man hunted the deer ran into the woods" requires giving up the analysis in which "the deer" is the object of "hunted". People who have just read such a sentence still produce more transitive structures, so the abandoned analysis primes later language. We ask whether language models keep using an analysis they have abandoned, and what in the model carries it. In 24 open models from 124M to 70B parameters, a garden-path sentence leaves two traces in the context. A residue of the abandoned analysis raises later object attachment, by about three quarters of the effect of a sentence in which the noun phrase really is an object, and it appears in sampled text, on held-out and human-normed items and for a second type of garden path. An adaptation toward the resolved structure scales with the sentence's disambiguation error and acts mainly on comprehension-like measures. Activation patching separates the two. Later text reads the residue from the role information in the noun phrase's states, which were computed under the object analysis before the disambiguation, and replacing these states removes almost all of the residue in the 32B and 70B models. The adaptation is read from the states that processed the disambiguation. Overridden statements show the same persistence (a corrected value keeps pulling later predictions in 8 of 9 models), and in most models the pull is carried by the positions after the statement. Finally, the human paradigm transfers only with controls for punctuation, because the models also write garden-path sentences themselves, which reverses the paradigm's raw statistic.

### [32] [Personality Latents: Conditioning Frozen Language Models on Individuals from Their Own Writing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36805)
*Gunhee Cho,Yun-Gyung Cheong*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Controlling the personality of a language model usually relies on written profiles or named trait categories, so it can only express what an author writes down or what a taxonomy names. We instead propose Personality Latents (PL), which learn a latent for each person from their own writing, with no personality labels and no authored profile, and inject it into a frozen language model as a soft prefix. Following generative latent optimization, each training person receives a free latent that is optimized through the frozen model itself, while an encoder learns to predict these latents so that a new person needs only one forward pass, with optional refinement at test time. We evaluate on held-out people by having the conditioned model answer neutral and interview questions and reading personality from its answers with scorers trained on real human writing. On the MBTI axes PL reaches an AUC of , ahead of persona embedding and prompt-based baselines under identical settings, and the ranking holds when the answers are scored in three different embedding spaces. A latent learned with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct also transfers personality to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct through a new adapter alone.

### [33] [Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36811)
*Runze Jiang,Yan Wang,Boran Jin,Bingyu Zhu,Longtao Huang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Knowledge improvement in large language models is shifting from predefined knowledge incorporation pipelines toward evaluation-guided updating. Existing methods use evaluation to localize model-specific knowledge weaknesses and guide targeted post-training. However, identifying what to improve does not necessarily provide sufficient information for deciding how to improve it. The same localized weakness can be compatible with distinct operational knowledge states: the relevant knowledge may be unavailable, available but difficult to access reliably, or accessible but ineffective for downstream use. We call this ambiguity knowledge-state aliasing. When compatible states favor different interventions, greater diagnostic resolution alone is insufficient for intervention selection. Moreover, model updates can change the underlying knowledge state before the observed weakness disappears, such that an intervention appropriate in one round may no longer address the bottleneck in the next. To address these challenges, we propose Recursive Knowledge Improvement (RKI), which formulates knowledge improvement as a sequential, state-aware intervention process. RKI organizes knowledge into graph-structured units that provide a shared basis for diagnostic evaluation and targeted intervention across rounds. At each round, RKI localizes knowledge weaknesses, estimates the model's operational knowledge state from diagnostic evidence and intervention history, selects a corresponding intervention, and re-evaluates the updated model before determining the next intervention. On HotpotEval and SafeInternalEval, RKI outperforms existing knowledge incorporation methods by 18.41 points on average. Further analyses show that knowledge states provide additional guidance for intervention selection beyond weakness localization and can change across model updates even when the observed weakness persists.
