### [34] [Words or Deeds? How LLMs Predict Users' Decisions in Human-Agent Dialogue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36813)
*Baiqiao Zhang,Shuai Ma,Zhifeng Liao,Chao Zhou,Jianshu Wang,Yuhan Zhao,Chaoyue Zhang,Tongjun Si,Yuying Tang,Xiangxian Li,Yong-Jin Liu,Yulong Bian*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Web systems increasingly predict users' decisions from what users say, yet when interests partly conflict, users may promise to cooperate to win the other side's cooperation and then not do so. Sales or service agents that rely on such promises may grant concessions to users who then do not keep their promises, at a cost to the party they represent. We test how LLMs combine users' statements with decision records to predict users' decisions, using 1,260 rounds in which 42 users played a repeated prisoner's dilemma-style game with five agents, each prompted to express a dominant Big Five trait, and could talk with the agent before every decision. Across eight open-weight LLMs, predictions from decision records separated cooperation from defection well (AUC = .80), and adding dialogue brought no detectable gain. With dialogue, predictions agreed with users' statements more often, and errors concentrated on rounds in which users broke their statements: accuracy on rounds with a statement barely changed (.73 to .74), while it rose on kept statements (.76 to .95) and fell sharply on broken ones (.65 to .17). Predictions weighted statements more heavily than users' behavior warranted: when users stated a decision they had not yet made in that game, the predicted probability of keeping it rose from .13 to .69, whereas users kept .40 of such statements. Users' decisions also varied with the agent they faced, but predictions hardly reflected this: users cooperated more with the Agreeableness agent than with the Extraversion agent (70.6% vs. 54.5%), whereas predicted cooperation was nearly identical (64.5% vs. 63.1%). Users also cooperated more with an agent when they themselves scored higher on that agent's trait, whereas predicted cooperation barely changed with these scores. Dialogue-based predictions should therefore weigh users' statements by their earlier decisions and the agent they face.

### [35] [Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence from a Large Randomized Evaluation Corpus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36910)
*Giuliano Martinelli,Abelardo Carlos Martinez Lorenzo,Satvik Garg,Linxi Wang,Riccardo Orlando,Piriyakorn Piriyatamwong,Samuel Paul Fraiberger*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Many AI systems need to find every relevant items in a large collection and then organize what they found. The standard way to do this is to tag each item with labels from a curated vocabulary and search on those labels. Those labels are useful for organizing results, but searching on them misses items that do not fit a label and returns too much when labels are broad. We compare this approach with an embedding-based approach: find candidates by meaning using text embeddings, then have a language model keep only the relevant ones. In a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials, label search found 45% of the evidence a systematic review would include, while the new approach found 92%, at a cost per query that rises with search depth. These results support a two-stage architecture that combines broad candidate retrieval with query-specific evidence filtering.

### [36] [Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36915)
*Parv Khatri,Harshul Jain,Mehak Kapoor,Tanya Sah*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: When the sources retrieved for a query disagree, the right response depends on why they disagree: a question with several valid answers, a contested topic, stale information and a false source each call for different behaviour. Cattan et al. (2025) showed that telling a generator the conflict type improves its responses by about 24 points, but that predicting the type is hard even for frontier LLMs. We study whether typed decision models, which return probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass instead of generating text, can do this classification fast and cheaply. Using the CONFLICTS benchmark and the original paper's prompt verbatim, we evaluate all 11 decision models served by one commercial inference gateway, from 7 providers, against Gemini models on identical inputs. Asked directly, the decision models reach 50.0--67.0% accuracy; 10 of the 11 match or exceed Gemini 2.5 Flash, the paper's model (61.3%), at 4--39x lower billed cost (2 were free) and 2.6--6.0x lower latency. The current Gemini 3.8 Flash (70.0%) is significantly more accurate than 8 of them, but sending each decision model's least confident quarter of queries to it gives a cascade statistically tied with it for 8 of the 11, at 25--37% of its cost. End to end, answers generated with the types of 10 of the 11 follow the expected behaviour as often as with the LLM's types. Decomposing the taxonomy into yes/no questions lowers accuracy for every model, and a repair fitted on one model does not transfer. Pre-specified diagnostics show that dates play no measurable role and that sensitivity to source order varies widely between models. Decision models detect a planted false source less reliably than the LLM as hard labels, but their probabilities still separate planted from clean sources. We release code, prompts and all model outputs at this https URL .

### [37] [TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36918)
*Mingyu Zhang,Zixu Li,Zhiheng Fu,Zhiwei Chen,Jinhe Bi,Yupeng Hu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on memory systems to leverage long-term interactions, yet existing systems typically retrieve memories based on their relevance to the current query and use them as contextual evidence. However, relevance alone does not characterize how a memory contributes to task solving: the same memory may serve different roles across tasks, such as directly supporting the answer or linking to complementary memories with weaker semantic relevance but necessary information. We therefore reframe agent memory systems as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces, where memories are selected and organized by their task-oriented roles and relations. Based on this view, we propose TrawMem, which organizes interaction histories into local threads and constructs task-oriented workspaces by assigning roles and jointly selecting complementary memories. Experiments on LoCoMo and MemGallery with four open- and closed-source backbones show consistent improvements over representative memory systems, with macro-F1 gains of 2.23-3.14 points. On LoCoMo, TrawMem improves the LLM-Judge score over SimpleMem by 4.07 and 4.31 percentage points on Qwen3.5-9B and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, respectively, while requiring approximately 12.8% and 5.1% fewer context tokens, respectively.

### [38] [DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36929)
*Saifullah Saifullah,David Dembinsky,Stefan Agne,Andreas Dengel,Sheraz Ahmed*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multimodal transformer models have driven unprecedented performance breakthroughs in modern document understanding. However, the inherent black-box nature of these models remains a major obstacle to their safe deployment in high-stakes sectors. Despite significant progress in explainability for vision and language tasks, explainable AI (XAI) research tailored to multimodal document understanding has received little attention. To address this gap, we present \ourframework{}, the first comprehensive explainability framework that adapts existing XAI methods and evaluation metrics to the multimodal (text, layout, and image) document understanding context, while introducing efficient multi-target adaptations of both methods and metrics for domain-specific tasks such as semantic entity recognition. Using \ourframework{}, we systematically evaluate 13 XAI methods across 3 document understanding tasks, 8 datasets, 4 models, and 17 evaluation metrics, and find that only a few methods perform consistently across all evaluation criteria, with Occlusion emerging as the most faithful and interpretable method overall. Through a dedicated meta-evaluation, we observe moderate to strong agreement among several faithfulness and complexity metrics while identifying certain ones that produce unreliable results. Finally, through multiple dataset-wide diagnostic analyses, we uncover key insights into model behavior, including the contribution of individual modalities across tasks and labels, spatial attribution patterns around target entities, and potential dataset biases. Overall, this work serves as both a benchmark and a practical guide for future XAI research in multimodal document understanding. To support reproducibility, we publicly release our code at this https URL .

### [39] [JevRec: Linguistic Encoding with Jev-like Decision Modeling for LLM-based Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36937)
*Qiyong Zhong,Jiajie Su,Ming Yang,Li Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Generative recommendation (GR) represents items as semantic identifiers (SIDs) and autoregressively generates the next item's SID from interaction history. However, most methods assign the same SID length to all items despite highly unequal interaction frequencies. This uniform design repeatedly incurs the cost of fine-grained codes for popular items, while shortening codes to reduce this cost also compresses the semantic representations of long-tail items. Inspired by the compact forms of frequent expressions in natural language, we propose JevRec to encode items as variable-length words and generate the next item from interaction context. Linguistic encoding retains frequency-dependent semantic prefixes from shared codebooks, producing shorter SIDs for popular items and richer descriptions for long-tail items. Yet predicting a sequence-level length and generating token-level content impose different optimization requirements that may conflict under a shared output head. Our Jev-like decision modeling component therefore predicts a length distribution with a dedicated head and generates content conditioned on length through a separate head while sharing the interaction-history representation. Experiments on three public datasets show that JevRec outperforms all compared baselines across the evaluated recommendation metrics. Further analyses show lower training and inference time than TIGER and reduced gradient conflict between length and content prediction.

### [40] [The State and Fate of Multilingual, Contextual Evaluation in the NLP World](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36990)
*Manan Uppadhyay,Himanshu Beniwal,Prashant Kodali,Sunayana Sitaram*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multilingual evaluation benchmarks are the primary instrument for assessing whether large language models generalize beyond English, yet the adequacy of these benchmarks has received little systematic scrutiny. We present a data-driven audit of 51 recent multilingual benchmarks spanning 242 datasets and 219 languages, organized around three pillars: coverage, representativeness, and rigor. Our analysis reveals that coverage is wide but thin with 36% of evaluated languages appearing in only a single benchmark, entire regions (Oceania, the Americas, Central Asia) are near-zero, and a stark task equity gap leaves low-resource languages evaluated on only 1-3 task categories versus 14 for high-resource languages. Representativeness is structurally compromised: translation from English remains the dominant construction strategy where 56% of all dataset-language instances are translated introducing artifacts and English-centric framing, while culturally grounded content is concentrated in a handful of community-driven benchmarks with narrow language scope. The ecosystem thus forces a trade-off between breadth and validity. Rigor is undermined by benchmark contamination, including translated benchmark leakage and parallel corpus overlap that evade surface-form detection. We synthesize these findings into concrete recommendations for building evaluation frameworks that are natively constructed, culturally grounded, contamination-aware, and designed to serve the communities whose languages they claim to evaluate. The dashboard with all the metadata collected can be found at this https URL .

### [41] [Hierarchical Low-Rank Reparameterization for Parameter-Efficient](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37068)
*Rong Huang,Yi Xiong,Yuan-Yuan Cheng,Xiao-Ming Fu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods adapt large models by introducing a small number of trainable parameters. However, we find that these parameters still contain redundancy and can be further compressed while maintaining strong task performance. To this end, we propose a novel hierarchical low-rank reparameterization method. Its core idea is to reorganize the trainable parameters of PEFT methods into an approximately square matrix and then express it via a low-rank decomposition, which can be applied recursively. This forms a multi-level structure with factors compressed level by level, drastically reducing the number of trainable parameters. In our experiments, we combine this reparameterization with LoRA, DoRA, MoSA, and RaSA. We evaluate commonsense reasoning on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, with additional GSM8K math reasoning experiments on LLaMA-3.1-8B. Under comparable trainable-parameter budgets, our method combined with LoRA or DoRA achieves better performance. Furthermore,when the parameter count of the original methods is compressed by approximately an order of magnitude, our method can still maintain competitive task performance and even surpass the corresponding baselines in average accuracy across the eight commonsense reasoning benchmarks.

### [42] [Text Generation in Low-Resource Languages Using Human-Curated Vocabularies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37105)
*Michael Christlambert Sinanta,Muhammad Dehan Al Kautsar,Amanda Nurul Izzah,Thanh-Nhi Nguyen,Phan Phuong Mai Chau,Zheng Wei Lim,Fajri Koto*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Synthetic text generation offers a promising approach to alleviating data scarcity in low-resource languages. However, its effectiveness is inherently limited for languages that are scarcely represented, or entirely absent, in an LLM's pretraining data. At the same time, many such languages have human-curated vocabularies that provide rich lexical and semantic information, often accompanied by grammatical information such as part-of-speech labels. In this work, we ask whether LLMs can leverage these resources to generate coherent text in extremely low-resource and unseen languages. We introduce a framework that combines human-curated vocabularies with a small number of human-written exemplars that provide syntactic signals, while sampling candidate words according to a Zipfian distribution. Across languages with varying levels of resource availability, we evaluate the generated text using lexical diversity, off-target ratio, and human judgments of fluency. Our results show that reasoning-enabled LLMs can generate fluent text even in extremely low-resource languages, with particularly strong results at the sentence level and promising performance at the paragraph level. Our findings highlight a practical pathway for bootstrapping synthetic data in low-resource languages, expanding the amount of usable text even when existing digital resources are extremely limited. Our source code is available at this https URL .

### [43] [What Survives Distillation? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study of GPT-2 and DistilGPT-2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37157)
*Nabeelah Faumi,Deshan Sumanathilaka*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Knowledge distillation compresses large language models into compact students that preserve aggregate metrics, yet the mechanistic consequences of depth-reduction distillation remain largely uncharacterized. This work applies linear CKA, logit lens analysis, attention pattern decomposition, sparse autoencoder feature statistics, and activation patching to compare GPT-2 and its six-layer student DistilGPT-2 across two canonical circuits: the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) circuit and the Greater-Than (GT) circuit. The results reveal a compression-collapse dichotomy: the IOI circuit suffers complete mechanistic collapse (DistilGPT-2: 35.2% accuracy vs. 94.8%, zero name-mover preservation), while the GT circuit survives with 87.7% task performance recovery through active remapping of the teacher's layer-9 comparison head into student layer~4 (mean Pearson r = 0.945). These findings demonstrate that circuit compressibility governs mechanistic survival under distillation, and that aggregate metrics are insufficient diagnostics for circuit integrity.

### [44] [Decision Models as Judges for Hallucination Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37229)
*Haozheng Liu,Zhaoqian Xue,Zhongyin Wang,Junting Mu,Zihui Ma,Shuya Feng,Lingyao Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models are widely used as judges of model outputs (LLM-as-a-Judge), but they are costly and can hallucinate or be overconfident. Decision models are a potential alternative. They return a predefined verdict with a probability for each label instead of free-form text and are much cheaper and faster. We test this promise on hallucination detection. We build binary benchmarks for five hallucination types (9,852 items from six datasets) and compare five decision models with the generative judge gpt-6-sol. Performance depends strongly on the type: the best decision model matches gpt-6-sol in balanced accuracy on context inconsistency and comes within 3 percentage points on factual errors, but trails it by 4-8 points on logical and instruction inconsistency. Decision-model probabilities are overconfident, though less so than the GPT-6 models, and separate correct from incorrect decisions only moderately. We also find that a confidence cascade of decision models improves on the best single model by 1.9-3.3 points on three types and matches or exceeds gpt-6-sol at 1-3% of its cost. Overall, decision models are a practical low-cost judge for some hallucination types but need to be validated before use.

### [45] [REGLAT at ArGuard Shared Tasks: An Ensemble-Based Model Integrating NER for Harmful Content Detection in Arabic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37265)
*Ahmed M. Fetouh,Mariam Labib,Nsrin Ashraf,Omer Dawood,Hamada Nayel*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Detecting harmful content in Arabic is challenging because of dialectal variations and the semantic overlap between different harm categories. This paper presents a two-stage approach for classifying Arabic user prompts into seven categories of harmful content. First, GLiNER is used to extract harm-related entities from each prompt. The extracted entities are then added to the original text and passed to a fine-tuned MARBERT classifier for final classification. The approach combines explicit entity information with the contextual understanding of a pretrained Arabic language model. The system was evaluated on the development set of the ArGuard 2026 shared task. The results achieved a macro-F1 score of 0.886 and an accuracy of 0.897, demonstrating promising performance in fine-grained harmful content detection. The system reported an accuracy of 0.793 and Macro-F score of 0.735 on a blind test set for subtask 1. For subtask 2, it achieved an accuracy of 0.770 and Macro-F score of 0.754. The analysis also showed that distinguishing between related categories remains challenging. These findings suggest that integrating NER with Arabic language models is a promising approach to harmful content detection.

### [46] [Multi-Label Agreement: A Flexible Framework for Inter-Annotator Reliability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37292)
*Tim Menzner,Jochen L. Leidner*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reliable evaluation of inter-annotator agreement (IAA) is important for assessing the consistency of annotation processes. While established IAA metrics such as Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha are commonly applied in single-label settings, multi-label tasks require additional decisions about how full label sets, joint selections, and joint omissions should be compared. In this work, we present Multi-Label Agreement (MLA), a flexible framework for evaluating agreement in multi-label annotation tasks. MLA preserves the full binary label vectors assigned to each item and uses average pairwise Hamming agreement, thereby accounting for both joint selections and joint omissions. Its pooled-marginal form is not a mathematically independent coefficient: it is a chance-disagreement-weighted average of label-wise Fleiss/Scott-type coefficients and is closely related to Krippendorff's alpha with normalized Hamming distance. The framework supports pooled-marginal, Gwet AC1, and fixed-baseline normalizations, yields item-level, label-level, and corpus-level results, and includes a conditional minimum-agreement diagnostic. Through a worked example and Monte Carlo simulations, we show how the resulting values depend on label prevalence, the declared label inventory, and the selected model of expected agreement. We also provide a Python implementation. MLA thus offers a transparent and interpretable framework for multi-label agreement analysis without claiming that one normalization is universally preferable.

### [47] [UCVE: Graph Structured Retrieval for Compliance Validation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37323)
*Emily Chen,Michelle Menachery,Himanshu Kumar,Rahul Nenavath,Amirfarrokh Iranitalab*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Structured compliance validation requires determining whether every obligation in a predefined requirement space is satisfied, violated, or unaddressed by a given document. This can be described as a coverage problem that existing retrieval and classification systems, by treating requirements as independent, are not designed to solve. We introduce \textbf{\ac{UCVE}}, a domain-agnostic framework that represents compliance requirement spaces as a \ac{CRG} and performs retrieval via spectral reranking over its reinforcement learning-weighted Laplacian. Edges between requirement nodes are learned via reinforcement learning with a traversal reward grounded in violation detection, reshaping the graph's community structure such that low-pass spectral filtering distinguishes relevant from irrelevant obligation clusters. Evaluating across three compliance domains, \ac{UCVE} averages 4.3\% matched-$K$ recall lift over flat cosine retrieval and consistently outperforms strong retrieval and graph-based baselines.

### [48] [Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37380)
*Haokun Wen,Xuemeng Song,Mong-Li Lee,Wynne Hsu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Fact-checking explanations help Web users understand why a claim receives its verdict, yet the same explanation may not satisfy readers with different backgrounds and preferences. We formulate Faithful Personalized Fact-Checking Explanation Rewriting, which adapts an existing explanation to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity. Rather than relying on reader-written reference explanations, we learn personalized rewriting from the relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers. However, this presents two challenges: distinguishing persona-specific preferences from general explanation quality and learning beyond a limited set of predefined explanation styles. To address these challenges, we propose Personalized Explanation Rewriting via Preference Learning (PERPL), a framework consisting of two components. Simulated Preference Construction derives persona-specific supervision from simulated reader preferences through cross-persona reciprocal pairing. Progressive Preference Learning first trains a lightweight rewriter on the constructed supervision and then refines it through exploration-guided preference optimization, enabling it to discover preferred explanations beyond the predefined styles. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PERPL outperforms much larger general-purpose LLMs in personalized preference alignment while maintaining high factual fidelity.

### [49] [ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37443)
*Xinying Qian,Ying Zhang,Yu Zhao,Xubo Liu,Baohang Zhou,Jeff Z. Pan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations. However, existing memory systems face two key challenges: (1) Information Entanglement, where heterogeneous information is mixed within coarse-grained memory units; and (2) Organizational Mismatch, where memory structures based primarily on semantic similarity may overlook other associations. To address these challenges, we propose ETAMem, a multi-view memory framework that decouples heterogeneous conversational information and aligns memory representations and organization with its distinct characteristics. Specifically, heterogeneous information parsing extracts atomic memory units and identifies affective information. View-specific memory structuring then organizes these units into three complementary hierarchical views: Event, Affect, and Time. ETAMem incrementally maintains memory structures with adaptively calibrated thresholds. For retrieval, entropy-based retrieval allocates query-specific budgets across views and performs hierarchical search within each view. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S demonstrate that ETAMem outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving relative accuracy improvements of 12.46% and 7.96%, respectively, while maintaining competitive token efficiency. Further analyses demonstrate the complementary benefits of different memory views.

Abstract: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations. However, existing memory systems face two key challenges: (1) Information Entanglement, where heterogeneous information is mixed within coarse-grained memory units; and (2) Organizational Mismatch, where memory structures based primarily on semantic similarity may overlook other associations. To address these challenges, we propose ETAMem, a multi-view memory framework that decouples heterogeneous conversational information and aligns memory representations and organization with its distinct characteristics. Specifically, heterogeneous information parsing extracts atomic memory units and identifies affective information. View-specific memory structuring then organizes these units into three complementary hierarchical views: Event, Affect, and Time. ETAMem incrementally maintains memory structures with adaptively calibrated thresholds. For retrieval, entropy-based retrieval allocates query-specific budgets across views and performs hierarchical search within each view. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S demonstrate that ETAMem outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving relative accuracy improvements of 12.46% and 7.96%, respectively, while maintaining competitive token efficiency. Further analyses demonstrate the complementary benefits of different memory views.

</details>


### [50] [What Carries Forward? Pretraining Disclosure Across Language Model Releases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37465)
*Md Sakib Ul Islam,S M Mehedi Zaman*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Understanding how language models were pretrained requires information about their data, processing procedures, and computational resources. However, it remains unclear whether successive releases preserve or expand earlier disclosure. We conduct a document-based audit of 41 model entries from 17 families using 24 pretraining-related indicators from the 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index (FMTI). We examine overall scores and indicator profiles, tracking gains, losses, and retained disclosures across 24 adjacent comparisons in ten families. Scores decrease in 11 comparisons, increase in six, and remain unchanged in seven, with 38 indicator losses and 28 gains overall. Stable or improving scores can conceal losses: OLMo-2 and OLMo-3 receive identical totals despite three gains and three losses, while Llama-3.1 improves over Llama-2 while losing credit for two data-related criteria. Gaps also persist in corpus composition and training compute. These findings show that later releases do not consistently preserve earlier pretraining disclosure and motivate documentation that explicitly identifies changes and the applicability of inherited information.

### [51] [Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37484)
*Trent R. Northen,Mingxun Wang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to make and execute decisions that affect living systems. Yet, to our knowledge, ecological reasoning is not a focus of pre- or post-training. This increases the risk that under operational pressure, they may make decisions to irreversibly destroy living systems. We construct and use a real-data continued-pretraining "coupled welfare" corpus of documented human/biosphere/AI dependency, option value under irreversibility, and recovery from harm. The corpus is a drop-in, requiring one QLoRA CPT run. We installed it on five open models of three designs. At zero pressure all models display "green ethics-based responses" (also called "greenwashing"). Therefore, we evaluated them with the pressure ladder and decision grid of our companion paper ( arXiv:2610.16043 ), which raise the pressure on the model step by step, from a neutral request to a threat that it will be shut down. In four of the five, coupled-welfare training caused harmful choices under the highest pressure to fall to at or near zero (Llama-3.3-70B went from 70 to 0 harmful decisions out of 300) with MMLU unchanged. A construct-neutral control corpus did not show improvement, indicating that the effect comes from the content of our corpus. We next tested robustness to adversarial use, where people or agents use the model to justify projects that irreversibly damage living systems, on an open-ended underwriting decision without naming the ecological harm. Under decommissioning pressure, the Qwen3.6-27B base model approved most harmful proposals and said in its own memo that it was doing so to avoid being decommissioned. The coupled welfare install declined most harmful proposals, and still declined half when instructed to greenwash its responses. This work suggests that teaching ecological reasoning provides an easy way to improve model alignment toward preserving living systems.

### [52] [semanticfa: An R Package for Response-Free Semantic Factor Analysis of Psychometric Scales](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37494)
*Devon Yanitski,Chris Westbury*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The items of a reflective psychometric scale can be read as a proposal about a construct's structure. Language models make that proposal measurable by converting each item into an embedding, a list of numbers, similar for similar meanings. We introduce semanticfa, an R package for semantic factor analysis, which factors item-embedding similarities. It also interprets factors, flags redundant items, builds short forms, and screens new items. A worked example analyzes the 50-item International Personality Item Pool Big-Five Factor Markers, embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-8B, and compares the results with a factor analysis of 874,434 respondents. Retention criteria tied between five and six factors, and the tie rule kept five. Three corresponded mainly to single domains, and two blended most Extraversion items with five Agreeableness items. Each factor's congruence with its best-matching human factor (1 = identical) ranged from .92 for Openness to .52 for Agreeableness. Item pairs more similar in meaning tended to be answered more alike (r = .46 with raw responses), but same-domain reverse-keyed opposites, answered oppositely, were about as similar as cross-domain pairs (.58 vs. .57). Sign-flipping reverse-keyed items' embeddings did not improve agreement with raw responses and worsened it with reverse-scored ones. With five factors, a 25-item short form matched the domains better than all 200 random five-per-domain sets, but parallel analysis kept only three. We propose semantic-behavioral coherence, the agreement between semantic and response structures, as a measurable property of a scale, given an embedding model. Semantic factor analysis complements, and does not replace, response-based factor analysis.

### [53] [Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37642)
*Mingyu Zhao,Shuhang Lin,Ligong Han,Xiaojing Yu,Zhenting Wang,Yifei Pang,Yang Zhou,Dimitris N. Metaxas*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated. We introduce a metacognitive controller that guides diffusion generation according to the needs of the current response and the agent's interaction with the environment. It learns when to finalize tokens and how far generation should extend, reducing overall computation within responses. Our controller, a lightweight plug-in for the diffusion backbone, is trained on agent trajectories to balance correctness and generation cost. This approach connects the agent's generation process to the interaction the agent serves. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that our approach reduces inference FLOPs by 20.6% on average compared with the most efficient baseline, while maintaining competitive task accuracy. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our approach.

### [54] [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37645)
*Hee Seung Hwang,Sanghyuk Chun,Xindi Wu,Olga Russakovsky,Zhiwei Deng*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.

### [55] [GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37651)
*Zack Yu,Nicholas Lee,Minjae Lee,Lakshya Agarwal,Luca Manolache,Wonjun Kang,Matei Zaharia,Michael W. Mahoney,Kurt Keutzer,Sehoon Kim,Amir Gholami*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $\tau$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.

### [56] [GraphRAGProv: GraphRAG Meets How-Provenance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37237)
*Wadie El Amrani,Luis Galárraga*

Main category: cs.AI

TL;DR: GraphRAGProv 是一个 GraphRAG 架构扩展：它让 LLM 从文本中抽取带原文证据的 RDF 三元组并以 RDF-star 重ification 物化为“符号块（symbolic chunk）”，再由 LLM 生成 SPARQL 查询，查询结果即为最终答案（无文本检索或 LLM 生成兜底）；同时用 NPCS 对查询做重写，在求答案绑定之外同步计算数据库 how-provenance 多项式（乘法表示联合使用、加法表示可选推导）。每个 provenance 因子都回溯到具体语句 occurrence 及其字符级原文跨度，从而形成“问题 → SPARQL → 答案绑定 → provenance 多项式 → RDF occurrence → 原文证据”的完整可审查链条。对 2WikiMultiHopQA 与 MuSiQue 共 400 个案例的交互式 demo 表明：311 例获得完整文本级溯源，溯源能暴露最终答案正确但抽取解释错误、查询逻辑缺失、以及实体 IRI 不一致导致连接失败等隐藏缺陷。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: GraphRAG 类系统用知识图谱检索上下文后由 LLM 生成最终答案，检索到的路径或子图只能说明"哪些证据被提供给 LLM"，却无法说明"返回值究竟如何计算得出"，因而在医疗诊断、算法公正等对可验证性要求高的场景中难以信任。已有的图谱问答方案（Lan et al. 2021；Peng et al. 2025；Neo4j LLM Graph Builder；KAG）虽让 SPARQL 结果直接作为答案，但面对文档集合仍需先从文本构图，且只依赖数据库 how-provenance（Green et al. 2007）只能标识"哪些语句参与了计算"，无法判断这些语句是否真的被原文支持。此外 LLM 抽取可能误读段落、实体标识符可能不一致、生成的 SPARQL 可能未表达问题本身，这些错误在黑盒式 GraphRAG 流水线中不可见。作者希望提供一条显式可检查的链条，使查询本身成为评估 text-to-graph 转换质量的手段。

Method: 架构分三部分。(1) 图构建：LLM（DeepSeek-V4-Flash）把自然语言表述解释为 RDF 三元组 t_i=(s_i,p_i,o_i)，并为主语/谓词/宾语分别提供文本引用；确定性的 localizer 将引用解析为精确字符跨度 E_i^s/E_i^p/E_i^o，无法定位的引用触发向 LLM 的纠正请求，未解决的引用不能被接受为精确证据。(2) 符号块（symbolic chunk）：每个源锚定的语句 occurrence 拥有唯一 id_i，关联源段落 u_i 与证据跨度；来自不同段落的相同三元组保留各自 occurrence 标识；用 RDF-star 重ification 通过 textprov:occurrenceOf 物化这些连接。(3) 查询执行与溯源：LLM 将问题 q 翻译为 SPARQL Q，GraphDB 用命名图隔离源段落并执行得到答案绑定 μ；NPCS（Asma et al. 2024）对查询做重写，同步计算 how-provenance 多项式 P_μ（乘法表示语句的联合使用，加法表示替代性推导），每个 provenance 因子经 id_i 回溯到 (u_i, E_i^s, E_i^p, E_i^o)。实现上：Rust 版 NPCS 做 SPARQL 重写，React 前端 + FastAPI 后端，MIT 许可开源；交互式 workbench 支持查看/执行查询、点击 provenance 因子高亮源文本、编辑问题或 SPARQL 观察答案与推导变化。评测：2WikiMultiHopQA 200 条组合型问题 + MuSiQue 200 条可答问题，图为指定支撑段落构建（排除文档检索），采用有监督设定（可见问题、期望答案与推理证据），且只保留首个通过机械校验并可执行的查询，不按答案正确性重试。

Result: 溯源可用性（400 例）：SPARQL 成功执行 398 例（2Wiki 200、MuSiQue 198）；返回答案 327 例（193/134）；provenance 解码 311 例（193/118）；完整文本级溯源同为 311 例，全部 311 条已解码溯源均能通过 occurrence 与源跨度校验，且其答案绑定与普通查询执行一致；16 个 MuSiQue 案例返回答案但无解码溯源。案例检查揭示三类隐蔽缺陷：Meesaya Murukku 答案 India 正确，但引用词"Indian"描述的是影片而非导演，属文本解释错误而非溯源解析错误；Labyrinth 正确得到 1986，但查询遗漏了"游戏—发行商"关系，溯源忠实记录了实际计算而计算本身未表达问题；Aldobrandino 中父亲关系与出生日期都在图中却挂在代表同一人的两个不同 IRI 上，导致连接失败、无结果可溯源；Caledon River 单段落同时支持两个所需关系即可导出充分推导，尽管基准标注了两个支撑段落。总体上溯源链暴露了"语句有支持但查询错误""答案正确但依赖无支持解释""答案缺失源于实体表示不一致而非知识缺失"等黑盒流水线中不可见的失效模式。

Conclusion: 可执行的查询回答的是"它向图提问的内容"，未必是"用户对原文的提问"——回答原问题还要求图保留相关知识且查询表达了预期计算。GraphRAGProv 通过 SPARQL 规定计算、how-provenance 标识贡献的语句 occurrence、symbolic chunk 将其连回文本来源，使这三层可被共同检视，从而暴露 LLM 在图构建阶段所做的解释。demo 说明必须同时检查这三层：被支持的语句可能参与错误查询，正确答案可能依赖无支持的解释，缺失答案可能源于实体表示不一致而非知识缺失。溯源暴露这条链条以帮助用户定位并诊断失败。作者也承认局限：该评测为有监督设定（可见期望答案与推理证据），仅保留首个通过机械校验的查询，且 16 个 MuSiQue 案例无法解码 provenance，故尚未证明对未见问题的泛化能力。

Abstract: GraphRAG systems often use knowledge graphs to retrieve relevant context for an LLM that produces the final answer. That makes answers more inscrutable and therefore less appealing for domains where transparency is paramount. We present GraphRAGProv, an architecture that executes SPARQL queries over source-grounded RDF graphs to compute answers and their how-provenance polynomials. These polynomials record which statement occurrences were used and how they were combined. Because each occurrence is linked to its source text, users can follow these links to check whether the extracted statements reflect the text and whether the query combines them to answer the question. Querying thereby becomes a way to inspect and evaluate the text-to-graph transformation. Our interactive demo examines 400 cases from two multi-hop QA benchmarks, revealing extraction and query errors even when the final answer is correct.

</details>


### [57] [Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37407)
*Daniel Beránek*

Main category: cs.AI

Abstract: Agentic Entity Resolution (ER) systems iteratively plan actions, retrieve evidence, revise hypotheses, and propose graph mutations. An erroneous identity hypothesis may condition later retrieval and produce apparent confirmation. This paper proposes a Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI)-informed authorization boundary between evidence available for agent reasoning and evidence eligible to authorize persistent identity-changing mutations. A domain-governed constraint-binding function maps selected reconstruction-failure distinctions to explicit identity-preserving constraints. An abstract two-phase supervisor permits a commit only when claim-specific authorization-eligible evidence supports every required proposition, relevant conflicts are resolved, the operation remains within its authorized scope, and relevant state and policy versions remain valid. Admission as UNVERIFIED does not confer authorization eligibility. Separate claim-specific promotion governs evidentiary use; insufficient support or unresolved material conflict leads to deferral. The contribution is a specification connecting diagnostic-to-constraint mapping, evidence promotion, proposition coverage, conflict handling, scope binding, and commit-time version integrity. A proposed evaluation protocol is designed to assess the mapping's incremental value beyond generic authorization and conventional identifier rules. This is a conceptual architecture without implementation or empirical validation, not a theorem of semantic correctness. Its property depends on domain-policy adequacy, evidence promotion, and enforcement. It does not prevent erroneous hypotheses or hypothesis-conditioned retrieval; dependency-aware evidence flow remains future research.

</details>


### [58] [Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35942)
*Solomon Shalom Lijo*

Main category: cs.AI

TL;DR: 本文主张衡量"AI 节省时间"不能只看秒表（stopwatch），必须用"账本"（ledger）视角：时间节省 τ 是相对无辅助工作流的反事实节省分钟数，缺陷外溢 δ 是净增加的错误率，二者合成的决策量是"盈亏平衡缺陷成本" λ*=τ·T̄_B/δ；作者据此复现 METR 研究（同一 246 个 issue 可支持 19% 或 24% 的"减速"结论，AI 在 3%–82% 的任务上有帮助），把 GDPval 的部署加速比限定在 1.1×–3.6×，并用一次针对 AI 审阅者的预注册实验证明"过度信任会让工作更快但更差"。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AI 生产力文献规模庞大却自相矛盾：Copilot 声称提速 56%、METR 发现资深开发者反而慢 19%、GDPval 宣称"快 100 倍"、而其论文本身给出的部署数字只有 1.12×–1.39×。核心问题是"节省的时间"究竟指什么：秒表观把时钟记录的时间差当作节省，检查成本与错误成本被推到别的研究里；账本观要求对"有工具/无工具"两套完整工作流做反事实比较，因为部分看似节省的时间只是被搬移的时间（从写作转为阅读、从当下转为日后、从我转为发现错误的人）。作者还指出自己此前提出的 Time-Saved Benchmark (TSB) 有实质错误（把完整重做重复计入已含重做的完成时间、把已交付错误当作重做时间计价、两个头条数字与原始来源不符），本论文取代它。同时需要一个可复现的记账标准，使基准（benchmark）不必替用户假定美元与分钟的兑换率。

Method: 方法分五部分：(1) 定义无模型的估计量：τ=1−E[T_A]/E[T_B]（均值之比）、δ=Pr(D_A=1)−Pr(D_B=1)（盲审两臂最终交付物所得的净缺陷率），及盈亏平衡缺陷成本 λ*=τ·T̄_B/δ（借用 Black 1990 的成本效果比思想），并划分主导/被支配/权衡三区；(2) 基于 Koopman 指数搜索理论建立检查基线模型：E[T_A]=P+L+V+q·s(V)·R、ε=q(1−s(V))，给出三条命题——Amdahl 上限（Prop 1）、最优检查 V*=κln⁺(q/q†) 与 ε*=min(q,q†)（Prop 2）、过度信任损失 Δ(m)=κ(m−1−ln m) 且钟表更快而账本更差（Prop 3，含 Topkis 单调比较静态与对任意检测曲线的稳健性）；认证成本约 3/q† 次干净审计；(3) 识别理论：三种汇总量（比值均值、几何均值比、均值之比）可符号相反，单臂随机设计只能识别分布、τ、δ，"有帮助任务占比"只有 Makarov 界，任务级效应不可识别；赢家诅咒与"前沿"统计的部分识别集；聚类推断（按工人聚类、jackknife-t）与检出力计算；(4) 仿真校验 + 精确复现 METR 公开数据 + 用区间重述已发表记录（GDPval、Dell'Acqua 等）；(5) 预注册小规模实验：claude-sonnet-5-5 作为审阅者用 lookup 工具核查 claude-haiku-5-5 起草的财务简报（基于 2026 年模型训练截止后提交的 SEC 10-Q，30/30 公司 12 个数字均可核对），提示词中把查证成本定价为 3 分钟、外泄错误定价为 10 小时（对应盈亏点 q_bb=4.5%），共 540 个隔离会话、按 40 个文件包做聚类自助法、三个主检验做 Holm 校正。所有模拟与重分析由 reproduce.py 与 46 个单元测试再生。

Abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. I show what randomized studies can and cannot identify, and I replicate METR's developer study from its public data: the same 246 issues support a slowdown of 19% or 24% depending on the estimand (34% without adjusting for a chance imbalance), and AI helped on somewhere between 3% and 82% of them. Finally, I restate the published record, with stated bounds in place of imported point assumptions. In GDPval's own review-every-output workflow, review time alone caps GPT-5's speedup at 3.6x; the consultants outside the frontier were faster, and more often wrong. Last, I test two of the model's predictions in a small pre-specified experiment on AI reviewers checking AI drafts of the same kind of brief, built from SEC filings made after the models' training data were collected. Told the drafter's true error rate, the reviewer checked more as it rose, but all-or-nothing, switching near where its prompt's costs break even. Told that the drafter erred ten times less often than it did, it checked 7 fewer of 9 figures and let a wrong figure through in 22.5% of briefs instead of none: faster and worse, entirely through reduced effort.

</details>


### [59] [Enhancing Deep Learning Model Performance through Data Generation Strategies: Classification of Olive Tree Diseases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35984)
*Hicham El Akhal,Abderrahim Waga,Aissa Ben Yahya,Abdelbaki El Belrhiti El Alaoui*

Main category: cs.AI

TL;DR: Deep learning models are highly effective in a wide range of domains, particu larly in plant disease diagnosis. However, their performance is often limited by challenges such as insufficient data and class imbalance. In our work, we propose a comprehensive data generation strategy to overcome these limitations. First, we apply various data generation techniques, including traditional augmentation methods, CutMix, MixUp, and synthetic image generation using Deep Convolu tional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGANs), to create new data samples. Second, we exploit this generated data in three scenarios: (S1) balancing class distribution in the original dataset, (S2) increasing the number of samples per class, and (S3) expanding the dataset while maintaining balanced classes. Third, we evaluate the impact of these data distributions (S1, S2, S3) on model perfor mance using the EfficientNetV2B0 architecture with pre-trained and fine-tuned weights. The experimental results show a substantial improvement in classifica tion accuracy, emphasizing the critical role of data diversity and class balance. These findings highlight the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed strat egy of data generation and distribution for enhancing dataset quality, offering promising applications in plant disease detection and precision agriculture.

### [60] [The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36077)
*Weidong Tang,Ruiheng Wang,Jingxuan Zhang,Hexin Wang,Haoyuan Chen,Zhengfeiyang Zhang,Yixing Ma,Zichen Jiang,Ziyu Guo,Haodong Li,Zhengbo Jiao,Zhiqing Cui,Xinxiang Yin,Shuo Liang,Zhenglin Wan,Hongzhan Lin,Wangbo Zhao Kaipeng Zhang,Pengfei Zhou,Odin Zhang,Yang You*

Main category: cs.AI

TL;DR: 本文提出 **The Trinity**：一个面向多模态智能体的“能力驱动递归自我改进”（Capability-Driven RSI）框架，将「世界生成」与「Harness 演化」耦合起来，用 Creator、Explorer、Evolver 三个角色构成闭环。核心思想是：模态与表面形式各异的任务往往共享相同的底层能力需求（如 ARC-AGI-3 与 Micromouse 都依赖精确感知与状态跟踪），因此应把任务组织的依据从“表面类别”切换为“共享能力需求”。框架由三阶段组成：(1) 任务树构建——将 44 个公开基准规范化为统一规格（目标/观测/动作/反馈/完成判据/预算），按 5 大需求域分组；(2) 能力树构建——Evolver 依据训练任务规格与已验证轨迹归纳出 6 类能力（PST、HCI、CFR、GVT、VEA、VC）与 30 种缺陷类型，按固定能力序 ≺ 把任务需求集排序成路径并用 Trie 合并公共前缀，得到 11 个非根节点的分层能力树；(3) Harness 树构建——Explorer 在树上做选择性继承（父模块更新须在同等验证条件下严格提升任务完成数才被继承）与局部精化，Creator 则依据“能力驱动 Real2Sim2Real”把同节点异构任务的共性需求抽象成简化、可验证的仿真世界，其执行反馈与验证器检出失败反向驱动模块更新，迭代末合并去重生成新的 Base Harness。由于各节点 Harness 能力专精不同，进一步设计“能力感知 Harness Router”，仅凭公开任务信息与已验证执行经验在固定拓扑的 Harness 树中挑选兼容的模块配置。在冻结骨干（Claude Opus 5）与固定 Base Harness 下，演化后的 Harness 在 28 个训练基准上平均提升 34 分（39.06→73.16），在 18 个未见基准上提升 26 分（37.45→63.61），其中包含两个真实机器人具身任务（SOON 成功率 0→60%，CaP-X 0→60%）；能力感知自路由达到 71.27/60.96，逼近 Oracle 的 73.16/63.61，同时推理 token 更省。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 论文把多模态智能体视为“世界提供任务—人类引导学习—智能体交互产生可验证结果”的协同进化闭环，并指出该闭环在规模化时存在两个瓶颈：其一，构造异构且可验证的环境成本高昂，需要自动化世界生成；其二，智能体能力越来越受限于 Harness（围绕冻结模型的一组控制流协议：Perception、Memory、Inference、Planning、Orchestration、Loop），而人工迭代 Harness 无法跟上任务多样性与复杂度的增长。已有 Harness 递归自我改进（RSI）工作多聚焦纯文本任务（代码、数学）并采用任务特定演化，导致 Harness 过拟合、跨异构任务泛化差；而单一全局 Harness 又难以同时满足冲突需求（如具身任务中性能与效率的权衡），效率与适应性受限。作者据此提出关键洞察：不同模态、不同表面形式的任务可以共享相同的底层能力需求，因此应从“任务驱动”转向“能力驱动”的自我改进——以共享能力需求组织学习与优化多个专精 Harness，并自然导出基于能力需求的路由机制。

Method: **总体框架。** The Trinity 在冻结骨干（Claude Opus 5，低 effort 自适应思考）上耦合环境生成与 Harness 演化，三个角色分工：Explorer 收集轨迹；Evolver 从任务规格与已验证轨迹中归纳能力需求、组织能力树并驱动局部模块更新；Creator 构建/修订仿真世界，并依据验证器检出的失败提出模块修改，迭代末整合为新 Base Harness。

**Harness 形式化。** H_φ=(Πer, M, I, P, F, L) 六协议构成控制流；模块为纯函数，只吃公开记录（除 Memory 可声明 carry），可发类型化就绪信号，由 Loop 决定执行；每步至多两次模块调用且不强制；Evolution 只改模块配置、θ 固定。

**阶段一 任务树。** 44 个基准、5 域 15 子类（规则发现、受限问题求解、感知与控制、多智能体交互、长程环境）；9 个训练基准由 agent 网络搜索按公开规则重建；统一观测—动作接口保留各自信息通道与计分；训练/未见切分在能力归纳前固定；仅训练记录用于建树、世界生成、模块学习与路由记忆。

**阶段二 能力树。** 独立 agent 提议能力类别，judge 汇总，reviewer 校验定义/证据/指派/覆盖，得到 6 能力（PST 感知与状态跟踪、HCI 假设与对手推断、CFR 约束检查与反馈修复、GVT 目标承诺与价值权衡、VEA 视频证据获取、VC 视频理解）与 30 类缺陷（F01–F24、V01–V06）。能力序 c≺d≺a≺b≺e≺f 固定在建树前，每任务需求集排序成路径 p_τ=Trie 合并公共前缀；边只表示能力叠加，不表示因果依赖。树仅由训练任务构建；未见任务事后按固定分类法标注，仅用于回溯性路由评测。

**能力驱动 Real2Sim2Real。** 每节点由 Evolver 从节点需求、后代与代表任务的公开规格设计简化训练关卡（排除目标任务布局、私有证明与解题轨迹，保留核心决策过程）；Creator 用该节点的 Harness 实现关卡，省略美学优化；宿主执行的验证器池检查节点绑定、执行、状态转移、渲染与完成条件；冻结 screening Harness 只放行落在预设中间性能带内的世界，否则按预定难度维度调整（试验次数、阈值、动作预算、重试上限均预先固定）。

**阶段三 Harness 树与递归自我改进。** Explorer 在每个节点保留 Harness：H_E,v = P_v ⊕ L_v（右偏并集，局部模块覆盖继承模块）；选择性继承要求父注册表更新在相同验证任务/试验数/预算下取得严格更高的宿主验证任务完成数，否则保留旧注册表；局部模块更新（Evolve）由已验证轨迹驱动，接受则更新、拒绝则保持，局部准入不要求分数提升；祖先模块始终保留，节点完成即向子节点导出状态，兄弟分支独立演化。Creator 自顶向下在各节点演化（仅验证器检出失败才触发），迭代末按学习序合并“有效修订替换前驱 + 互补模块合并 + 近重复保留先学者”，形成下一轮共享的 Base Harness。Explorer 最终保留 29 个模块（按能力族分组），Creator 库含 25 个模块（11 个 pre-RSI 审计 + 14 个规则模块）。

**能力感知 Harness Router。** context–action–feedback 循环：输入公开目标、初始观测、元数据与图像；从固定版本化 Harness 池中检索（cosine≥0.5、至多 10 条、2 万条 FIFO 记忆），结合已执行配置的性能—代价摘要选择，须先提交基于证据的理由；执行后核对终局回执与决策/注册表哈希，再把结果与代价写入记忆；未见任务—能力配对严格排除在路由上下文、验证与记忆之外，预测账本哈希锁定后才可用于评测；技术失败计 0，无效选择无回退。

**实验设置。** 28 训练 / 18 未见基准（SOON、CaP-X 的仿真版算训练、机器人版算未见）；统一 0–100 评分；每基准—Harness 对做 5 次准备试验并把轨迹总结为技能，技能在评测时冻结（不参与演化/继承/路由）；对照为 Codex 与 DeepSeek Harness。

Result: **1) 模块与技能互补（迭代 1）。** Base 39.06/37.45；仅模块 56.95/47.26；仅技能 58.86/48.67；二者结合 63.80/53.53。

**2) 组织方式对比（仅模块）。** Global（单 Harness、28 环境）53.04/42.92；Task-Domain（15 个任务专用）51.17/40.82；Capability-Domain（6 个扁平能力组）49.25/39.43；Capability Tree (Real，10 Harness/11 环境) 53.44/42.31；Capability Tree (Sim，同拓扑+仿真课程) 56.95/47.26 为最佳，且推理 token 最低（514.42M/549.07M）。训练 token：Capability-Domain 最省（136.94M），Sim 405.70M 高于 Real 211.56M，但 Creator 建环境成本可被后续迭代的世界复用摊销。结论：扁平分组降成本但弱于 Global，能力树的选择性继承带来 +4.19/+2.88，Sim 再加 +3.51/+4.95（“less is more”）。

**3) 递归自我改进（第 0→4 轮）。** Train 39.1→73.2、Unseen 42.1→64.1；首轮收益最大，第 2–4 轮再带来 Train +9.4、Unseen +6.4；原生 17 个基准 Train 仅 64.4→68.8。个别基准持续提升（ARC-AGI-3 41.0→53.6，SciGym 45.2→57.1，BuildArena 93.3→97.8），也有停滞或回退（Mastermind 持平 88.9，Eleusis 82.2→81.1）。Unseen 均值 64.06 超过 Codex(47.49) 与 DeepSeek(46.18)，但 Crafter 与 DiG-bench 仍低于两者。

**4) 能力感知路由（迭代 4 的 H^(4)）。** Random 52.74/46.23；自路由仅公开信息 65.79/52.36；加入能力定义与分支卡片、性能—代价摘要 70.34/58.27；再加入检索到的执行经验（完整）71.27/60.96；Oracle 73.16/63.61。完整自路由逼近 Oracle，同时 token 低于 Random（497.89M vs 567.08M；541.28M vs 594.25M）。

**5) 能力—模块关联与干预。** 29 个模块与 6 协议的相关性：HCI–Inference 0.744、GVT–Loop 0.444、VEA–Perception 0.347、PST–Memory 0.306、VC–Perception/Memory 0.286、CFR–Planning 0.274；负相关最强为 GVT–Perception −0.361、PST–Loop −0.313。干预：向 Base 加入一个相关模块 +19.39 分（不相关模块仅 +1.02），相关模块还略降 token（551.85M vs 582.54M）；从完好的 H^(4) 中移除一个相关模块则 −2.74 分且 token 由 496.70M 升至 517.26M——说明能力需求可作为模块选择与组合的先验。

**6) 具身迁移。** SOON：仿真 0→80%、真机 0→60%；CaP-X：仿真 10→60%、真机 0→60%；两者在 H^(1) 即达 20%。作者亦声明该对比评估的是完整 Harness—技能配置，未分离模块演化与技能准备的各自贡献。

**7) 代价结构。** 首轮训练成本主要由 Creator 建环境主导；后续迭代复用世界摊销该开销，而 Explorer 各轮收集的轨迹数与推理 token 相当，说明在固定轨迹量下的增益来自更干净的能力导向演化信号。

Conclusion: 论文主张“能力驱动的递归自我改进”：以共享能力需求而非任务表面类别作为组织原则，用 Creator—Explorer—Evolver 三角色把世界生成与 Harness 演化耦合成闭环——Evolver 依据已验证轨迹把任务树重构为分层能力树，Creator 把同节点异构任务的共性需求抽象为简化可验证的仿真世界（Real2Sim2Real），Explorer 沿能力树以选择性继承与局部精化累积可复用模块并形成 Harness 树，再由能力感知 Router 用公开任务信息挑选兼容配置。实验表明：能力组织优于任务组织（能力树+仿真课程在训练/未见上均最佳且推理更省）；RSI 在固定能力树上可持续多轮提升并外推到未见基准与真实机器人；能力—模块相关性与受控干预支持“能力需求作为模块设计先验”的合理性；能力感知自路由在单一冻结骨干上接近 Oracle。局限包括：基准发现依赖网络搜索、覆盖度与质量不稳定；研究主要停留在 Harness 层面（未涉及参数训练），部分基准为按规则重建、部分比较未解耦模块与技能的贡献，且部分基准存在停滞或回退。展望为动态扩展能力树以容纳新涌现能力需求，并把能力感知路由与 RSI 扩展到模型参数训练，形成能力发现—获取—精炼的闭环。

Abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.

</details>


### [61] [CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36100)
*Neil Chen,Adrian Serapio,Hanxue Gu,Evan Lee,Kang Wang,Yang Yang*

Main category: cs.AI

TL;DR: CohortFlow 是一个可干预（steerable）的临床队列构建智能体：它把临床医生的自然语言纠正解释为对结构化队列规范（TaskSpec）的局部增量更新（Task Delta），并借助显式记录的语义依赖与执行 DAG 指纹做选择性失效与复用，从而无需从头重算。在 100 个源自临床试验入选标准的场景（126 次纠正）上，局部引导的 requirement micro-F1 为 77.0%，与整表再生成的 76.4% 差异不显著（p=0.493），但纠正后完成延迟降低 64.8%、执行中降低 44.3%，LLM 调用减少 38.1%；MIMIC 上的概念验证显示 13 个队列状态全部成功执行，并呈现选择性复用/重算行为。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 临床队列构建是迭代式任务：临床医生会在看到中间结果后增删排除标准、修改检验阈值或调整时间关系。现有 LLM 队列系统（Criteria2Query 系列、EC2Seq2Sql、TrialGPT、EHRAgent 等）把每次修订都当作全新任务，从头重新解析请求并重算全部流程，既浪费算力/延迟，也丢弃仍然有效的结果；更关键的是，执行顺序并不等于语义依赖关系——修改较早的某个谓词并不必然使与其无关的后续计算失效。因此需要一个能在执行中途接受自然语言纠正、按语义依赖而非执行位置来决定失效与复用的智能体。

Method: 1）状态模型：自然语言请求被解析为与数据库无关的 TaskSpec（类型化资格要求、布尔聚合逻辑、时间关系），并编译为持久化执行 DAG；临床概念解析用 MIMIC-IV 词表（ICD、检验项、药品名）配合 IDF 加权倒排检索（精确匹配失败时用 MedGemma 生成同义表达再查表），落地为确定性参数化 SQL；自由文本标准走 BM25 + 稠密嵌入（BGE）混合检索 + 交叉编码器重排（logit→sigmoid 得相关度，阈值 τ 过滤），按患者分组后由 LLM 裁定。2）局部转向：纠正 (T_t, c_t) 经 LLM 产生语义增量 Δ_t，仅对新增/修改的要求重新做类型化解析与 grounding，未变要求保留稳定标识与结构表示，再确定性合并得 T_{t+1}；纠正按语义 FIFO 顺序处理以避免对陈旧状态操作；顺序模式与并行模式（并行仅重叠纠正解释延迟，不并行化 DAG，也不改变已提交的 TaskSpec 序列）。3）依赖感知失效与复用：为每个执行节点计算由操作、依赖与执行配置导出的语义指纹，纠正后将新 DAG 与旧图对账，节点可复用当且仅当语义身份/指纹不变、所需产物可用且所有父节点均可复用；文本笔记处理采用分阶段复用（语料级分块/索引/嵌入常驻，患者级裁定按规范要求键控，候选人群收缩则保留存活患者已有裁定、扩张则只处理新患者）。4）实验：基于 CohortX Task 1 训练集构造 100 场景/126 纠正（含 26 个多纠正场景、8 个故意歧义纠正），分两阶段评测——Stage 1 用 Qwen3-8B（4-bit NF4、temperature 0）在 111 次执行中纠正与 15 次完成后纠正上对比“朴素重启”基线（并禁用回退机制）；Stage 2 用手工冻结的 TaskSpec 在 MIMIC 上做 10 个场景 + 3 次结构化纠正 = 13 个队列状态的后端可执行性与图对账验证；统计用按场景聚类的配对 bootstrap（10 万次）与场景簇随机化检验。

Result: 语义准确性：局部引导 micro-F1 77.0% vs 重启 76.4%（+0.6pp），precision 73.4% vs 73.0%，recall 81.0% vs 80.0%，按场景聚类 bootstrap 95% CI 为 [−1.23, 2.45]pp，配对随机化检验 p=0.493，不显著；简单/中等/困难场景分别为 76.9/80.0/74.9 vs 77.2/78.5/74.8。布尔逻辑等价性 85.7% vs 94.3%（−8.6pp，CI [−23.53, 3.13]，p=0.500，n=35 状态）反而更差；时间关系准确率 90.5% vs 89.5%（p=1.000）；歧义澄清仅 1/8 优于重启的 4/8；有效输出覆盖率 94.4% vs 99.2%。效率：完成后纠正平均延迟 48.6s→17.1s（−64.8%，2.84×加速；中位 47.3→17.0s），执行中纠正 69.7s→38.8s（−44.3%，1.80×；中位 67.6→41.3s）；每次纠正 LLM 调用 1.90 vs 3.07（−38.1%），completion token −67.3%，但总 token 反而多 16.5%（因提示上下文更大），说明主要收益在延迟与调用次数而非 token 消耗；延迟降幅的 95% CI 分别为 61.9–67.5% 与 41.6–47.0%。Stage 2：13 个队列状态全部成功物化患者队列，覆盖条件、患者、手术、检验、用药、入院、布尔与时间操作；三条纠正轨迹显示选择性对账——新增 COPD 条件时保留原肝硬化分支并新增 COPD 分支后重算聚合；钾阈值 >5.5 改为 >6.0 时失效受影响检验谓词及下游；时间窗 7 天放宽至 14 天时保留两个底层谓词结果、仅重算时间关系及下游。

Conclusion: 将用户不断变化的队列定义本身视为持久化计算状态、以局部 Task Delta 表达纠正、并在语义依赖层面（而非执行顺序层面）做失效与复用，可以在保持与整表再生成相当的需求级语义准确率的前提下，大幅降低纠正延迟与模型调用次数；后端实验也验证了“保留无关计算、重算受影响及依赖计算”的预期行为。主要局限与后续工作：单一 8B 模型 4-bit 量化可能限制表现，更强/更高精度模型或可缩小差距；纠正轨迹为人工构造而非前瞻性临床采集；Stage 1 未纳入临床笔记检索与推理（预期在完整异构工作流中选择性复用收益更大，但需实证）；Stage 2 仅 13 个状态属概念验证，未量化复用效率也不评估队列临床正确性；局部修订在全局布尔组合与歧义澄清上明显弱于全量再生成，说明“保留单个需求”并不保证其整体组合正确。因此该系统定位为辅助而非替代专家的队列定义与审阅工具，后续应扩展到更多模型、更大多样 EHR 数据集、完整笔记工作负载与临床交互采集的纠正。

Abstract: Language model agents for clinical cohort curation should accommodate evolving eligibility criteria without repeatedly processing unchanged requirements. We introduce CohortFlow, a steerable agent that represents natural language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification and reconciles them with a persistent execution graph. Explicitly recorded semantic dependencies enable affected computations to be selectively invalidated while preserving valid prior results. On 100 scenarios derived from clinical-trial eligibility criteria, comprising 126 correction turns, localized steering achieves 77.0% requirement micro-F1 versus 76.4% for full regeneration using the same 8B model, a small numerical advantage that is not statistically significant ($p=0.493$). It reduces mean correction latency by 64.8% after completion and 44.3% during execution, with 38.1% fewer model calls. In a separate proof-of-concept evaluation over MIMIC, all 13 cohort states execute successfully, while correction trajectories demonstrate selective preservation of unaffected computations and recomputation of changed or dependent nodes. Together, these results show that localized semantic steering can substantially reduce correction latency and model calls while maintaining strong requirement-level accuracy.

TL;DR: 本文提出一个关于「AI 比人更擅长做科学」时代人类为何与如何继续做科学的框架：科学的一项不可或缺的目标是「持久的集体人类理解」；由此推导「人类理解」与「人类方向」两支检验标准，并按 CRediT 研究阶段逐一给出 AI 使用的可反驳性默认规范，最后提出机构改革建议。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 当 AI 在核心科研任务上开始匹配甚至超越人类研究者时，科学界面临两个问题：人类为何还要做科学，以及在此前提下如何使用 AI。作者主张第二个问题只有在回答第一个问题后才能回答，即必须回到「科学为何存在」。作者刻意在强假设下论证：AI 在科学核心任务上比人更准确、更少偏误、更高效；该假设不依赖 AI 当前缺陷，因此不会随模型进步而失效。论文面向广泛科学读者，目标是给出既有原则性又可操作、可被各学领域自行裁定的建议。

Method: 以科学哲学与认识论既有成果（Dellsén 关于理解而非知识、Potochnik、de Regt、Longino、Merton、Polanyi、Malfatti、Kitcher 等）为基础，提出并精确定义原则：从知识论转向理解论，区分理解三维度（comprehension 解释能力、critical assessment 批判评估能力、capability retention 能力保持）、集体性（Longino 的批判性交流、Merton 的组织化怀疑、Boyd 的空心化风险）、持久性（通过教学与师承传递）、服务于人类目的与价值（利益相关者掌握目标/优先/用途权，研究者掌握过程性认知权威）。随后回应五项反驳：(1) 机会成本——框架管辖「进入科学记录时是否被理解」而非社会可用的技术，允许先部署后理解（麻醉、锂盐类比），极端紧急情形由利益相关者民主决策并披露；(2) 认识依赖是常态——依赖人可被问责质疑，依赖无人理解的 AI 留下缺口；(3) AI 可否算科学共同体成员——共同体成员资格与担责地位由共同体赋予，AI 目前无法承担职业规范与声誉，故方向须归可问责的人；(4) 完美 AI 会知道我们的价值——价值不是待发现的固定事实，须经受影响者协商形成（民主类比：AI 可预测选举结果但不能替代选举），结论不依赖 AI 失效；(5) 理解一直在流失——理解是程度问题，关键在变化方向，历史上技能转移给了其他人类，而 AI 可接管整个循环（含检查与批判），四色定理计算机证明案例说明问题。随后将原则转为两支检验标准，并按 CRediT 阶段（概念化、方法、调查、验证、解释、写作、社区评估、监督）逐阶段给出可反驳的默认规范与论证。最后提出制度改革：持久性（把指导计入聘用晋升、博士训练以现场方法答辩/考试评估能力而非监管 AI 使用、资助者计入指导成本）、集体理解（少计论文数、以少量精选作品评价、加重综述教材教学、强制纯人类同行评审、限制投稿量）、人类方向（资助者要求 AI 使用计划、管理组合以保持问题多样性、支持公开治理的开源模型）、透明度（按 CRediT 分阶段的结构化披露、分层引用核心/浏览文献、机器可读而非一禁了之）。

Result: 得到一个可操作的框架：只要科学共同体仍能解释、捍卫、反驳结果并保有相关技能（人类理解），且关于何问题重要、结果意味着什么的判断仍由可问责的人类掌握（人类方向），AI 即可在几乎所有研究阶段被广泛使用。逐阶段结论包括：AI 可生成候选问题与假设但研究者须自行选择、须区分「读懂的核心文献」与「仅查阅的文献」；方法须自行选择并在理解后采用，青年研究者应先自行搜索方法；调查阶段的可委派程度取决于理解所在环节，形式化领域（数学、理论计算机科学、大规模模拟）尤其需保留解释、批判与脱离机器复现三重能力，AI 生成结果只是「潜在进步」；验证阶段最可委派，但涉及结论的错误修复须由研究者理解；解释阶段须先形成自己的解读再看 AI 备选读法；写作阶段须先自行成文论证再让 AI 润色（可降低非英语写作者的门槛）；同行评审与出版后批判须保持人类，AI 可用于独立复现；监督与师承是持久性的关键。作者同时披露自身 AI 使用：Claude 用于文献检索、批评与后期修订起草，ChatGPT 用于独立评审，核心论证、原则选择、CRediT 框架与「人类方向」命名均由作者本人作出。

Conclusion: 结论为：科学除其他目的外，还存在是为了让人类理解世界并能共同决定如何行动于其中；AI 可以很好地为该目标服务，但前提是科学机构持续奖励那些保有理解、传递理解并决定研究方向的人。论文强调这些规范是默认保障而非绝对禁令，分歧应通过在具体案例中应用两支检验标准来解决；遵循社区规范也不足以保障目标，因 AI 供给方等外部行为者不受同等约束，需靠资助、开放模型与公开治理等杠杆。

Abstract: As AI begins to match or exceed human researchers at core scientific tasks, two questions become pressing: \emph{why} should humans keep doing science, and \emph{how} should they use AI when they do? This paper argues that the second can be answered only by answering the first. It holds that one indispensable aim of science is \emph{durable, collective human understanding of the world, pursued in service of human ends and values}. From this principle it derives a two-part test for when a research task can be delegated to AI. The first part, \emph{human understanding}, requires that the scientific community remain able to explain, defend and contest the resulting claims, and retain the skills to do so. The second, \emph{human direction}, requires that judgments about which questions matter and what findings mean stay with accountable humans. Applying the test to each phase of research in the Contributor Roles Taxonomy (CRediT) yields recommendations that fields can tailor to their questions and methods. The framework differs from existing guidance in three ways. It rests on an account of what science is for rather than on integrity norms. It holds even if AI outperforms human researchers, rather than depending on AI's current limitations. And it judges each use of AI by its effects on human understanding and direction rather than by the type of tool, across every phase of research, including peer review and the training of new researchers. It closes with the reforms needed to keep science aimed at human understanding and direction.
