### [353] [Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37388)
*Mihai Nica,Janosch Ortmann*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).

### [354] [How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37389)
*Sooho Moon,Yunyong Ko*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Knowledge graph embedding (KGE), a fundamental technique for knowledge-centric Web and KG-augmented AI applications, is commonly trained through contrastive learning with negative samples to learn discriminative representations. Despite its empirical success, two crucial questions regarding negative samples remain underexplored: (Q1) how many negative samples should be used for each positive sample and (Q2) how much should each negative sample contribute to learning? To answer these questions, we propose RADAR, a novel contrastive learning framework for KGE models with two effective strategies, respectively: (1) Risk-aware negative budget allocation quantifies false-negative sampling risk by modeling an open-world KG as a stochastic partial observation of its closed-world counterpart and adaptively assigns a negative budget to each positive sample based on its risk; (2) Distribution-calibrated negative weighting assigns negative weights by calibrating the weighting strength for each positive based on two complementary characteristics of the negative-score distribution: dispersion and concentration. Extensive experiments on 3 real-world KGs with 4 KGE models reveal that RADAR achieves the best KGE performance on average across all model--KG combinations and reduces sampled false negatives by over 90% compared with conventional fixed-budget methods.

### [355] [LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37390)
*Hubert Baniecki,Przemyslaw Biecek,Martin Pawelczyk*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Language model performance depends strongly on the mixture of domains in the pretraining data corpus. Popular data mixing methods select these domain weights by training many small proxy models on random mixes and then fitting a regression model to predict performance from the mix. We recognize this practice as a domain attribution problem, where the regression measures each domain's contribution to the target metric. Through this lens, the standard Dirichlet sampling of proxy data mixes is a poor regression design that requires tuning and cannot support a linear fit for hundreds of domains. Building on classical optimal experimental design, we introduce LinMix, which samples mixes at the vertices of the capped simplex so that each domain is at its cap or absent. This hyperparameter-free vertex sampling decorrelates domain effects, enabling an interpretable linear model whose coefficients are the domain attributions. The optimal mix given by LinMix provably keeps only domains with positive attribution values and requires no search over candidate mixes. We further establish the optimality of vertex sampling, and prove that Dirichlet sampling inflates the attribution error when its mixes concentrate around the prior data mix. Pretraining experiments with 1B-parameter OLMo2 and 4B Qwen3.5 language models show that LinMix outperforms Dirichlet-based data mixing across reasoning, code, and math benchmarks, with relative gains of 46% on MBPP and 14% on GSM8K. At 288 fine-grained domains, only vertex sampling supports a linear fit, and LinMix improves benchmark accuracy by 11% on average over the best nonlinear baseline.

### [356] [Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37413)
*Zhong Han*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment. For arbitrary Borel couplings, we prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for standard Euler sampling from the true source. A fourth displacement moment gives an explicit $O(N^{-1})$ bound; a second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence as drift error vanishes. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, original bridge-path KL stays of order one, comparison-path KL is of order $1/\log N$, and terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$ on the same grid. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling instead has a second-moment $O((M_2+d)/N)$ bound; finite-entropy Schroedinger bridges for the probability Brownian reference are included. We also construct a current-state learner with expected output KL consistency from iid endpoint pairs. Numerical diagnostics illustrate the distinct errors. Conditional diffusion identities specify a restoration interface, while image controls find no iterative advantage over cheap probabilistic predictors. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.

### [357] [When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37430)
*Ananth K Suresh,Aveen Dayal,Gouthaman KV,Aditya Pola,Vineeth N Balasubramanian*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: For reliable deployment, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) should recognize when an image provides insufficient evidence to answer a question and withhold unsupported answers. Yet refusal alone is not necessarily evidence of such recognition: models may refuse because of unrelated safety constraints or without identifying the missing evidence. We study how refusal on visually unanswerable questions is shaped by three sources of control: inference-time instructions, post-training, and internal activation interventions. Across three MLLMs on the MoHoBench benchmark, we systematically manipulate the meaning and placement of refusal instructions, compare supervised and preference-based post-training, and intervene on a refusal-related activation direction derived from naturally answered and refused examples. We find that refusal is highly sensitive to both the meaning and placement of instructions, with model-specific changes at the sample level that are obscured by aggregate refusal rates. Evidence-aware and general refusal instructions have stronger effects than an intentionally mismatched safety instruction. Post-training produces larger increases in refusal, but can also induce responses that combine refusal language with attempted answers. In contrast, activation intervention produces smaller yet transferable changes across prompt conditions, without evidence of indiscriminate refusal on tested visually answerable samples. These findings show that refusal is jointly shaped by external instructions, post-training, and internal representations, highlighting the need to disentangle evidence recognition from a model's learned propensity to refuse.

### [358] [CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37442)
*Congwei Zhang,Youming Tao,Yifei Zou,Yu Yang,Ruirui Zhang,Xiaoyu Zhang,Falko Dressler,Xiuzhen Cheng,Dongxiao Yu*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained edge platforms is often dominated by expert-weight movement rather than computation. Although each token activates only a small subset of experts, routing is input-dependent, so all experts must remain accessible and memory movement dominates latency. Existing approaches such as uniform pruning and expert dropping overlook two properties of MoE execution: expert combinations are highly skewed in frequency, and experts contribute asymmetrically within each combination. We present CRISP, a combination-aware framework that co-designs pruning and runtime scheduling for efficient MoE serving on memory-constrained edge platforms. CRISP reorders neurons by importance so one stored expert can support multiple execution widths, assigns differentiated execution to hot, warm, and cold combinations based on frequency and expert role, and exploits heterogeneous widths to overlap expert loading with computation. Across Mixtral-8x7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B, CRISP improves throughput by up to $2.1\times$ at the same memory budget while limiting accuracy loss to 3.6\% relative to full-width inference. Our results highlight that efficient edge MoE serving requires jointly optimizing which expert capacity is preserved and how expert execution is scheduled.

### [359] [Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37451)
*Raban Emunds,Jannis Blüml,Quentin Delfosse,Kristian Kersting*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks. While (neuro-)symbolic approaches improve transparency by incorporating symbolic reasoning, applying them directly to low-level actions results in overly complex, unreadable policies. We introduce NEXUS, a hierarchical RL framework that resolves this tension by combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By shifting transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, NEXUS drastically reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and the design of reward functions and meta-policies by interaction with LLMs. We demonstrate that NEXUS agents learn disentangled skills, are interpretable regarding high-level goals, are better aligned to goals described in the game manual, less prone to reward hacking and more robust to game simplifications than deep RL. Finally, we isolate and evaluate the impact of different meta-policy architectures (neural, symbolic, neuro-symbolic) on environmental return and aligned task performance.

### [360] [An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37456)
*Kevin Lee*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: An input skip can reduce reconstruction error while leaving a model's distribution of new samples unchanged. For a Gaussian variational autoencoder (VAE) with constant input skip $0\leq\alpha<1$, a model without a skip can be written in skip form by multiplying its decoder output by $b=1-\alpha$ and its noise variance by $b^2$. The distribution of observations and latent variables and its exact generative scores stay the same, while reconstruction mean squared error (MSE) is multiplied by $b^2$. Separate training can produce different generators because optimization depends on the parameter coordinates. In a Gaussian experiment with known density, changing skip and observation variance together reduces MSE but worsens energy score and the estimate of negative log density from importance sampling. On seven annual Deep-ocean Assessment and Reporting of Tsunamis (DART) records, energy score differences at the same observation variance have both signs on four original records and favor the skip on three records from 2018. Probabilistic principal component analysis (PPCA) has lower mean energy scores than every neural DART fit. With the encoder and decoder kept the same, estimating observation variance from training reconstruction error can also worsen energy score. Assessing generation requires more than reconstruction error.

Abstract: An input skip can reduce reconstruction error while leaving a model's distribution of new samples unchanged. For a Gaussian variational autoencoder (VAE) with constant input skip $0\leq\alpha<1$, a model without a skip can be written in skip form by multiplying its decoder output by $b=1-\alpha$ and its noise variance by $b^2$. The distribution of observations and latent variables and its exact generative scores stay the same, while reconstruction mean squared error (MSE) is multiplied by $b^2$. Separate training can produce different generators because optimization depends on the parameter coordinates. In a Gaussian experiment with known density, changing skip and observation variance together reduces MSE but worsens energy score and the estimate of negative log density from importance sampling. On seven annual Deep-ocean Assessment and Reporting of Tsunamis (DART) records, energy score differences at the same observation variance have both signs on four original records and favor the skip on three records from 2018. Probabilistic principal component analysis (PPCA) has lower mean energy scores than every neural DART fit. With the encoder and decoder kept the same, estimating observation variance from training reconstruction error can also worsen energy score. Assessing generation requires more than reconstruction error.

</details>


### [361] [GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192$\times$ Length Extrapolation in Linear Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37524)
*Elisabeth Fink*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Self-attention mechanisms have established the Transformer as the dominant backbone across natural language processing, source code intelligence, and automated theorem proving. However, all-to-all pairwise token comparison enforces a quadratic $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ compute and memory barrier alongside severe softmax attention dilution as sequence length $N$ scales beyond the training horizon. Inspired by recent advances in algebraic graph learning (\textbf{WPNet}), this work introduces \textbf{GTFormer}, a syntax-free hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) that replaces flat self-attention for general long-context sequence modeling. GTFormer organizes raw token streams into a bounded-degree hierarchy combining a balanced binary reduction tree ($\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ depth), horizontal boundary-bridging shift edges, random expander shortcuts, multi-channel convex highway gating, and a top-down broadcast pass. Across eight long-context code, log, and multi-hop retrieval benchmarks trained exclusively on sequences of length $N \le 512$, GTFormer extrapolates zero-shot to $N = 4{,}194{,}304$ ($8192\times$) on a single commodity GPU in linear $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, maintaining near-perfect accuracy where standard and RoPE Transformers suffer from out-of-distribution attention collapse and out-of-memory exhaustion.

### [362] [Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37553)
*Peize Ding*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Label-free reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) rewards a language model for agreeing with its own majority vote. It improves reasoning at first but eventually collapses: the self-assessed reward goes to one while accuracy falls, often until the model gives the same answer to every problem. The collapse appears only when training uses many problems. We explain this dataset-size dependence as a collective instability. In a solvable many-problem model in which problems share parameters, a population whose problems prefer different answers amplifies any shared perturbation for as long as the population-averaged slope $\langle F'\rangle$ of the single-problem self-reinforcement drift $F$ is positive. This holds while problems are still uncertain about their answers. Per-problem sharpening, slowed by $1/N$ for $N$ training problems, races against the shared mode, which grows at a rate $\propto\lambda^2$ independent of $N$, where $\lambda$ is the strength of the shared coupling. This yields a critical number of problems $N_c\simeq\ln(1/\delta)/(\lambda^2G)$, where $\delta$ seeds the shared mode and $G$ decreases with the initial confidence. Simulations of the model confirm the predictions: a sharp transition, $N_c\propto\lambda^{-2}$ up to a logarithmic correction, a single critical amplification $\lambda^2NG$ across couplings, confidence profiles and training variants, a logarithmic dependence on batch size, and no collapse for confident initial models. A kernel version of the theory identifies a protective coupling (generalization of sharpening) and a marginal-entropy bonus that stabilizes the uniform collective mode. In label-free RL of a small Transformer, removing the shared direction prevents collapse entirely, restoring it causes collapse, and collapse grows with training-set size and base-model entropy.

### [363] [Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37563)
*Jiafeng Lin,Yutian Zhang,Huan Zhang,Yuxuan Wang,Jinyan Feng,Yuhui Liu,Zhongyi Pei,Jianmin Wang*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Predictive maintenance is vital for commercial aviation, yet progress remains hindered by the lack of public, large-scale real-world datasets. As a result, most methods are developed and evaluated on proprietary data, limiting reproducibility. We introduce Pneuma, the first publicly available large-scale benchmark for predictive maintenance using onboard time series from in-service commercial aircraft. Built around bleed air systems, Pneuma contains over 920 million multivariate time steps across four aircraft types and 9 verified fault scenarios, directly aligned with real maintenance logs. The dataset exhibits key real-world challenges, including substantial class imbalance, subtle fault evolution patterns, and significant variance across aircraft configurations. We structure the benchmark around three tasks: multivariate forecasting, supervised fault classification, and unsupervised anomaly detection, with labels derived from actual maintenance records. Under unified settings, we evaluate over 25 models from four methodological families on 9 carefully curated subsets. The results reveal that even strong contemporary models struggle with subtle fault signatures. Further analyses show consistent gains from additional in-context examples and multivariate inference, while forecasting quality is strongly associated with anomaly detection performance. Together, these findings provide practical insights into effectively modeling complex real-world aviation time series. We hope Pneuma will serve as a rigorous and reproducible foundation for advancing data-driven predictive maintenance toward real-world deployment in commercial aviation.

### [364] [LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37570)
*Nesta Midavaine,Floris Fok,Paulo Mendes,Joao Silva,Önder Akaçık,Dimas Lima,Zülküf Genç*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. LCM-Promo is a task-specific Large Commerce Model (LCM): a finetuned LLM trained on transactional commerce data to predict user intent and promotion response. It learns monotonic promotion-response curves from production logs by interpreting single-token outputs as conversion-threshold probabilities, while conditioning on session context such as day and delivery shift. In a production A/B test on churn reactivation, LCM-Promo increased conversion by 1% and reduced promotion cost by 6% relative to the Segment-EMA production baseline.

### [365] [EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37609)
*Sihan Yang,Weichen Bai,Ruichuan An,Yiming Cheng,Zhiyuan Feng,Tianyi Jiang,Renye Yan,Ning Ding,Yifan Zhang,Renrui Zhang,Yehui Tang,Wentao Zhang*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: As executable environments for language agents scale, generating and verifying their rollouts becomes increasingly expensive. Under finite rollout budgets, this raises an important question: can data management at the environment level make agentic reinforcement learning (RL) more efficient by organizing, evaluating, and scheduling task instances together with the environments that determine their tools, states, transitions, and verification? To address this question, we introduce EnvSched (Environment-aware Scheduling), an online scheduler that learns from rollout history. EnvSched assigns scheduling value through two complementary modeling choices: exploitation prioritizes tasks likely to provide informative reward differences, while coverage spreads each batch across underobserved environments and interaction patterns. EnvSched organizes environment--task pairs as nodes in a dual-relation graph, with within-environment edges capturing task semantics and shared tool, state, and verifier structure, and cross-environment edges capturing abstract execution and reward topology. By propagating historical rollout statistics along both edge types, it predicts within-task reward variance. These predictions guide a scheduler that allocates each batch to tasks with high predicted reward variance and underobserved environments and tasks. Environment quotas and a similarity penalty further limit concentration and redundancy, yielding informative and diverse batches without additional pilot rollouts. In RL on Qwen3-8B, EnvSched achieves an average score of 48.81 across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent after 40 training steps, exceeding the highest score attained by random task selection after 120 steps. It also improves downstream performance across model sizes at the same training budget.

### [366] [Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37648)
*Andrew Szot,Samira Abnar,Omar Attia,Abbas Kazerouni,Michael Kirchhof,Cheng-Yu Hsieh,Raviteja Vemulapalli,Alexander Toshev*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.

### [367] [Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37657)
*Igor Shilov,Xiaoxue Yang,Alexander Panfilov,Evgenii Kortukov,Matthieu Meeus,Peter Romov,Wojciech Samek,Jonas Geiping,Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions.

### [368] [When Should We Intervene at Test Time?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37658)
*Jiahao Zhang,Xinling Wen,Liangliang Li,Yu Chen*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class. Average accuracy hides these failures and cannot tell a model when to use an intervention. Target labels can guide this decision, but they are scarce and some choices are already clear. We introduce PORTAL, a controller that chooses when to deploy an intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying. Each available prediction rule is a candidate, and its predictions are fixed before current feedback arrives. Every acquired label therefore evaluates all candidates on the same input. PORTAL combines these shared comparisons and directs queries toward candidates that can still overtake the current leader. It stops when the remaining labels cannot change the choice or when the possible accuracy gain no longer justifies another query. Our analysis links the required feedback to accuracy gaps and shared mistakes, explaining why some choices need much less evidence. Experiments show that this control turns an intervention that loses accuracy overall into a useful choice on selected batches. It prevents severe failures caused by changes in arrival order and preserves gains across complete corruption streams. When a fixed rule already works well, PORTAL uses little feedback to retain its performance. Periodic label checks reveal when past evidence needs refreshing and help the controller recover as conditions change. The acquired labels also train stronger candidates for future batches, and selection brings nearly all of their accuracy gains into deployment. The same feedback therefore improves both the choice made now and the predictions available to later batches.

### [369] [Online Interval Selection with Binary Predictions: Optimal Consistency and a Continuous Robustness Tradeoff](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37361)
*Zhong Han*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study online interval selection with binary predictions of membership in a final optimal solution. Requests arrive in arbitrary order; accepted requests may be revoked, but rejected or revoked requests cannot be recovered. With rewards proportional to interval length, the best consistency under finite strict robustness is $d=(3+\sqrt5)/2$ when both guarantees hold almost surely on each fixed input, including for randomized algorithms. A continuous lower bound forces consistency strictly above $d$ at every robustness budget below $4\varphi+3\approx9.472$, whereas our deterministic algorithm attains $d$ with exact robustness $\varphi^5\approx11.090$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Each held interval inherits a ledger recording positive prediction mass lost through irrevocable decisions. A tunable replacement cost gives a continuous family with exact consistency throughout and exact robustness on two parameter intervals, including $(C,R)=(25/9,10)$ and $(4,7)$. Randomization permits expected consistency approaching one with finite expected robustness, whereas almost-sure robustness forces expected consistency strictly above two at every finite budget.

### [370] [An Unconditional Space-Approximation Lower Bound for Semi-Streaming Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36577)
*Yang P. Liu,Kheeran Naidu,Hoai-An Nguyen,Janani Sundaresan*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We prove the first unconditional lower bound tradeoff between the number of passes and the approximation factor of maximum matchings in the semi-streaming model. Specifically, we show that any algorithm that outputs an $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation to maximum matching requires $\Omega(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ passes for constant $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$. Prior to our result, such tradeoffs were proven only conditioned on a certain combinatorial assumption about the density of Ruzsa-Szemerédi graphs. The state-of-the-art unconditional lower bound rules out any approximation factor better than $(8/9)$ in two passes but leaves open the possibility of a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for any $\varepsilon > 0$ even in three passes. We provide two different proofs of our result: the first proof uses the recent hierarchical-embedding framework of Assadi, Konrad, Naidu, and Sundaresan (STOC 2024) along with combinatorial constructions using Ruzsa-Szemerédi graphs. The second extends the two-level Ruzsa-Szemerédi hierarchy of Konrad and Naidu (SODA 2024) beyond two levels and proves the corresponding communication lower bound directly by induction, rather than through a reduction to Index.

### [371] [Uniformity Testing for the Monomer-Dimer Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36630)
*Joy Qiping Yang,Yuichi Yoshida*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study uniformity testing for the monomer-dimer model on a known graph $G=(V,E)$. Given samples from an unknown distribution $D_w(M)\propto \prod_{e\in M} w_e$ over matchings $M$ of $G$, we ask whether $D_w$ is the uniform distribution over all matchings of $G$ or is $\varepsilon$-far from it in total variation distance. Our main result is that, for every maximum-degree bound $\Delta$, uniformity can be tested with $\widetilde O_\Delta(\sqrt m/\varepsilon^2)$ samples, where $m=|E|$. We complement this with an information-theoretic lower bound for general graphs: for every pair of parameters $n\le m\le n^2$, there are graphs with $\Theta(n)$ vertices and $\Theta(m)$ edges on which every tester requires $\Omega(\sqrt m/\varepsilon^2)$ samples. Thus, for bounded-degree graph families with $m=\Theta(n)$, testing uniformity over the space of matchings has $\widetilde \Theta(\sqrt n/\varepsilon^2)$ sample complexity, in contrast with the $\Theta(n/\varepsilon^2)$ samples needed to estimate $D_w$ in total variation distance.

### [372] [Differentially Private Preconditioned Power Iteration Method for Principal Component Analysis that Adapts to the Coherence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36691)
*Duy V. Le,Ta Duy Nguyen,Alina Ene,Huy L. Nguyen*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we are given as input a matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ and an integer $k\leq d$, and the goal is to find the top $k$ right-singular vectors of $A$. We consider the setting where each row of $A$ is the private data of an individual, and we design an $(\epsilon,\delta)$-differentially private algorithm whose utility guarantee improves with the coherence of the input matrix. Prior works were either restricted to the case $k=1$ or ensured significantly weaker privacy protections. Our algorithm is based on a preconditioned variant of the power iteration method that is designed to significantly reduce the noise needed to ensure privacy.

### [373] [Linear-Time FPT Rectilinear Planarity Testing of Series-Parallel Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37018)
*Giacomo Ortali*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: A planar graph is rectilinear planar if it admits a planar orthogonal drawing without bends. For series-parallel graphs in the variable embedding setting the best known testing algorithm takes $O(n^2)$ time. We show that rectilinear planarity of a series-parallel graph with maximum degree four can be tested in $2^{O(k)}\cdot n$ time, where $k$ is the number of degree-4 vertices; the planar embedding is not fixed. In particular, the running time is subquadratic when $k=o(\log n)$. Each node of the SPQ$^*$-tree stores the set of its admissible spiralities; we show that this set is a union of $2^{O(k)}$ arithmetic progressions of step two. All proofs are in the paper and are additionally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

### [374] [Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Mixed Evacuation Problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37065)
*Naoyuki Kamiyama*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: The mixed evacuation problem is a variant of the dynamic transshipment problem where there exist two modes of transportation and we allocate supplies to each mode of transportation in such a way that we can send all the supplies from sources to sinks within a given time limit. It is known that this problem can be solved in polynomial time when the number of sources and sinks is small. In this paper, we prove that the mixed evacuation problem can be solved in polynomial time with the ellipsoid method.

### [375] [Tight Bounds for Randomized Generalized $k$-Server on Uniform Metrics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37192)
*Junho Hwang*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the generalized $k$-server problem, each of $k$ servers moves in its own metric space, and a request $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ is served once some server $i$ stands at the point $r_i$ of its space. We determine the randomized competitive ratio against an oblivious adversary when every space is a uniform metric. With unit distances the ratio is $\Theta(k\log k)$: we give a $(k+1)\ln(2k)$-competitive algorithm and show that for large $k$ every algorithm has ratio at least $\frac{1}{20}k\ln k$, improving the bounds $O(k^2\log k)$ and $\Omega(k)$ of Bienkowski, Jeż, and Schmidt. When server $i$ pays $w_i$ per move, the ratio is $\exp(\Theta(k))$: we give a $20^k$-competitive algorithm, which also applies to weighted $k$-server on uniform metrics. This improves the $\exp(O(k^2))$ bound of Bijoy, Mondal, and Chiplunkar and matches the $\Omega(2^k)$ lower bound of Ayyadevara and Chiplunkar up to the base of the exponent. Both algorithms follow normalized weights exactly, through couplings whose expected movement is controlled by the decrease of the logarithm of the total weight. The lower bound hides a random permutation among the solutions of random permutation constraints, which split into small, well-separated components, and then forbids one position to one server at a time.

### [376] [A Linear Kernel for Planar Semitotal Domination](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37295)
*Paloma T. de Lima,Lukas Retschmeier*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: A set of vertices $S$ in a graph $G$ is a semitotal dominating set if $S$ is a dominating set and every vertex in $S$ has a witness, that is, another vertex in $S$ within distance at most two. The Semitotal Domination problem asks whether $G$ admits such a set of size at most $k$. We study this problem parameterized by the solution size. We provide a linear kernel of size $358k$ on planar graphs, a result that adds to several existing linear kernels for other domination variants on planar graphs. Additionally, we show Semitotal Domination is $W[2]$-hard on split graphs, on bipartite graphs and on $t$-claw-free graphs, it is $W[1]$-hard on circle graphs.

### [377] [safeL4: Rethinking Safe-Language-Based Single Address Space Microkernels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35999)
*Zheyuan Xu,Xiaobei Zhang,Zihan Li,Zekai Nie,Guangtao Zhu,Zhuang Lu,Qianying Zhang,Shijun Zhao,Haibo Chen,Rui Hou*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: Microkernels provide good features such as high security, safety, and flexibility, but their reliance on hardware-based isolation leads to heavy performance overhead, limiting their widespread adoption. Although constructing single-address-space microkernels based on safe language-based isolation is a promising approach to addressing the performance issue, this approach still faces challenges in maintaining the principle of minimality and enforcing capability-based, fine-grained access control over system resources. We propose safeL4, an approach to constructing microkernels based on safe languages. It guarantees minimality through low-level abstractions for unsafe operations, and implements a capability system based on the safe language's object capabilities to achieve fine-grained access control over all operations on system resources. We implement a prototype system in Rust, and our evaluation results show that the primitives provided by safeL4 are, on average, 1.9$\times$ faster than those of seL4.

### [378] [Callosal: Rethinking the Kernel Page Cache for Disaggregated Storage and Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36347)
*James McMahon,Amit Samanta,Seung-seob Lee,Ryan Stutsman,Anurag Khandelwal*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: Classic distributed filesystems like NFS centralize filesystem operations on a server and use custom, filesystem-specific approaches for managing cache consistency across client nodes. This limits scalability, and it leads to weak consistency, ruling out applications that concurrently access and mutate shared files. Our key insight is that these legacy designs are now too storage-centric; with today's large memories, OS page caches do most of the "heavy lifting" in accessing data, not the filesystem and block storage layers. In response to this, we present Callosal, a page cache for a cluster of machines that is centered on shared disaggregated memory. Rather than serializing operations through a filesystem server and using ad hoc caching like NFS, Callosal is built around the existing Linux page cache paths and is accelerated by RDMA and programmable switches. Callosal delivers the strong consistency that programs expect with local filesystems (like in ext4 and tmpfs) while avoiding the additional network access delays and bottlenecks that host-based solutions incur. We compare Callosal against NFS, CephFS, and local filesystems; often Callosal can provide caching performance similar to local filesystems while also scaling across nodes. For mixed read/write workloads, on average Callosal has 4.6x higher throughput than NFS when contention is not extreme, and it offers strong consistency guarantees like CephFS, while outperforming it. For a file-backed key-value store with 1% writes and uniform access, Callosal scales 1.7x across 4 nodes, while CephFS collapses across nodes.

### [379] [USB Differentiated Service for Networked Cyber-Physical Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36436)
*Anton Njavro,Rafiuddin Syed,Shriram Raja,Zhiyuan Ruan,Richard West*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: Cyber-physical systems are increasingly complex, requiring high throughput, low-latency data processing across multiple cores and compute devices. Additional functional safety challenges dictate the need for high system availability in the presence of failures. Together, these requirements are addressed using a network of compute nodes across which data processing, control and functional safety tasks are distributed. A key challenge is how to address the service requirements of independent data flows, spanning a set of hosts and I/O devices. In this paper, we show how to develop connectivity between hosts using a custom xDCI gadget driver that uses USB interrupters to differentiate the processing of separate data flows. Our solution is the first to handle both isochronous and bulk communication at USB 3.0 transfer rates, with predictable bus latencies down to the granularity of a 125 microsecond microframe, which is sufficient for many CPS control operations. We present an end-to-end solution that couples the predictable execution of user-level tasks with interrupt processing and data communication, so that multiple virtual connections are able to share a common bus. This work is not only applicable to host networking but also device I/O, which makes it arguably desirable for CPS scenarios requiring short-range communication, such as in vehicle control area networks or robotics.

### [380] [When Connectivity Misleads: Guiding Agentic Search with Contrastive Evidence Paths](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36134)
*Junchen Li,Liang Xu,Rongzheng Wang,Qizhi Chen,Junhao Wen,Shuang Liang*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: 本文指出用 PPR 等图扩散做检索排序会因「连接数多」而系统性抬高高连接干扰文档的名次，并让智能体在有限观察窗口内被噪声文档挤占，进而提出 CEP（对比式证据路径）：用「最强单条路径支持 + 背景访问分布校准」为候选打分并保留其来源路径；再以 SCI（结构化语料交互）把候选与路径组织成地图（map），配合 read/bash/graphsearch/graphexpand 供智能体验证来源与从锚点做定向扩展。在 BrowseComp-Plus（830 查询、10 万文档）与 TREC-COVID 上，SCI 以三种骨干模型取得最优准确率（91.08%/95.30%/94.94%）与最优 nDCG@10（81.77%），相对各骨干最强基线工具调用最多降 54.0%、生成成本最多降 38.6%，并显著抑制了连接数导致的排序虚高。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 检索增强生成正从「一次性检索」转向「搜索智能体 + 语料交互」：智能体在有限观察窗口（每轮仅见少量候选预览）内用候选排序和文档间关系决定下一步动作。已有工作用跨文档实体图配合交互式语料访问做多跳证据发现，但存在两个结构性缺陷：
1) **连接诱导的排序偏置（Connectivity Induced Ranking Bias）**：PPR 类扩散法把多条路径的传播贡献累加到节点分上，连接数多的干扰文档即使内容价值低也会排名靠前甚至进入 Top10，挤占观察窗口；作者的受控实验表明，在文档内容、查询、初始种子固定的前提下，仅给干扰文档加边就能显著提升其 PPR 名次。
2) **探索中的路径盲区（Path Blindness）**：扁平的节点分数不暴露「种子→候选」的来源路径，智能体即便把候选收进工作区，也只能靠窗口内的零散线索猜测该读哪篇、下一步搜什么，工作区中的金标准文档可能始终未被读取。
因此需要一种既能纠正连接带来的结构偏置、又能显式给出证据链的检索机制，并把图检索与语料交互真正耦合起来。

Method: **1. 文档图构建（离线）**：用 GLiNER2.5-small 抽取 8 类实体（阈值 0.5），保留 2 ≤ df(e) ≤ τ(=4) 的跨文档实体；文档-实体二部图上用 Ã_ve = log(1+c_ve)·γ_ve 并按实体归一化得 A_ve，对数项抑制高频实体的边际贡献；投影为文档图 W_uv = Σ_e A_ue·A_ve，行归一化得静态转移矩阵 P。

**2. CEP 检索（Contrastive Evidence Paths）**
- *起点与问题条件化转移*：按段最大内积语义分 d_Q(v)（Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B，1024 段长/128 重叠/截取 256 维）与文档级 BM25 用 RRF（k=60）融合，取 Top-R(=1000) 为起点，权重 p_i ∝ 1/j；用 g_Q(v)=(k+r_Q(v))^{-1/2} 重加权目的地并归一化得问题条件化转移 K_Q，使路径偏向与原问题相关的文档。
- *最强路径支持*：M_i(v) = max_{π:0≤ℓ≤H} p_i(v0)·λ^ℓ·Π K_Q（λ=0.5，H=3），用 max-product 动态规划（广义 Bellman-Ford 形式）迭代求解，通过记录最大前驱回溯得到最优路径及路径上相邻文档的共享实体。
- *背景访问分布校准*：以均匀重启 PageRank（α=0.5，迭代 24 次，孤立节点质量均摊）估计 b_Q(v)，得校准分 S_i(v) = M_i(v)/√b_Q(v)；√ 缓和背景概率差异影响。附录 A 证明把校准因子并入边权（K̃_Q = λK_Q·h(v)/h(u)，h=b^{-1/2}）与端点校准完全等价，且中间背景因子相消、环权小于 1。
- *收集*：按 S_i 取 Top-B(=1000) 候选，把候选及其最强路径上的全部文档全文并入工作区（按文档 ID 去重）。

**3. SCI 交互框架**：提供 read、bash、graphsearch、graphexpand 四个工具。graphsearch 用 CEP 收集文档并为每查询构建「地图」：Top10 候选 + 240 字符预览 + 来源路径 + 共享实体链接；graphexpand(a,q) 以锚点为唯一起点做 2 跳、束宽 64 的 CEP 束搜索（K_q 与 b_q 按扩展查询重算），可将工作区中已存在但未展示的文档重新带回地图。上下文在 20 万 token 时清理旧工具输出（保留最近 12 条）。

Result: **主结果**
- BrowseComp-Plus（100,195 文档/830 查询）：SCI 准确率 91.08%（GPT-6-Luna）、95.30%（DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash）、94.94%（Qwen3.8-Flash），均为最高；相对各骨干最强基线工具调用减少 14.9%–54.0%、生成成本减少 8.4%–38.6%。对 AtlasNav（同样用图）轮数相近但工具调用约减半；对 NeMo Agent（轮数最少）则准确率更高、成本更低。端到端平均耗时在三个骨干上均最低（45.18s/62.11s/333.78s）。
- TREC-COVID：nDCG@10 达 81.77%，比 RARG++（75.97%）高 5.80 个百分点，同时轮数 −56.3%、工具调用 −33.6%、成本 −48.3%；RISE-BM25 工具调用更少但排序质量显著更差（58.42）。
- 语料扩展：从 100K 扩到 1M 文档（叠加 FineWeb-Edu 90 万），SCI 准确率降至 85% 但始终优于 RARG++；graphsearch 平均 0.877s、graphexpand 0.264s，仍具交互可用性。

**消融**
- 检索算法（初始检索金标准召回@100/500/1000）：CEP 50.59/71.68/78.15%，均最高；Top10 预览召回 26.50% vs PPR 21.88%、Dense 20.83%。PCST（返回子树，无法排 Top10）整体落后。
- CEP 组件：去掉「最强路径支持」或「背景校准」均降低工作区与预览召回，其中校准的作用更大；两者同去最差。
- 结构化地图与局部扩展（100 查询、GPT-6-Luna）：完整 SCI 93% 准确率，去掉地图结构或禁用扩展各降至 83%，两者同去降至 80%；无地图时 read/bash 调用显著上升，说明路径指引与锚点扩展是发现关键证据的关键机制。

**行为与机制分析**
- 证据覆盖演化：工作区金标准召回 78.15% → 94.65%，地图 30.55% → 76.48%，预览 26.50% → 73.87%。
- 局部扩展在 830 个查询中的 511 个被触发，新增 67 篇金标准文档，并让 372 篇「已入工作区但从未展示」的金标准文档首次出现在地图中（其中 37/212 篇随后被 read 或 bash 访问）。
- 连接偏置抑制：CEP 检索结果的平均度与高连接节点占比在 Top10/100/1000 均低于 PPR；金标准文档中位名次从 245 提升到 147，2,407 组配对中 73.1% 胜出。
- 受控加边实验：PPR 下干扰文档平均名次 50.67 → 24.96、Top10 进入率 0% → 15.22%；完整 CEP 45.79 → 75.87 且 Top10 进入率保持 0%，而去掉背景校准时名次几乎不变（42.21 → 42.21）——直接证明校准项是抑制连接红利的关键。

**补充对比**
- 小模型（Qwen3.8-27B，100 查询）：SCI 84% 准确率、19.92 轮/22.64 次调用，优于 RARG++（83%，−50.1% 轮数、−54.0% 调用），远超专门训练的 OpenResearcher-30B-A3B（46%）与 QUEST-35B-RL（48%）。
- 与图 RAG（1,545 文档缩减语料）：原生管道 HippoRAG2/PathRAG/LinearRAG 为 42%/28%/28%；接入 Pi Agent 后升至 89%/83%/85%，而 SCI 达 97%、成本 $0.55 远低于 $2.43–$5.13；SCI 在全量 10 万语料上仍达 93%，成本 $1.96。

Conclusion: 连接数并不等于证据价值：图扩散的多源累加会把「易被到达」误当成「更值得读」。本文用「最强单路径支持 + 背景访问分布校准」这一对比式打分纠正了连接诱导的排序虚高，并把来源路径作为一等公民返回给智能体，再通过结构化地图与锚点扩展把图检索与语料交互打通，形成「检索—验证—定向扩展—再检索」的持续证据探索闭环。结果表明该组合在准确率、排序质量、工具调用数、生成成本与端到端时延上同时优于传统检索智能体、语料交互智能体与图 RAG 方法。

需要留意的边界与可质疑点：① 依赖论文所设定的实体抽取质量与 df 上限（τ=4），图质量的上限受限于实体抽取误差，且连通性/枢纽节点效应只是被「除以背景访问概率」而非真正消除，背景分布本身仍由度数结构决定；② max 路径支持偏向稀疏、单一强链路的候选，可能低估多条中等强度证据协同的文档；③ 端点校准依赖均匀重启的 PageRank 作为「无偏」参照，其合理性是经验性假设；④ 地图消融与机制分析多在 100 查询子集上完成，主结果的 nDCG@10 依赖智能体返回的 10 条排序，与常规检索评测口径不完全可比；⑤ 论文明确指出局限在于固定语料，未处理语料演进下的增量图更新（作者将其列为未来工作）。

Abstract: Search agents can use cross-document graphs to discover sources through multi-hop connections and choose subsequent actions based on candidate rankings and relationships within a limited observation window. However, documents may rank highly because their numerous connections make them easier to reach, without necessarily providing more valuable evidence. Graph diffusion methods such as Personalized PageRank (PPR) aggregate propagation contributions from multiple sources, allowing highly connected distractor nodes to crowd the observation window. Flat node scores also obscure cross-document evidence trails, limiting continued exploration. We propose Contrastive Evidence Paths (CEP), which scores candidates by their strongest individual paths on a query-conditioned document graph and calibrates these scores against the same graph's background visitation distribution to mitigate structural bias. CEP ranks candidates by the calibrated scores and retains the corresponding source paths. Building on CEP, we develop Structured Corpus Interaction (SCI), which organizes candidates and their connecting paths into a structured Map, enabling agents to verify source documents and pursue missing information through expansion from anchor documents. Experiments on BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-COVID show that SCI achieves state-of-the-art answer accuracy and nDCG@10 with the lowest generation cost. Compared with the strongest baselines by task performance, maximum reductions in tool calls and total generation costs exceed 50% and 40%, respectively. Further analysis confirms that SCI with CEP suppresses ranking inflation induced by structural connections and improves gold recall and exploration efficiency.

</details>


### [381] [Counterfactual Profile Perturbations for Recommendation Explanations: A Reproducibility Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36208)
*Meysam Varasteh,Elizabeth McKinnie,Robin Burke*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: 这是一篇对反事实推荐解释方法 LXR（Learning to eXplain Recommendations，Barkan et al., 2024）的复现与扩展研究。作者扩展 LXR 到 top-10 推荐项，新增 Pop（物品流行度）与 LF（矩阵分解潜在因子相似度）两个基线，分析流行度影响（热门物品更易解释、长尾物品解释更短但覆盖率低），并用穷举搜索估计最优扰动下界。结果表明 LXR 可泛化到非 top-1 项且 LXR10 更优；LF 在 MF 推荐器上甚至优于 LXR；平均扰动规模偏大（多数超过 5 个物品），实用性存疑；穷举最优 MPNR 约 7，与 LXR10 差距不大，说明 LXR 次优但不悬殊。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 推荐系统解释研究长期面临两难：要么为复杂推荐模型提供透明性（但难以用自然语言概括模型内部机制），要么退而给出只是对推荐过程的合理化（rationalization）而非真实反映。LXR 通过学习用户档案中的“反事实扰动”（若用户不喜欢物品 i1、i2、i3，则目标物品 i 不会被推荐）提供因果性、真实性且与具体推荐模型解耦的解释。然而原论文存在四方面局限：(1) 只解释 top-1 推荐项；(2) 借用计算机视觉方法用“被消除的档案百分比”报告结果，但推荐系统用户画像长度差异巨大，百分比粒度掩盖了绝对扰动规模；(3) 基线仅含 LIME-RS、SHAP 等反事实方法，缺少如物品流行度这类简单基线；(4) 缺乏对 LXR 相对最优（最小）扰动的接近程度评估。因此本文提出 RQ1–RQ4 四个研究问题以系统检验 LXR 的能力边界。

Method: 方法上分为四部分。①推荐模型：矩阵分解（MF，二值交互向量经投影矩阵得用户表示，与物品向量内积后 sigmoid）与变分自编码器（VAE，编码器输出高斯潜变量、解码器重构交互，架构参照 Liang et al. 2018），先训练推荐器并生成推荐，作为 LXR 训练数据。②解释模型：LXR（解释器 e 将用户二值档案 x 与 one-hot 目标物品 y 映射为解释掩码 m，通过反事实损失项在固定的推荐器输出上训练，得出 profile item 的重要性评分，取高分项构成扰动 Π）；LXR10（扩展版，每个用户从 top-10 推荐中采样一个目标物品训练，以处理 RQ1）；新增两个基线——Pop（物品在训练集中的评分流行度）与 LF（用 MF 的物品潜在因子向量作为稠密嵌入，计算目标物品与档案物品的潜空间相似度，Adam 优化训练）。③数据：ML1M（≥3.5 分，576,128 评分 / 6,037 用户 / 3,381 物品）、Yahoo Music（≥70 分，采样 13,797 用户，365,750 评分 / 4,604 物品）、Pinterest（随机采样 486,744 评分 / 19,155 用户 / 9,362 物品），80/20 训练测试划分，训练集 10% 用于调参。④评测：用绝对物品数取代档案百分比——从空扰动开始逐个加入最高分物品，当目标物品在推荐列表中下降 k=10 位时停止；定义 MPNR（Minimum Perturbation to Not Recommend，最小使目标项下降 10 位的扰动大小）与 Coverage（存在可行扰动的用户比例），并用 Ranked Biased Overlap (RBO) 比较不同解释器所得扰动列表的重叠度。任务分为 Top1（解释 top-1 物品）与 Top10（随机选自 top-10）两种。最优性研究：对 ML1M 中 LXR MPNR ≤ 20 的用户，穷举所有小于 20 的档案子集搜索最小扰动。

Result: Top1 任务：LXR10 在所有条件下优于或等于 LXR；LF 表现强（MF 下 MPNR 低至 7，与 LXR 同为 8；VAE 下在 Yahoo/Pinterest 上接近 LXR），但因可访问推荐模型参数并非黑盒；Pop 在 MF+Yahoo 上 MPNR=14 表现意外好，VAE+ML1M 下 MPNR=61 则明显较差。Top10 任务：LXR10 最强（VAE 下 ML1M MPNR=12、Yahoo 7、Pinterest 8；Coverage 达 97–100%），LF 在全部 MF 场景占优（MPNR 4–5）并在 Yahoo+VAE 上与 LXR 持平，但在 ML1M+VAE 上明显更差；Pop 普遍最差。覆盖率-扰动曲线显示绝大多数用户的扰动规模超过 5 个物品，原论文用百分比报告掩盖了这一点。RBO 分析显示 LXR10 与 LF 的扰动列表重叠度低（0.16–0.36），说明最优扰动解不唯一，不同解释器找到的是语义不同但效果相近的物品子集。流行度过滤实验（LXR10-filter，剔除最热门 15% 物品）：MPNR 普遍减半（ML1M 18→12、Yahoo 6→3、VAE 下 12→7、7→3），但 Coverage 大幅下降（Yahoo 98%→33%、97%→40%），表明热门物品主导了可解释性但其反事实解释对用户而言可信度低。穷举最优搜索结果：最优 MPNR 平均约 7，MF 下 LXR10=10、LF=9；VAE 下 LXR10=8、LF=11，说明 LXR10 略次优但差距不大。推荐器本身：VAE 在 HR@10 与目录覆盖上全面优于 MF（ML1M 0.19/0.44、Yahoo 0.40/0.23、Pinterest 0.10/0.72），MF 表现出明显流行度偏差，Pinterest 推荐任务最难。

Conclusion: LXR 可有效推广到 top-10 推荐项，且采样式训练（LXR10）进一步提升效果，说明该反事实扰动机制并不限于 top-1 项。流行度本身不是强解释信号（Pop 基线在多数条件下表现平平），但过滤热门物品后会显现出 Coverage 与 MPNR 之间的强烈权衡：长尾物品的解释更短却覆盖更少，表明热门物品可能需要基于用户群体的全局式解释，而长尾物品适合用户档案级反事实解释。最关键的是实用性结论：即便最优解释器的平均扰动规模也偏大，多数情况下超过 5 个物品，使 “若你未喜欢这些物品则不会推荐” 的模板在实践中难以被用户理解与接受，因此需要引入对扰动项的聚类/摘要机制。LXR10 在扰动规模上已接近穷举最优（7 vs 8–10），进一步算法优化空间有限，未来突破点更可能在解释表述与解释类型划分上。作者提出四个后续方向：用户研究（验证理解度与接受度，尤其是扰动规模的影响）、扰动摘要化、扰动唯一性研究（同一任务可能存在多个有效解，需引入扰动规模之外的评估指标）、混合解释类型（对不受档案影响的极热门物品采用全局模式解释）。此外，MF 的物品嵌入在反事实任务中甚至优于 LXR 本身，若能推广到其他推荐算法，将为“玻璃盒”式模型导向透明性提供无需额外训练模型的路径。

Abstract: This reproducibility paper explores the counterfactual explanation technique known as Learning to eXplain Recommendations (LXR). Prior work has shown that LXR can reliably identify perturbations that, if applied to a user's profile, cause the user's top ranked item to no longer be recommended, thereby explaining the item's recommendation as a function of the user's rating choices. In this paper, we extend this work in multiple ways. We expand the scope of the original LXR study to look at explanations for items other than the most highly recommended item, finding that LXR is also effective at this version of the task. We consider alternate baselines for LXR, including item popularity and latent factor similarity, and we see that for some tasks these alternatives work surprisingly well. We also examine the impact of item popularity, finding that LXR offers better explanation quality (shorter perturbations) when less popular items are being explained. Finally, we conduct a brute-force exploration of a subset of the perturbation space in order to estimate a lower bound for optimal perturbation size against which LXR and other such methods can be compared.

</details>


### [382] [The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36763)
*Ziluowen Luo,Ruochen Liu,Jun Yin,Hao Yan,Zhengxuan Hu,Xinze Shi,Chaozhuo Li,Chengqi Zhang,Senzhang Wang*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: 本文提出 API（Adapting the Pretrained Interpretable vocabulary）框架，用机制可解释性领域预训练的稀疏自编码器（P-SAE）特征字典直接充当生成式推荐（GR）的语义 ID 词表，无需任何推荐域内的额外词表拟合。API 包含两个核心组件：PID（Pretrained Interpretable IDs，基于激活强度与特征流行度加权的优先级选择，保留特征索引、相对激活强度与语义标注）与 SPA（Semantic Prediction Adapter，联合预测特征索引序列与强度分布，并以条目级偏好对齐损失保证目标商品排序）。方法在 Beauty/Sports/Toys 上取得 12 项指标中 9 项最佳，tokenization 成本仅为 RVQ 的 1/108、UTGRec 的 1/179，并支持特征级检索解释与可控干预（steering）。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 生成式推荐（GR）通常在 PLM 物品文本表示上拟合离散语义 ID（SID）词表（如 RVQ、RQ-VAE、OPQ、HiD-VAE、UTGRec 等），存在三方面问题：(1) 需要额外的词表拟合优化成本；(2) 词表语义覆盖依赖拟合数据域，跨域泛化受限；(3) 学到的 token 通常不具备可直接解释的语义。作者指出：机制可解释性研究产出的预训练稀疏自编码器（P-SAE）已经为 PLM 提供了带人类可读描述的特征字典，其特征索引天然可作为可复用的 SID 词表。但直接复用需解决两大挑战：(a) 推荐适配——紧凑 token 预算下需保留物品区分度，并让目标物品在共享主特征的候选中胜出；(b) 检索解释——需把特征可解释性从物品内容延伸到检索决策。

Method: API 框架（无额外词表学习）：

(1) PID 构造（§4.1）：冻结 GPT-2-small 与其配对 P-SAE（Bloom SAE，SAELens，24,576 个带标注特征）。按 Eq.(3) 用解码器范数缩放并对 token 位求均值得到物品级特征激活 a_ij；从 top-256 正激活特征中取 M=32 构成候选池 C_i；用选择优先级 π_ij = log(1+a_ij)·log(1/ρ_j)（ρ_j 为目标域训练集上该特征在候选池中的平滑流行度）选出 K 个特征，使低流行度特征可补偿弱激活、缓解共享主特征挤占预算；按激活强度降序排列索引，并以归一化对数强度 q_i 保留相对强度（Eq.5）；再挂接预训练语义标注 m_i，构成 PID_i = (c_i, q_i, m_i)。命题 4.1 给出同 token 序列物品的可分性上界 n_max ≤ 1+⌊δ/(Δ−2ε)⌋（由重建误差 ε 与强度和变差 δ 界定碰撞数）。

(2) SPA（§4.2）：历史编码不用仅 K 个 PID token，而用完整候选池 C_i 的“特征–强度”对 E_i，经特征编码器 Ψ_θ（可训练特征嵌入 + 强度编码、标准化 log(1+a) 后由 8 组 gain/shift 调制、经 GELU、锚点与位置嵌入）压缩为每物品 5 个 token，再由推荐 Transformer F_θ 得到 H_u。输出端联合预测目标物品的特征索引序列分布 p_θ(c|H_u)（支持 AR 与 PR 解码）与归一化强度向量 q̂_u。

(3) 条目级监督（§4.3）：物品得分 s_θ(u,i) = ℓ_u(i) − β·D_H(q̂_u, q_i)，D_H 为平方 Hellinger 距离；联合损失 L = E[−s_θ(u,i+) + λ·L_pref]，L_pref 为候选集上的偏好对齐（log-sum-exp 形式），确保目标物品排在其余候选之前。命题 4.2 证明共享特征序列时目标与竞争物品的间隔 ≥ β(Δ_q − 2√(Δ_q ε_u))，ε_u < Δ_q/4 即保证正确排序。

(4) 检索解释（§4.4）：将序列对数似然按位置分解，特征级贡献 φ_{u,i}(c_{i,r}) = ℓ_{u,r}(i) + β√(q̂_{u,r} q_{i,r})，候选间得分差逐特征分解为 Σ_j(φ_{u,i}(j) − φ_{u,i′}(j))，并与预训练语义标注配对，形成“为什么偏好 A 而非 B”的证据链。

实验设置：Amazon Beauty/Sports/Toys 官方划分；T5 与 GPT-2 两种骨干，AR（TIGER 式）与 PR（RPG 式）解码；对照含 Random、OPQ、RVQ、RQ-VAE、RKMeans、HiD-VAE、PID（无 SPA）等词表方法，以及 GRU4Rec、BERT4Rec、TIGER、LC-Rec、RPG、UTGRec、Ghost、DiGR、TDPM 等完整框架；指标 Recall@5/10、NDCG@5/10（全目录、PR 精确打分，AR 用宽度 50 的目录约束 beam search）。另外以 collision rate、Overlap@20（标题 TF-IDF 与 PLM 参考）、feature exposure@10 评估 PID 质量。

Result: (1) 排序性能：API 在 12 项“数据集×指标”比较中 9 项最佳（Toys 四项全胜），Beauty R@5/N@5 与 Sports R@10 次优；相对 GRU4Rec、BERT4Rec、TIGER、LC-Rec、RPG、UTGRec、Ghost、DiGR、TDPM 均占优（GPT-2 骨干下 Beauty R@5 0.0457、Sports R@5 0.0271、Toys R@5 0.0414）。T5-AR 相比最强学习式词表基线 Recall@5 提升 2.5%–4.2%；SPA 在全部 6 个 AR 设置与 18 个 PR 设置中的 16 个上优于直接 PID。

(2) PID 质量：K=4 时碰撞率由 Native SAE 的 80.76% 降至 17.09%（Beauty 15.16%、Sports 21.48%、Toys 14.64%）；随机选择碰撞更低但内容对齐显著更差；置换“特征–激活”谱后碰撞不变而 Overlap@20 跌至 0.2% 以下，说明低碰撞≠内容保真；K=8 时激活加权余弦邻域比仅索引 Jaccard 邻域在 PLM 参考上高 1.03%/2.60%/4.41%。

(3) 消融（T5-PR, K=8）：仅索引预测 → 加偏好对齐使 R@10 分别提升 13.3%/45.9%/9.4%；单独加强度建模会降低 NDCG@10，但与偏好对齐耦合后再提升 4.0%–6.0%，完整 SPA 最优，说明强度证据需与条目级偏好对齐配合。

(4) 词表复用与成本：冻结 P-SAE 字典、仅用目标域 IDF 即可跨域复用，在 Toys/Sports 上碰撞率与 R@5 领先，Beauty 上略逊于 R-SAE；三任务累计 tokenization 时间为 API 3.78×、RVQ 407.69×、UTGRec 674.99×（以一次 GPT-2 编码为基准），几乎消除词表拟合开销。

(5) 可解释性与可控性：Sports 特征 f_4260（弹药/武器）标题一致率 98.7%、相对词表基线提升 7.91×；Toys 案例中 LEGO 积木盒以 +0.2897 分差超越 Bruder 积木配件，其中 +0.2993 来自 token 似然、−0.0096 来自强度一致性，按 PID 位置可定位正/负证据特征；冻结参数、仅编辑历史激活，f_4260 在 +0.50 剂量下使目标物品 exposure@10 提升 1.365 个百分点（332 名用户，95% CI [0.652, 2.189]）。

Conclusion: API 证明“词表已经存在”：把 P-SAE 的预训练特征字典适配为 GR 的共享 SID 词表，可在零额外词表拟合成本下获得有竞争力的推荐性能，同时把可解释性从物品语义延伸到检索决策（特征贡献分解 + 激活干预）。核心洞见是：仅用特征索引不足以区分物品与解释排序，必须联合建模相对激活强度，并配合条目级偏好对齐监督；反之，强度证据只有在偏好对齐存在时才真正带来增益。局限与未来方向：可解释特征字典的语义质量受预训练 SAE 覆盖度限制；当前解释与 steering 仍在玩具级（Amazon 三域）与有限特征上验证，效应量较小（1.365 pp）；PR 的偏好损失是全目录 softmax、AR 仅用 1 正 4 负近似全目录交叉熵，两种解码的损失形式尚未统一；未来可学习更通用的可解释词表并探索其对推荐与部署的完整潜力。

Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) predicts the next item through its semantic ID (SID). Existing methods commonly fit SID vocabularies to pretrained language model (PLM) representations of item descriptions, incurring additional training costs and making vocabulary coverage dependent on the fitting domains. We observe that pretrained sparse autoencoders expose PLM features with human-interpretable semantic annotations, allowing feature indices to serve as a reusable SID vocabulary. However, reusing this vocabulary requires preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets and learning to favor target items over candidates with shared dominant features. It also requires extending feature interpretability from item content to retrieval decisions. To address these challenges, we propose API, a framework that Adapts the Pretrained Interpretable vocabulary for effective and explainable GR without additional vocabulary learning. Within API, Pretrained Interpretable IDs (PIDs) retain selected feature indices and relative activation strengths for item discrimination. With PIDs as supervision, the Semantic Prediction Adapter (SPA) learns user preferences from interaction histories through joint feature-index and strength prediction. SPA combines both predictions to score candidate items, with item-level supervision encouraging the observed next item to outrank its alternatives. API further explains candidate score differences through feature contributions paired with their pretrained semantic annotations. Extensive experiments show that API achieves competitive performance across backbones and decoding schemes, while preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets and enabling explainable retrieval.

</details>


### [383] [PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36958)
*Xiaohan Ye,Zihan Gong,Jingqian Zhao,Lianyu Du,Yunmeng Shu,Xu Chen,Zesheng Zhou,Renchun You,Bocheng Chen,Jinsong Lan,Haihong Tang,Bo Zheng*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: 本文提出PailitaoMMSearch2.0：一种部署于淘宝Pailitao的统一端到端多模态生成式检索系统。它基于原生视觉语言模型（VLM），直接从用户上传的查询图像加自由形式文本指令（如“找同色的长袖款”）生成商品的三层Semantic ID候选集，无需显式意图标签或意图路由专家模型。系统沿数据、意图、场景三个维度扩展：可组合的数据工具集支撑冷启动合成、真实流量精修与持续生产；CPT+混合意图混合预算SFT+统一RL（Sample–Beam rollout）训练单一策略；模型规模（0.8B/2B/4B）与推理预算（No/Low/High-think）暴露质量–成本可调工作点。线上A/B实验显示商品浏览量+17.90%、成交+27.04%、GMV+8.94%（均p<0.05），已全量上线。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 工业界现有生成式检索模型普遍与固定线上场景耦合，存在三类绑定：(1)监督绑定——训练数据被既有入口的交互日志主导，格式、曝光与意图分布受限，对尚未上线的新意图几乎无监督；(2)意图绑定——一个模型只拟合一种检索关系（视觉相似、编辑、搭配等），新增关系需引入意图分类器、路由规则或额外专家模型，系统复杂度与维护成本上升，且路由误差会传导到检索结果；(3)资源绑定——模型规模、解码策略与推理预算按单一SLO选定，难以在高吞吐候选生成、延迟容忍型复杂搜索及其间众多工作点间复用。开放式图文商品搜索（如“拍一件衬衫找运动短裤搭配”“找同品牌女款”“找可折叠儿童款”）同时暴露这三重限制：同一图文接口却表达不同检索关系，且查询复杂度差异大，部分需多步比对类目、风格、功能与约束。因此需要一种不要求用户或上游路由显式命名意图的统一系统。

Method: 问题形式化为“统一开放式多模态生成式检索”：请求x=(I,Q,C)（查询图像、自由文本指令、可选上下文），模型π_θ自回归生成商品SID集合Y=Decode_B(π_θ(·|x))，每层码本8192条的三层SID序列确定性映射到商品；隐含检索关系z与推理预算b需由模型从x中推断；部署配置c=(m,b,B)（模型规模、推理预算、束宽）在P95延迟与服务内存约束下最大化关系相关性。三维扩展：(1)数据扩展——五个可复用工具（Coarse-Filter、Fine-Filter、Query-Text-Gen、CoT-Gen、Quality-Control）按意图与生命周期编排为冷启动合成、真实流量精修、持续生产三条工作流，Quality-Control为强制终端闸门，用独立人工标定集校准rubric；(2)意图扩展——CPT（在电商商品标题理解、SID预测、属性预测、用户行为预测与通用语言任务混合语料上继续预训练）、多意图多预算SFT（相似/编辑/搭配三意图联合优化，No/Low/High-think三种受控CoT粒度）、统一RL（按β_t平衡采样各运营切片，GRPO使用Sample–Beam rollout：先从冻结旧策略采样N条推理前缀，再对每个前缀以宽度B做束搜索生成B条SID分支，共NB条轨迹按意图rubric打分并归一化，对推理与SID token同时施加裁剪代理目标；束选择不可微，故为束条件代理而非无偏on-policy估计）；(3)场景扩展——原生VLM（Qwen3.5）构建0.8B/2B/4B三档模型，No/Low/High-think提供细粒度工作点，应用按资源与延迟包线自行选择，无需引入路由模型。评测采用人类校准的多模态评估器（对Top-10按0–3分档），报告GR、ER、NDCG@10并对三意图宏平均；自动评估器对Good/Excellent的精度为92.4%–93.5%/93.6%–93.9%。

Result: 离线：2B Low-think为最佳整体工作点，宏NDCG 0.918、宏ER 55.1%，平均RT 278ms且仅用1块GPU；相较Qwen3.8-Flash-Next、GPT6-luna与内部召回排序流水线宏ER分别+2.9/+3.3/+5.6点，RT分别降低74.1%/92.4%/64.4%，GPU由4块降至1块；优势主要在搭配意图（NDCG 0.955、ER 74.3%，较两个改写式系统高13.2与7.0点，较内部流水线高30.1点），但相似与编辑意图仍弱于内部流水线与改写式系统。0.8B→2B宏ER+4.8点仅增91ms；2B→4B在Low-think下宏ER反降0.1点而RT增至617ms，4B在High-think下取得全表最佳宏ER 55.41%。数据扩展：数据量30%→100%宏ER 46.32%→49.03%（+2.71点，相似受益最大+5.08点，边际收益依意图而异）；去掉真实流量监督−0.78点，再去掉质量控制再−0.28点，合计−1.06点（质量控制主要利好匹配与编辑）。意图扩展：CPT使宏GR+0.8、宏ER+1.2点；跨意图混合中相似监督使编辑ER 33.11%→35.88%（正向迁移），加入匹配监督后匹配ER达66.09%、相似ER +0.93点，编辑轻微−0.45点，显示迁移非对称；标准统一RL使宏ER 49.03%→52.70%（+3.67点，匹配+7.84），替换为Sample–Beam后进一步+2.30点，最终较SFT高5.97点（相似+4.09、编辑+5.05、匹配+8.79）。场景扩展：0.8B下No-think最优（ER 50.78%、136ms），2B下Low-think最优（55.13%、278ms、8.6推理token），2B High-think匹配ER升至74.88%但RT近翻倍至544ms；4B High-think宏ER 55.41%、编辑41.27%、匹配75.57%，代价为54.99推理token与1133ms。线上：约10%流量、约14天A/B，商品浏览量+17.90%、独立用户浏览+13.62%、成交+27.04%、GMV+8.94%、CTR+0.58pp、转化率+0.37pp，均统计显著（p<0.05），相关场景已100%全量上线。

Conclusion: 论文的核心主张是：面向开放式的图文商品检索，可以通过"数据–意图–场景"三维解耦扩展，把原本按场景切分的多套模型/路由体系整合为一个共享策略加可配置工作点的系统，从而在提升检索质量的同时显著降低时延与GPU成本，并把线上业务指标转化为可度量的收益。其贡献有三：给出从场景专用生成式搜索向统一开放式多模态检索迁移的工业级实现蓝图与问题形式化；提出可组合数据工具集+多阶段训练配方+容量/推理预算工作点的三维框架；提出Sample–Beam RL rollout并通过离线、人评、线上实验验证。局限与后续工作：所谓"开放式"仅指查询接口而非全关系覆盖，评测仅限单一电商域的三类购物关系；多数消融基于2B，三个模型规模是独立检查点而非共享权重的弹性集合，交互未充分探究；离线评测依赖自动裁判，与数据过滤与奖励模型的评估器可能存在相关误差；线上A/B为系统级归因，无法拆分组件贡献。后续将扩展关系分类体系、联合优化检索质量与延迟/Token成本、研究跨预算共享参数的自适应或蒸馏模型、引入评估器集成与周期性人工审计，并考察目录与流量漂移下的稳定性。

Abstract: Generative retrieval models have been increasingly adopted in search and recommendation systems. However, industrial generative retrieval models are commonly specialized to a fixed online scenario: they learn from scenario-specific interactions, support a narrow set of query forms and retrieval objectives. We study how to remove these couplings and build a unified end-to-end multimodal search system for open-ended image--text queries, heterogeneous shopping intents, and online scenarios with different resource constraints. We present \textbf{PailitaoMMSearch}, which directly generates product Semantic IDs from a raw query image and free-form instruction and scales along three dimensions. \textbf{Data scaling} uses a reusable toolset that can be composed into intent- and lifecycle-specific workflows for cold-start synthesis, quality control, real-traffic refinement, and continuous data production. \textbf{Intent scaling} progressively equips one model with e-commerce product knowledge, multiple retrieval relations, and adjustable reasoning budgets through continual pre-training (CPT), mixed-budget supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and unified reinforcement learning (RL). The RL stage combines intent-balanced optimization and Sample--Beam rollouts aligned with multi-candidate serving. \textbf{Scenario scaling} exposes quality--cost operating points across model capacity and reasoning budget. The system is deployed in multimodal search applications on Taobao Pailitao. A controlled online A/B test reports statistically significant improvements, including item page views $\textbf{+17.90\%}$, transactions $\textbf{+27.04\%}$, and gross merchandise value $\textbf{+8.94\%}$.

</details>


### [384] [REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37584)
*Yuxi Huang,Silin Zhou,Chenhao Wang,Zihan Li,Gangming Guo,Pei Ke,Shen Gao,Shuo Shang*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: REGER 是一个面向生成式推荐（GR）的统一框架，核心思想是把“物品之间的关系”（语义相似、序列转移、偏好排序）显式注入到 GR 的三个环节：先用「生成式语义检索」预训练让 SID token 嵌入继承语义邻域关系，再用「物品转移结构注意力」（全局+对齐 SID 边界的局部注意力头）编码交互历史，最后用「层级协同偏好蒸馏」（HCPD）把判别式教师在 SID 前缀树各合法分支上的完整条件分布蒸馏给生成器，与交叉熵联合优化。作者证明了物品偏好分布沿 SID 前缀树的精确因子化以及物品级 KL 分解为加权前缀条件 KL 之和，从而为 HCPD 提供了理论依据。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 生成式推荐（GR）通过自回归生成离散语义 ID（Semantic ID, SID）来推荐物品，被认为能把物品语义/协同关系编码进 token 序列，但存在三点未被显式建模的瓶颈：(1) 语义相似性——SID token 嵌入随机初始化、模型从零训练，无法继承连续表示中的物品语义邻域关系；(2) 转移结构——历史被展平为 SID token 序列后用双向自注意力编码，注意力不尊重完整 SID 边界，也不显式刻画相邻物品间的有向转移（前一物品→当前物品）；(3) 用户偏好——next-token 交叉熵（CE）只监督正样本 SID 这一单一目标，未利用候选物品集合之间的相对偏好/竞争关系，物品间的排序关系缺乏显式约束。此外，已有工作多聚焦于改进 tokenization（把协同信息注入 SID 或与推荐目标对齐），而"如何把连续嵌入空间中的物品间关系迁移到离散 token 序列的建模与生成中"仍是 GR 的固有瓶颈。

Method: 整体为两阶段流水线（编码器-解码器基于 T5/Sentence-T5 + RQ-VAE tokenizer，固定长度 SID，额外加一位区分物品）。(1) GSR（Generative Semantic Retrieval）：以物品文本嵌入（Sentence-T5+PCA-whitening，768→128 维）的余弦相似度取 top-k 语义邻居构造 (源物品, 邻居) 预训练样本，编码器输入源物品 SID，解码器生成邻居 SID，按 teacher forcing 用 CE 训练；预训练同时更新 SID token 嵌入与主干参数，并按验证集推荐性能选 checkpoint，使稀疏交互物品也获得语义监督（默认 K=10，lr 3e-3，最多 100 epoch，patience 10）。(2) ITSA（Item Transition Structure Attention）：每层 encoder 混合 token-global 头（整段历史标准双向自注意）与 item-local 头（掩码限制只能看当前物品及其紧邻前驱物品的完整 SID，物品内部保持双向），仅改注意力掩码、不增参数，形成从前驱到当前的有向局部通道；两个阶段共用同一 ITSA 编码器，GSR 阶段局部窗口退化为单个 SID；头比例超参（2014: 2:4 / 5:1 / 3:3；2023: 5:1 / 5:1 / 4:2）。(3) HCPD（Hierarchical Collaborative Preference Distillation）：把 SID 组织为前缀树，叶子对应物品、前缀对应内部节点，定义前缀质量 m_P(a) 与条件分布 P(v|a)。定理 4.1 证明物品偏好可精确因子化为 P(i)=∏_ℓ P(s^ℓ|s^<ℓ)；定理 4.2（KL 链式法则）证明 D_KL(P||Q)=Σ_a m_P(a)·D_KL(P(·|a)||Q(·|a))，即物品级 KL 是各非终止前缀条件 KL 的加权和（附录 D.3 进一步说明：若目标按教师分布采样，HCPD 是该缩放 KL 的无偏估计）。教师采用冻结的 DuoRec（对比学习缓解表示退化），其物品分布 P_T(i)=softmax(r_u(i))，教师条件分布 q_T(v|a) 由前缀质量聚合得到；学生分布 q_θ(v|a) 在同一合法 next-token 集合 V(a) 上重归一化；损失为在目标 SID 真值前缀 a_ℓ 上对全部合法 token 的 KL 平均：L_HCPD=(1/(L+1))Σ_ℓ D_KL(q_T(·|a_ℓ)||q_θ(·|a_ℓ))，与 CE 联合优化 L_GR=L_CE+λ·L_HCPD（λ=0.8/0.8/1.0 等）。附录 D.4 从目标函数与梯度层面证明 HCPD 与 TCA-Aux（全体词表 KL）在固定重加权下不等价：HCPD 的梯度正比于 q_θ(v|a)-q_T(v|a)，对被低估的非目标分支给出直接纠偏信号，且不额外惩罚合法概率质量 Z<1；附录 E 显示仅在合法集合上归一化的 HCPD 在 N@5/R@5 上优于 HCPD-Full（全词表 KL 变体）。推理阶段无教师参与，采用无约束 beam search。

Result: 在 6 个真实数据集（Amazon Reviews 2014 的 Beauty/Sports/Toys 与 2023 的 Instruments/Scientific/Games，5-core、历史截断 20、3 个随机种子，R@{5,10} 与 N@{5,10}）上：REGER 一致优于全部生成式基线（TIGER、LETTER、EAGER、Unger、ETEGRec、DIGER、ActionPiece、TIGER-SST、DECOR、Latte、TopoTok）与混合检索基线（LIGER、MemGen-GR），并在多数设定下超过其教师 DuoRec。例如 Beauty R@5=0.0594/N@5=0.0395（对比 TIGER 0.0435/0.0291、ActionPiece 0.0507/0.0339、LIGER 0.0532/0.0348）；Toys R@5=0.0612 vs ETEGRec 0.0438；2023 数据集上取得最佳或次佳。将 HCPD 直接套在 TIGER 上也全面超过 TCA、TCA-Aux、APAO-pointwise、GFlowGR-DB/TB（同一 DuoRec 教师）。消融显示三组件均有贡献，去掉 HCPD 降幅最大（R@5 下降 10.9%–18.0%），GSR 次之，ITSA 亦稳定有效；分析实验表明 GSR 使物品对相似度与语义参考的 Spearman 相关性提高、ITSA 的局部头在注意力图上呈现清晰的次对角带（前驱→当前）。效率上 HCPD 训练显存 3094MB / 23s 每 epoch（TIGER 3072MB / 19s，GFlowGR 3664MB / 228s），推理速度不变（16s）。教师选择分析显示 DuoRec 优于 SASRec，较弱教师仍能提升 R@50 但会损害 top-5 指标。

Conclusion: 论文的主要结论是：GR 的性能瓶颈不在于 SID 结构本身，而在于生成器是否在语义学习、历史编码与生成三个环节显式利用了物品间关系。REGER 通过 GSR（预训练继承语义邻域）、ITSA（边界对齐的全局+局部注意力显式建模有向转移）与 HCPD（基于前缀树 KL 分解理论的协同偏好蒸馏）构成统一框架，在六个基准上稳定超越 GR/混合/判别式基线，且训练开销可接受、推理零额外成本；其核心启示是把物品知识"内化"到生成式推荐模型自身（而非仅依赖外部稠密检索或更好的 tokenization），并说明教师的价值不在于其 Top-K 精度而在于其刻画用户候选物品相对偏好的能力。局限方面，HCPD 仅在真值 SID 路径的前缀上计算条件 KL，其前缀权重与全树 KL 分解中的教师前缀质量一般不一致，附录 D.3 已给出相应说明；此外方法依赖 SID 前缀树结构与额外一轮预训练。

Abstract: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items. However, randomly initialized SID token embeddings and GR models trained from scratch do not directly inherit the semantic relations inherent in items, while inter-item collaborative relations are learned largely implicitly through token-level attention and next-token supervision. To address this limitation, we propose REGER, a unified framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation. We pretrain the GR model through generative semantic retrieval, enabling it to inherit inter-item semantic similarity by learning to generate semantic neighbors' SIDs. We combine global attention with local attention aligned with SID boundaries to capture historical context and directed transitions between adjacent items. We further develop a theoretical framework for hierarchical preference decomposition over the SID prefix tree, proving an exact factorization of collaborative preference distributions and a weighted decomposition of item-level KL divergence into prefix-conditional KL divergences. Building on this analysis, we distill a discriminative teacher's full conditional distributions over all legal next tokens at ground-truth prefixes along the target SID path, jointly optimizing this objective with cross-entropy. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over existing GR baselines and support the effectiveness of the proposed preference distillation.

</details>


### [385] [QESChunker: A Single Objective Unifies Overlapping and Non-Overlapping Chunking for RAG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36557)
*Yifan Zhao,Qianyang Zhao,Xinyu Guan,kai wei,Yuming Deng*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: Chunking is a fundamental preprocessing step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), yet most existing chunkers rely primarily on heuristics. We introduce the Question--Evidence-Supervised Chunker (QESChunker), to our knowledge the first method for constructing static chunk indices from question--evidence supervision. QESChunker constructs document-specific chunk indices by optimizing over human-annotated or LLM-generated question--evidence pairs, without access to held-out test queries. We formulate non-overlapping and overlapping index construction through a unified question--evidence utility-maximization objective, turning chunking into a supervised combinatorial optimization problem. Under the non-overlap constraint, the objective decomposes over chunks and can be optimized exactly in polynomial time by dynamic programming. When overlap is allowed, the objective becomes monotone submodular; exact optimization is NP-hard, but our greedy achieves a $(1-1/\sqrt{e})$-approximation. Across two self-constructed and three public datasets, both variants outperform existing chunking methods in complete-evidence recall in nearly all evaluated settings, under the same overlap regime and a fixed hybrid retriever. These results recast chunking as supervised, budget-aware index construction for evidence retrieval.

### [386] [Coverage Under Contradiction: A Benchmark for Negation-Aware Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37162)
*Pasha Abrishamchian,Eugene Yang,Andrew Yates,Nazli Goharian,Ophir Frieder*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: Coverage-evaluation benchmarks quantify whether retrieved evidence covers the different pieces of information needed to satisfy an information need. Existing benchmarks mostly consider factual claims that may already be known to pretrained retrieval components, leaving open whether retrievers find corpus evidence when it contradicts those priors. We study how retrievers behave when their parametric knowledge and the information in a corpus disagree. To do so, we develop a process to augment a nugget-based coverage benchmark with controlled contradictions. For each nugget, we create a negated counterpart and edit its supporting documents to support that negation while preserving the context. Applying this process to CoverageBench, a benchmark measuring information coverage, we create CoverageBench-Negate, spanning six datasets and roughly 63,000 original-edited evidence pairs (one per nugget-document link). We attach rich construction metadata to every pair and additionally provide out-of-family LLM judgments over all pairs and a human audit of a sample. In baseline experiments, BM25 separates original from edited near-twin evidence substantially better than dense retrievers (Qwen3 and Jina), which stay near chance. We release the benchmark on Hugging Face Datasets (nuggets, documents, pairs) together with the construction materials, including the prompts used to create it.

### [387] [Modeling Preference Dependencies with Directed Acyclic Graphs for Narrative-Driven Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37280)
*Mingzhe Lu,Jian Qin,Ruize Qin,Jinhao Liu,Yunpeng Li,Hang Su*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: Narrative-driven recommendation allows users to express multifaceted needs through free-form text where stated preferences naturally qualify and condition one another. Existing methods typically treat narratives as flat keyword combinations or unconstrained generative queries, failing to capture how complex preferences hierarchically refine and contextualize each other. We propose the Preference Dependency Graph Framework (PDG-F), a narrative-driven recommendation framework centered on explicit preference dependencies. Specifically, PDG-A (PDG-Agent) first parses unstructured requests to organize user preferences and their mutual qualifications into a directed acyclic Preference Dependency Graph (PDG). Through this graph, candidate evidence from the open Web is acquired via directed path retrieval, and final recommendations are determined by topological path ranking. Comprehensive experiments across three diverse domains spanning English and Chinese contexts confirm that PDG-F consistently achieves superior recommendation performance over competitive baselines, open-domain retrieval agents, and frontier language models. Further diagnostic analyses show that our dependency-guided retrieval markedly raises the attainable candidate-pool ceiling, demonstrating the fundamental value of modeling preference dependencies in narrative-driven recommendation.

### [388] [Is the education gap in generative AI use smaller than the internet's was at a similar level of use? Evidence from 16 European countries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36181)
*Keisuke Watanabe*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: New technologies are usually adopted first by people with more formal education. This paper asks whether the education gap in generative AI use in 2025 is smaller or larger than the internet's gap in the same country in the year when overall internet use was at a similar level. It uses public Eurostat survey data on ICT usage by individuals aged 16 to 74. Each country's 2025 rate of generative AI use in the last three months is matched to the internet year whose overall last-three-months use was closest, within 5 percentage points, and the gap between people with high (ISCED 5 to 8) and low (ISCED 0 to 2) completed education is measured as a log ratio and as a percentage-point difference. Sixteen of 35 countries could be matched; most of the others were early internet adopters. In the matched countries, the generative AI gap was smaller in 13 of 16 countries on the log ratio (median change -0.625, 95% bootstrap interval -0.969 to -0.291, two-sided sign test p = 0.021) and in 15 of 16 on the percentage-point gap (median change -27.6 points, interval -32.2 to -16.8, p = 0.0005). The point-gap result keeps its sign in every generative-AI-versus-internet sensitivity analysis with 8 or more countries, including comparisons restricted on both sides to ages 25 to 54 and 55 to 74, but its size is sensitive to matching that takes education composition into account (about -10 to -11 points in 7 and 8 countries). The ratio result is fragile: it fails the decision rule when countries matched at their first internet observation are removed (9 of 11, p = 0.065). The analysis follows an unpublished plan whose timing cannot be verified, so it is not presented as pre-registered. The results describe unadjusted education contrasts in a non-random set of countries, not an education effect, and do not generalise to the EU as a whole.

### [389] [RELAY: One Query, Two Roles for Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36000)
*Zesheng Li,Chengchang Pan,Honggang Qi*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: Sequential recommendation must combine semantic preferences with behavioral associations to deliver accurate rankings at low inference cost. Sharing history selection connects preference representation directly to the behavioral evidence used in candidate scoring. We present RELAY, a compact sequential recommender built around one query, two roles: semantic readout and behavioral-memory routing. A single learned query forms a semantic preference representation and reuses its attention to route direct-history and transition evidence into candidate scores. Candidate-conditioned gates calibrate the two memory channels for each candidate. RELAY trains both roles with a single catalog likelihood and produces the final ranking in one forward pass. Full-catalog experiments on six datasets show that RELAY achieves the highest Recall@5 and NDCG@5 among the compared methods on every dataset, improving over the previous best model by 14.22% and 17.88% on average. With 2.044 million predictor parameters, RELAY reduces predictor size by 65.12% and achieves a 1.75~1.79$\times$ inference speedup over the previous best model.

### [390] [Preserving rare-item recall under a storage budget: quantization, distillation, and the limits of teacher fidelity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36267)
*Han Chen,Yingrui Li*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: Under a fixed embedding-storage budget, recommenders can use a small full-precision model, a distilled student, or a higher-rank low-precision model. We asked which choice preserves rare-item recall and whether teacher fidelity reflects it in seven dataset-backbone cells: matrix factorization on Gowalla, this http URL , Amazon Video Games, Steam, Goodbooks-10k and MovieLens-20M, and LightGCN on Amazon Video Games. Seven candidates fit in 168 bytes per user or item row: 40-dimensional Bayesian personalized ranking (BPR), two 40-dimensional unbiased knowledge distillation (UnKD) students, and factorizations of a 300-dimensional teacher's scores at ranks 40, 80, 155 and 300, stored in 32, 16, 8 and 4 bits. Each test set was evaluated once after fixing candidates and confirmatory analyses. The rank-300 4-bit factorization used 13% of teacher storage and retained 95-103% of its tail recall@20 and 93-97% of its NDCG@20 in every cell. The rank-40 factorization had the lowest tail recall in every cell; the 4-bit factorization had 1.2-12.7 times its tail recall and 0.99-1.46 times its NDCG. UnKD students retained 56-102% of teacher tail recall. In all ten prespecified comparisons across five prospective-expansion cells, the 4-bit factorization had higher tail recall, with simultaneous 95% intervals excluding zero. Teacher-hit retention, the share of the teacher's relevant tail hits also found by a model, ordered 23 of 147 candidate pairs differently from tail recall and identified the wrong tail-recall leader in 3 of 7 cells: models can find relevant tail items the teacher misses. In these cells, spending bytes on rank rather than precision preserved rare-item recall at 7.5 times the arithmetic per score. Compressed recommenders should be judged by total tail recall, not teacher fidelity alone.

### [391] [Cross-Day Compatibility of Daily Item Embeddings: An Empirical Study of Alignment, Scale Management, and CTR Adaptation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36408)
*Yicheng Wang*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: Daily item co-occurrence embeddings are paired with next-day behavior without future-behavior leakage. Multi-day click-through rate (CTR) training therefore mixes versions whose directions and norms may differ for the same item. We compare Word2Vec and an item-graph XSimGCL adaptation across initialization, inheritance, post-processing, training constraints, and downstream augmentation. The inventory contains 48 configurations, including 32 common-protocol CTR evaluations. Observed metrics are reported as relative percentage changes from the corresponding Word2Vec baseline (0%), with raw values and exact dataset sizes withheld. Three findings emerge. First, multiple upstream interventions improve compatibility and CTR. ID-init and orthogonal alignment increase cosine by 51.2% and 93.4%, and GAUC by 2.2% and 2.6%, relative to ordinary Word2Vec. Retrieval and geometry remain insufficient downstream surrogates. Second, warm starts perform strongly but accumulate scale. The day-matched norm increase over Word2Vec reaches 102.5% after eight days; daily global rescaling limits it to 8.2% and attains the highest observed GAUC increase, 4.0%. Third, CTR learning through a dimensionality-reducing encoder further adapts to residual drift. Against dimension-matched random-projection, SVD, and untrained-network controls, trained encoders attain the highest cross-day cosine for four of six upstream methods. The other two rank third and second in train-to-test cosine. These industrial results support complementary roles for upstream stabilization, inherited-scale management, and downstream task learning.
